top plate and installing mono trusses for the roof.  The employee fell and

transported to the hospital and admitted for treatment of fractures to both
wrists.

At 6:55 a.m. on June 7, 2019, Employees #1, #2, and #3, employed by a utility
services company, drove in two utility pickup trucks to their starting work
location, a two-lane rural road with no shoulder.  They parked their trucks in

blocked.  They then began to unload tools and equipment they would use to
inspect and treat wooden power poles located on the opposite side of the road.
Each truck was equipped with a single rotating orange light and vertical flagger
flags on the back.  As the three employees unloaded tools from the rearmost

driver-side rear corner of the utility truck.  Employee #1 was thrown across the

At approximately 10:00 a.m. on December 14, 2018, an employee was working as a
laborer for a landscaping service. He was working at a private residence.
Workers were trimming trees in the backyard of the residence. To climb the
trees, they were using climbing gear consisting of a harness, rope, and tie-off
lines. The employee started his ascent into a tree by securing a rope to a
branch and then climbing up. He made it up to the tree branch and used his arms
to pull himself up onto it, when the branch broke at the crotch. The employee
fell approximately 10 feet (3.0 meters), hitting a chain-link fence before
hitting the ground. The employee was treated at a hospital for a fracture of his
L1 vertebra. He was hospitalized. The employer notified DOSH at 1:05 p.m. that
same day, meeting the reporting requirements. DOSH arrived at the site to open
an inspection on March 18, 2019. The employee used a tie-in point that was not
on or around the main leader or a major upright branch of the tree. Had he used
a more appropriate tie-in point, he most likely would have prevented the
accident. The employer was to be issued a SAR for T8 3427(a)(4).
At 7:55 a.m. on January 3, 2019, an employee was working as a laborer for a
landscaping service. He was at a worksite that was a fixed facility consisting
of a commercial indoor and outdoor area. He was an employee of the employer, and
the incident occurred at the place of employment. He was operating a chain saw
to cut tree branches. As he was cutting, one of the branches moved quickly, and
the employee's left hand came into contact with the moving chain. The index
finger on his left hand was partially amputated. The employee went to a
community hospital, and the finger was reattached there. He was not
hospitalized. A representative of the employer reported the injury to the San
Bernardino district office at 3:10 p.m. that same day. The employer reported the
incident to the Division, pursuant to Title 8 CCR Section 342(a), in a timely
manner. A CSHO from the San Bernardino district office arrived at the site and
opened the investigation at 2:45 p.m. on January 28, 2019. One of the factors
that caused the incident was that the employer failed to ensure that the
employee was trained and instructed in the areas that include the hazards
involved in the job assignment of tree trimming and proper safe use of all
equipment, including, but not limited to, safety equipment and personal
protective equipment. The incident would have been prevented had the employee
been properly trained. No Serious Accident Related violation of Title 8 CCR was
determined. Other violations were found, however, and the employer was cited.

administrator for a janitorial service. He was operating a trash compactor. A

employee's right thumb from a pinhole size leak. The wound became infected. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 7:30 a.m. on May 8, 2019, an employee was working as a machinist for a firm
that manufactured industrial molds. He was operating a vertical lathe. The lathe
was a 60 inch (1.5 meter) Webster-Bennett vertical lathe boring mill, with
serial number 5890-1. It ran approximately eight hours every day, and four to
six days a week, depending on product demand. The lathe had a table that spun in
operation. The table could operate at 3.8 to 83 revolutions per minute (rpm). On
the day of the incident, the table was set to rotate at 25 rpm. The employee was
setting up the jacks on the table to get a part ready to run. The center of
table was full of metal chips. The employee cleaned the center of the table. The
employee came out of the turntable area and turned the table on. There were
still chips on the jack, causing the part not to sit flat on the table. The
employee turned the table off again. He grabbed an air hose to blow the chips
off the jack. The air hose hit the lever that turned the machine on. The table
began to spin as the employee was reaching across the table to blow away the
chips. The air hose and the employee's sleeve were caught by the table, and the
employee was pulled into the machine. He suffered six broken ribs. He was
hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 6, 2019, an employee was working as a machinist for a
temporary employment agency. He had been sent to a shipyard, where ships were
repaired. He was riding a JLG boom lift up to inspect the stern of a ship. When
employee was about 30 feet (9.1 meters) up, he stopped the lift. When the lift
stopped, the bucket moved. The employee was thrown off balance. To keep from
falling, he reached out and grabbed the lip of the bucket. As he did this, the
bucket made contact with the ship. His fingers were caught and crushed between
the lift bucket and the hull of ship. The employee was sent to hospital and
released. One of his fingers was surgically amputated. Two others were crushed,
but amputation was not required. The employee was not kept at the hospital
overnight. Elsewhere on the report form, it was stated that the employee was
hospitalized.

pulled into the machine. Employee #1's thumb was pinched by the rebar and
bending rod, and the thumb tip was amputated. The employee was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 3:00 p.m. on March 18, 2019, an employee and coworker carried a twenty-one

shoulder, bounced off the ground and struck the employee on the back of the

At 9:48 a.m. on February 5, 2019, Employee #1 was retrieving a box. While

was hospitalized for treatment.

At 6:30 a.m. on March 22, 2023, an employee was riding on a bus.  The driver ran
a stop sign, and the bus was struck by an oncoming truck.  The employee was

At 12:30 p.m. on March 4, 2023, an employee was making a delivery.  The employee

At 11:21 a.m. on November 29, 2023, an employee was driving a truck. The

piercing injuries.

aircraft, is the deflating of the tire before a tool ever touches the tire. This

the two pieces of the wheel together.  Once just enough of the bolts were

was standing just to the right of the employee during the wheel blow-out, was

gash from the bridge of nose up to the forehead. The right eye and the area
around the eye suffered severe bruising.

At 9:30 a.m. on June 28, 2022, two employees were leveling sewer pipe in a
trench. The two employees were in a trench that had a depth of approximately 23
feet deep and 34 inches wide, with no protection system. The trench had straight
vertical walls. The closest mean of egress for the two employees was
approximately 132 feet from where they were working. The foreman began cutting
across the trench to dig a smaller trench (side cut) for joining pipe to be
laid. The trench collapsed, and the two employees that were in the trench were
killed. There were 3X trench boxes (8 foot x 24 foot) on site, but they were not
used. The foreman chose to work with vertical walls for the trench due to his
soil type determination of soil type being stable; additionally, he requested
ladders the day before the collapse, as they did not have tall enough ladders to
install the trench boxes. The soil type results from the Salt Lake City Lab were
type B for all 3X soil samples gathered at the site and sent in for analysis.
The afternoon before the trench collapse it did rain, and photos taken by the
CSHO and police department revealed water in the bottom of the trench.
At 10:38 a.m. on February 13, 2023, an employee who worked as an assembler for
an analytical equipment manufacturer was walking towards his workstation when he
tripped and fell over an air hose running across the aisle. The hose was
stretched across the floor between the Global brand hose reel and an Advance
Product Tools brand air lift table. The employee made impact with the concrete

the employee was seen by the surgeon who put an air cast on his right arm. On

death as accidental and the cause as "Hypertensive and Atherosclerotic

in a Ground Level Fall". The coroner concluded that impact with floor led to
injuries and treatments that eventually lead to the employee's death.

One employee was conscious for 1-2 minutes following the event, then collapsed.

At 10:55 a.m. on December 12, 2022, an employe who worked as a Dump Truck Driver

At 10:00 a.m. on July 11, 2022, an employee was delivering an appliance to a

The passenger vehicle struck the back of the stopped delivery straight truck,
striking the employee and pinning him between the two vehicles. The employee was

debris generated from the impact of the two vehicles. The delivery truck

incident.
An employee was working as a nurse in a skilled nursing facility when she was

contracted COVID-19 and subsequently died from her infection on December 10,
At 3:30 p.m. on December 9, 2022, an employee was attempting to reset an alarm

At 7:00 a.m. on December 21, 2022, an employee was working from an A-frame

At 10:00 a.m. on December 16, 2022, an employee was clearing a site for a new

At 3:00 p.m. on December 12, 2022, an employee was unloading a delivery when he

At 10:00 a.m. on December 20, 2022, an employee was helping prepare the swing

At 6:50 a.m. on October 7, 2022, an employee was dismantling a commercial rack

At 10:00 a.m. on December 6, 2022, an employee was working at an adult day care

found the employee on the ground and called for emergency services. The employee

At 11:09 a.m. on December 19, 2022, an employee was installing a heating unit

At 1:00 a.m. on December 22, 2022, an employee was using compressed air to clean

At 7:00 a.m. on December 18, 2022, an employee was installing a fiber optic line

At 3:30 p.m. on November 22, 2022, an employee was attempting to connect his

At 7:15 p.m. on December 21, 2022, an employee was assisting in troubleshooting

At 11:30 a.m. on December 21, 2022, an employee was troubleshooting a

At 9:00 a.m. on December 16, 2022, an employee was preparing to plug an

At 3:20 a.m. on December 27, 2022, an employee was removing excess beans from a

ensure that the driveway was clear so he could move the truck forward and then

bucket truck sheared in two pieces.  The employee suffered internal injuries and

The accident occurred in a restaurant that is part of a hotel.  During the

The accident occurred during a municipal public works project. The employer is a

At 12:00 a.m. on June 29, 2023, an employee fell while walking in the service

At 12:05 p.m. on September 25, 2023, an employee was cutting lettuce at the

At 8:30 a.m. on October 2, 2023, an employee backed up to connect the trailer.

At 11:36 a.m. on October 2, 2023, an employee was using a weed-eater to finish

shock to his right hand that traveled through his body and exited out of his

At 7:00 p.m. on August 16, 2023, an employee was on a ladder planning for a

At 4:45 p.m. on August 15, 2023, an employee was working in a department store

At 7:00 p.m. on May 12, 2023, an employee working as a day laborer was

At 12:00 noon on August 15, 2023, an employee stepped off the back of a moving

shoulder, in the process of delivering a mini excavator.  The mini excavator
would be used for future debris clean-up work along the shoulder. Employee #1
removed the tie-down straps/chains that held the excavator to the trailer. As
Employee #1 returned to the delivery vehicle/truck he was struck by a
tractor-trailer that swerved off the road, leading to his fatality.
At 12:00 a.m. on September 5, 2023, an employee, a crew member for Flagger
Force, was at a traffic control jobsite located at the intersection of Carver
School Road and Butterfield Drive in Winston Salem, NC. The employee was
attempting to cross Carver School Road to a position for traffic control for
flagger duties. The employee was struck by an oncoming vehicle when he stepped
into the active traffic lane. Traffic control had not been fully implemented to
control all lanes of traffic. The employee was taken to Atrium Wake Forest
Baptist Hospital on the date of the incident and was taken off life support on
September 22, 2023, when he died.
At 1:00 p.m. on November 6, 2023, an employee was working by himself towards the
end of his shift. The employee rolled an argon cylinder and brought an empty
acetylene cylinder inside the garage bay. Without witnesses or surveillance
footage, it cannot be determined what the employee's task was. While the
employee was in the garage bay, a gas explosion occurred with the acetylene
cylinder. This resulted in a loss of limbs, ruptured aorta, shrapnel lodged in
the head, and extreme blood loss. The employee was transferred to a hospital in
Louisville, where he died from his injuries during surgery.
At 3:00 p.m. on November 3, 2023, Employee #1 was collecting and disposing of
tree limbs at the base of a tree. A coworker climbed approximately 30 feet up a
tree to cut branches.  When the coworker cut a large tree branch, it fell to the
ground striking Employee #1 in the head, rendering him unconscious. Employee #1
was killed.
Based on a video, at 6:15 p.m. on October 27, 2023, an employee was walking,
wobbled, and then fell down.  He moved for 15 minutes and then stopped moving.
The employee worked alone. The employee died of a heart attack.
At 5:15 p.m. on November 7, 2023, an employee was in a bucket, while it was
being driven out of a residential driveway. He was pushing a communications line
out of the way so the truck he was on could pass underneath of it. The employee
pushed the communications line out of the way, when he was shocked by the power
line that ran above the communications line.  The employee was killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on November 11, 2023, Employee #1 was employed by power line
contractor.  Employee #1 and a coworker were utilizing a Ditch Witch compact
loader to place an empty, wooden cable spool into a dump truck after performing
surface restoration of an area that had fiber cable previously installed. The
compact loader would not lift the spool high enough for it to be dumped into the
dump bed and the front of the machine began to rise due to the weight of the
wooden spool.  Employee #1 exited the control deck of the compact loader and
moved to its left side and the coworker moved to the right side of the machine.
Both employees began to push the wooden spool from the compact loader's bucket
into the dump bed.  When the wooden spool left the bucket, the machine and
bucket lowered, striking Employee #1 in the head.  Employee # 1 was taken to a
medical facility for medical treatment of a head laceration.  While at the
hospital, Employee # 1 had a personal medical event (heart attack) and died.
At 2:36 p.m. on October 26, 2023, an employee was changing a hydraulic coupling
adapter for the auger attachment (Bobcat, Auger, 30C Auger, Serial Number
944534633) onto the skid steer tractor (Bobcat T590, Compact Skid Steer, Track
Loader Model, ID no. ALJU24957). The farm manager found the employee lying on
the ground in front of the skid steer tractor.  According to the farm manager,
the employee was breathing shallowly and was coherent.  There are no cameras on
the premises, and no one witnessed the event.  The farm manager called 911
immediately upon realizing that his employee had fallen to the ground.
Paramedics arrived and took the employee to the hospital, where he died that
same day.  Doctors initially claimed that he died of cardiac arrest.  Following
Detective Rodriguez' review, he ordered an autopsy that disclosed that the
employee had striations in his liver, marks on his chest, and a broken rib.  The
cause of death has not been disclosed by the Medical Examiner to date. It was
postulated that the employee removed hydraulic pressure to the auger attachment,
and it lowered on top of him.  The employee might have been able to escape on
his own and may not have mentioned the incident to the farm manager.  The
injuries sustained eventually led to his death.  The exact object that harmed
the employee cannot be known for sure.
At 10:00 a.m. on November 9, 2023, an employee was in the process of saw-cutting
the asphalt driveway to add irrigation lines. The employee was in the process of
making a cut across the driveway with a STIHL TS 500i quick cut saw to remove
asphalt in order to install irrigation lines under the driveway. A coworker was
helping the employee with dust suppression. The employee had made it
approximately ? of the way across the driveway, when he turned off and set down
the saw to take his safety glasses off to wipe off the fog that had accumulated
on them. At that point, the employee collapsed to the ground and lost
consciousness. The foreman/supervisor was located on the other side of the
private residence and was summoned to the driveway by the coworker.  9-1-1 was
initiated. The employee died due to cardiac dysrhythmia.
At 3:00 p.m. on September 28, 2023, an employee was driving a motor vehicle,
when he lost control of the vehicle.  The vehicle was in a traffic accident, and
the employee was killed.
At 10:00 a.m. on November 10, 2023, an employee was walking to the felled trees
with an idling chain saw. The employee tripped and fell onto the chain saw
blade, lacerating his neck. The employee was killed.
At 5:30 a.m. on November 9, 2023, an employee was driving a snowmobile back to
employees suffered third degree burns and subsequently died from their injuries.
At 10:00 a.m. on April 30, 2023, an employee working as a construction laborer
on a residential project started work spraying foam insulation. The employee
(the helper) and a coworker (the sprayer) had been working starting in the attic
since the previous day and were working their way down. By the evening on April
30, 2023, the coworker was down on the ground floor and the employee was on the
second floor scraping excess foam from between the studs, sweeping and cleaning
up. According to the employer (co-owner) and sister-in-law of the employee, he
spoke on the phone with his spouse for less than a minute around 6:05 to 6:06
p.m. outside of the structure. The coworker then noticed the foam was getting
low and called out for the employee to change the barrel in the truck. After not
hearing a response, the coworker turned around and found the employee
unconscious near the front door and staircase. The coworker attempted to rouse
the employee and when he could not, he called 911 and began chest compressions.
The coworker called 911 at 6:10 p.m. and one minute later an ambulance arrived
on scene and found the worker unconscious and pulseless. The employee had died
of a heart attack caused by atherosclerotic and hypertensive cardiovascular
blades where facing up toward the sky. The employee suffered severe injuries to
the head and neck and was killed.
At 1:45 p.m. on September 18, 2023, an employee was operating a lawn mower off a
public road. A vehicle ran over the curb and hit the lawn mower, pinning the
employee and lawn mower against a tree. The employee was killed.
At 11:50 a.m. on September 19, 2023, an employee was operating a riding lawn
mower, mowing grass down a hill at a school field. The employee went off the
edge of an approximately 4-foot embankment and was pinned under the riding lawn
mower. The employee sustained fatal injuries to the head.
At 1:30 p.m. on August 31, 2022, an employee overturned a mower while mowing on
an incline at Terrace Gardens at Estouteville Farm. The employee was killed when
the mower overturned.
At 7:50 a.m. on June 30, 2023, an employee was employed by WSDOT as the bridge
attendant on the SR99 bridge by himself and went off the bridge overnight. When
his relief arrived the next morning, he was nowhere to be found and a search was
initiated.  The employee was found in the Duwamish Waterway approximately 0.5
miles downstream.
At 1:09 p.m. on August 17, 2023, an employee working as a truck driver
(owner/operator) was delivering wire rack materials to a drywall and insulation
contractor. A coworker (forklift operator) who worked for the contractor was
unloading the wire racking using a forklift with 48-inch forks. There was one
stack of material left to be unloaded, which was located in the center of the
trailer and was stacked three high. The trailer is 102 inches wide. The employee
climbed on top of the trailer to assist with the offloading of material. The
forklift was positioned as close to the trailer as possible, and the employee
was positioned on the opposite side of the stack. The coworker began to lift the
stacks of material as the employee tried to hold the stacks stable. The stacks
toppled over toward the employee pushing him off the trailer and causing him to
fall to the asphalt parking lot below. The coworker found the employee was
unresponsive and bleeding from a contusion on his head and from the nose.
Weather was not a factor. The forklift tines were too short to reach completely
under the material to maintain a safe lift of material. Also, the employee's
position was not appropriate for the task. The coworker called EMS who
transported the employee to St. Vincent's Hospital, where he later died of a
head injury.
On September 13, 2023, an employee who was engaged in sugar cane planting
operations in an open field began to feel ill and collapsed and was transported
to a hospital.  On September 16, 2024, the employee died of injuries related to
heat-stroke.
At 12:44 p.m. on August 29, 2023, an employee was climbing a tree in preparation
for cutting a tree limb when he fell to the ground and was killed.
At 6:00 p.m. on September 7, 2023, an employee was delivering packages. The
employee was exposed to the hazard of high heat from direct sun and radiant heat
during the performance of his job duties, including loading his vehicle with
packages, sorting packages, retrieving items, lifting packages up to 50 pounds
or more, collecting signatures if needed, upkeeping of the vehicle, and driving
to multiple locations.  The packages were varied in size, weight, and quantity,
which contributed to the physical demand put on the driver to lift and deliver
packages in a productive manner.  The National Weather Service issued a heat
advisory that included the worksite in Austin, TX, on the day of the incident.
9 Line Transport Inc. is a third party contractor that assists in conducting
deliveries for Amazon's distribution warehouse.  Employees routinely work
outdoors in excessive heat conditions. The hazard associated is working in
excessive heat conditions when performing multiple deliveries, while not having
access to a cool down area.  The employees deliver packages varying in size,
weight, and quantity to various locations, while being exposed to the heat
inside the vehicle and heat produced when stuck in traffic.  The employees do
not have air conditioning in all the vehicles, and while making deliveries spend
several minutes looking through their cargo to find the packages that need to be
delivered.  Working in a metal shell truck increases the outside temperature
about 10 degrees per every 5 minutes sitting in the sun.  Employees have limited
means to regulate their body's temperature due to the physical demand of
delivering multiple packages at a rapid pace; then, getting into a hot vehicle,
subdural hematoma, subarachnoid hemorrhage, burst T4 vertebrae, broken right
clavicle, fractured ribs, pulmonary contusions and brainstem bleeding. The
employee was killed.
At 10:45 a.m. on December 4, 2023, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were working as
Visual Security Officers at their assigned posts. An individual entered the
store, and the security camera operator followed the individual with the
security cameras.  The individual put two hats into his clothing and attempted
to walk out of the store. Over portable radios, the loss control team put a call
out to apprehend the induvial leaving the store from the Market Street entrance.
Employee #1 and Employee #2, who were working as Visual Security Officers to the
vestibule by Market Street, went to assist in the apprehension of the
individual.  The individual became hostile towards Employee #1.  Soon after, a
coworker, who works as a Detective for Macy's, arrived to apprehend the
individual.  The individual resisted the coworker, and both Employee #1 and
Employee #2 did not assist in the physical apprehension of the individual.  The
individual dropped the merchandise and since the coworker was unable to cuff the
individual, they let him walk out of the store.  The Visual Security Officers
returned to their assigned posts in the store.  Soon after, the individual
re-entered the store, saw Employee #1 and attacked him with a knife, stabbing
him multiple times.  Employee #2 witnessed the attack and attempted to remove
the individual off Employee #1. Employee #1 died from his injuries.  Employee #2
received numerous stab wounds, resulting in his hospitalization.
At 12:00 p.m. on November 26, 2023, an employee was retrieving a box containing
30 individually wrapped noodles.  The employee fell to the concrete floor.  The
employee fractured his skull and was killed.
At 6:45 a.m. on November 30, 2023, an employee had begun his workday according
to his normal schedule, which was to drive his personal vehicle to the wash
station (West Yard), where he picked up his assigned truck and trailer (#526)
before picking up his first load of weanling pigs at the assigned barn.  On the
day of the incident, he deviated from the route to stop at his personal
residence. The employee was struck by a vehicle and found dead beneath the back
tires (dual wheels) on the driver's side due to blunt force trauma. There were
no eyewitnesses. The police report did not find the truck and trailer to be in
violation of any traffic rules. The police report noted that the truck was found
running and had not been placed in park or had the parking brake engaged.
At 1:15 p.m. on December 1, 2023, Employee #1 was working for a siding
contractor.  Employee #1 was installing ornamental downspout sheet metal.
Employee #1 was using a 32-foot fiberglass extension ladder to access his work
approximately 16 feet above the ground.  Employee #1 fell to the concrete

At 3:00 p.m. on December 1, 2023, an employee was speaking with a coworker while
operating a powered industrial truck. The employee drove approximately 6-8 feet
away, when the employee lost consciousness and crashed the powered industrial
truck into a pole. The employee died of natural causes.
At 6:30 p.m. on November 29, 2023, an employee was walking to his work post
after returning from a lunch break. The employee suffered from hypertensive and
atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, resulting in acute congestive heart
failure and death.  There was no object or substance that directly harmed the
employee, i.e., the manner of death was natural causes.

On October 5, 2023, the employee was pronounced brain dead and on October 8,

At 12:00 a.m. on July 10, 2024, an employee was unloading a Cottrell EZ5307
model trailer and fell and was killed. The North Carolina Department of Labor
(NCDOL) conducted numerous interviews, medical records reviews, and direct
observations of the unloading process but was unable to determine the exact
height from which the employee fell, where the fall occurred, or how the
employee landed. Due to the lack of evidence regarding the fall, NCDOL was
unable to document a citation for a fall from height. Additionally, the preamble
to Subpart D of the Walking and Working Surfaces Standard discusses exemptions
for rolling stock, and Subpart D does not clarify whether rolling stock is
covered under the standard. Due to the lack of industry-specific requirements
for fixed fall protection systems for car haulers, the CSHO was unable to
establish employer knowledge of a violative condition. No violations of North
Carolina occupational safety and health standards were observed, and no
citations were recommended. A letter of recommendation will be forwarded to the
employer, advising the implementation of portable ladder access when unloading
the trailer.
At 3:15 p.m. on July 24, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a property management
company, had completed work for the day and was resting with coworkers under
shade in the front yard of a residential home. The crew had finished building a
block retaining wall, and the supervisor was not present at the time of the

At 6:30 a.m. on August 4, 2021, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was installing siding from a scissor lift. The scissor lift was missing the
entry/exit door, which served as a guardrail. While working, the employee fell
approximately 18 feet to a lower level. The employee sustained a traumatic brain
injury and remained unresponsive following the incident. Emergency services
transported the employee to the hospital, where he was admitted. Unfortunately,
the employee later died.
At 10:30 a.m. on July 13, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a company performing
concrete and brick work, was on a lunch break and walking toward the building.
As the employee was approaching the building, he tripped over a 2-inch pipe
railing, falling forward. The employee sustained a head laceration and injuries
to the vertebrae in the neck. Emergency services were called, and the employee
was transported to a local hospital.  He was pronounced dead at the hospital.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 5, 2024, an employee working for a flooring contractor was
working with a coworker, his supervisor, replacing a ceiling tile. The only
witness to the event was the coworker. The team set up a non-self-supporting
ladder to access the T-bar ceiling. The employee climbed the ladder while the
coworker held the ladder. After the employee replaced the ceiling tile, he began
to descend the ladder holding the replaced ceiling tile. According to the
coworker, the employee was approximately 6 feet off the ground when he attempted
to hand down the ceiling tile to the coworker. While the coworker was reaching
to grab the tile, the ladder shuddered, and the employee jumped off the ladder.
The coworker attempted to catch the employee who fell knocking the coworker to
the ground. The employee struck his head on the tile floor. The employee was
transported to a medical center with a head injury. The employee died at the
hospital due to a hemorrhage.

shock and was transported for medical care. The employee died from the injuries
on June 26, 2024.
At 3:00 p.m. on May 15, 2024, a riding lawn mower being operated by the deceased
went down a 12-foot embankment, landing on top of the victim. The Yakima County
Coroner reports that when EMS arrived, the employee was conscious and
responsive. However, the employee died during transport due to a crushing chest
injury.
At 1:00 p.m. on July 30, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a tree trimming company,
was using a pole saw to cut limbs. While lifting the pole saw, it made contact

Emergency services were called to the scene, but the employee died from the
fatal injuries. The incident occurred while working near overhead powerlines,
and the employer has been cited for violations related to working with
electrical hazards and aerial lift safety.
At 1:45 p.m. on July 30, 2024, Employee #1, a sorter/laborer employed by a
recycling facility, was walking across the area where materials were being
dumped. The employee's role involved directing vehicles to dispose of trash and
sorting through materials for recycling. While crossing the facility, a
front-end loader carrying a large steel tamper box used to compact materials on
the scales entered the area. The steel tamper box struck the employee, knocking
him down and causing him to fall under the tires of the front-end loader. The
employee was crushed and died from the fatal injuries. The incident occurred in
a high-traffic area where vehicles and heavy equipment were operating, and the
employer has been cited for safety violations related to vehicle and pedestrian
separation.
At 12:00 p.m. on June 18, 2024, Employee #1, operating Truck Unit # TKD287 with
an end-dump Trailer Unit # TRD173, was tasked with transporting topsoil material
from a work zone located next to the northbound main lanes of US HWY 59. After
parking the vehicle and performing an inspection, the employee walked around his
truck. Coworkers observed the employee at a distance before they left the area.
No witnesses were present at the time of the incident. The employee was run over
by his own truck. A company tire-man noticed the truck smoking in the trees and
found the unresponsive employee on the ground. In an attempt to prevent a fire,
the tire-man opened the driver-side door, climbed up to the cab, and discovered
the manual shifter was still in 1st gear. The tire-man shifted the vehicle into
container. At that time, the shipping container rolled over onto the employee.
The employee was struck by the container and pinned between the container and
the trailer. The employee died from multiple crushing injuries.
At 11:30 a.m. on June 10, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a
landscaping service was mowing a commercial property with an Ex Mark Lazer Zero
Turn Lawn Mower (serial number 403127090). The employee struck a steel water cap
on a metal standpipe that was situated just above ground level. The mower deck
contacted the cap, and the employee was ejected from the mower into the mower
blade. The employee was hospitalized to treat a lacerated artery in his left
calf. The employee died in the hospital due to blood loss.
At 5:45 p.m. on June 7, 2024, Employee #1 was working on an active highway
construction project, conducting inspections, measurements, and progress checks

Employee #1 performed the tasks and left the work zone. Later that evening,
Employee #1 re-entered the active work zone without making verbal or visual
contact with the Grader Operator. The employee unknowingly entered the path of
the moving grader and was struck by the left front tire of the 44,093-pound
grader, resulting in fatal crushing injuries.
At 6:30 p.m. on June 12, 2024, Employee #1, employed in highway maintenance, was
mowing grass along a public highway. While operating the bush hog, the front
tire became ensnared in a hole, causing the employee to be thrown from the
machine onto the ground in front of it. The employee became trapped between the

At 5:30 p.m. on June 4, 2024, an employee working as a painter for an assisted

While responding Coworker #1's request, the employee was shot in the head

from multiple crushing injuries including injuries to his back, chest, head,
neck and internal injuries.
At 9:25 a.m. on June 10, 2024, Employee #1 was attempting to cross a highway to
reach the median. While attempting to clear the guardrail and enter the median,
the employee was struck by a motor vehicle. The employee sustained fatal
injuries from the impact.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 13, 2024, two employees working as laborers for a dairy
support service were filling a Diller Model #STAL7250 Manure Tanker (Serial#
LD9TA33ZXMC804135). The rubber pipe sock came off the Jamesway manure filler
pipe. Employee #1 entered the tanker to retrieve the pipe sock and was overcome.
Employee #2 entered the tanker to render aid to Employee #1 and was also
overcome. Both employees died from asphyxiation due to exposure to gas such as
hydrogen sulfide, methane, and ammonia and oxygen deficiency.
At 11:56 p.m. on June 6, 2024, an employee working as a heavy truck driver for a
long-distance trucking company had parked his vehicle at a truck stop. The
employee was chatting with a coworker (another trucker) when three persons
approached the employee and coworker intending to rob them. The employee died
from being shot multiple times.
At 11:30 p.m. on June 7, 2024, an employee working for the national park service
was providing directions to a patron. The employee fell over a landscaping wall
and hit his head on a large rock. The employee died at the scene due to head
trauma including a fractured skull.
At 4:15 a.m. on June 3., 2024, an employee working as an office clerk for a
24-hour bail bonds office was working the night shift. At 4:15 a.m., the
employee responded to a knock on the door. The person at the door attacked the
employee including punching and kicking him. The employee died as a result of
his injuries. According to the local police department, the incident was a
random act of violence.
At 12:27 p.m. on May 16, 2024, Employee #1 was laying on the ground looking into
a storm drain after removing the grate, preparing to install a storm drain
debris catch. A vehicle entered the parking lot and inadvertently struck both
the employee lying on the ground and a coworker standing nearby. The impact
caused fatal injuries to Employee #1, who was crushed by the vehicle. Emergency

swerved and hit a pole.  The employee was killed.

At 10:30 a.m. on June 24, 2024, an employee working as a construction laborer

At 7:30 a.m. on February 4th, 2025,  Employee #1 was working for a roofing

installation of a bridge girder when the crane boom supporting the girder broke.
The boom struck the employee in the head. The crane's rated capacity was
exceeded due to the weight of the girder and the boom angle. The employee
suffered a fatal head injury.

Employee #1 was discovered and it was determined to have died from natural
causes on January 8 when he was found in the sleeper berth of his truck at the
employer's terminal in Seagoville, Texas. This was not covered by OSHA.
At approximately 10:14 a.m. on July 25, 2024, Employee #1 was operating a
Polaris Sportsman 450 ATV to pick up trash along a road right-of-way. The

and crashed the ATV through a vinyl privacy fence. Employee #1 was ejected from
the vehicle and died from the injuries at the scene. No autopsy was performed by
the medical examiner.
At 1:30 p.m. on January  9, 2025, Employee #1 was working as a construction
laborer for a civil engineering firm and was refueling gas canisters. A coworker
was operating a Link Belt 250X4 LF hydraulic excavator on the transfer barge

swing radius of the excavator. The excavator rotated and pinned the employee

injured due to multiple injuries.
At 10:18 a.m. on January 7, 2025, Employee #1 was operating a side-by-side
utility vehicle on a paved rural highway with a coworker. The employees were
extremities and was transported to a local hospital. He was later air lifted to
a medical center for further treatment. The employee died in the medical center
later that day.
At 2:00 p.m. on May 10, 2024, Employee #1 was overseeing the power wash machine
near a pool. While on-site, the employee fell into an empty pool. The employee
was transported to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with an anoxic brain
injury. Unfortunately, the employee passed away on May 18, 2024, due to the
injuries sustained from the fall.
At 12:15 a.m. on October 16, 2024, an employee working for a company that
provides support services for oil and gas operations was pounding in a T-post to
prevent a water transfer hose from rolling down the hill. The hose separated
under pressure and struck the employee causing him to fall to the ground. The
employee died from a fracture right leg and blunt trauma caused by the flying
hose or the fall.
At 8:00 a.m. on October 25, 2024, an employee working as a mechanical engineer
for a car manufacturer had just arrived at work and was walking to his office.
The employee collapsed during the talk due to coronary artery disease. The
employee died from acute thrombosis of the left circumflex coronary artery,
which was ruled as death from natural causes.
At 11:30 a.m. on October 29, 2024, an employee working for a remediation service
was most likely picking up rebar from a crushed concrete process that was
completed earlier. An excavator had tipped over and pinned the employee was
under the bucket. The employee died due to being crushed under the excavator arm
attachment.
At 5:00 a.m. on October 29, 2024, an employee working for a gated community had
been assigned to provide security. The employee was not responding to calls
while on patrol so a coworker was sent to check on him. The coworker found the
employee parked behind the library unresponsive in the back seat of the security
vehicle. The employee had died from a drug overdose.
At 4:30 p.m. on October 25, 2024, an employee was working on a crew with four
other employees fueling a boat when an explosion occurred. The employee died
from 3rd degree burns to his body and blunt force trauma to his head. Four other
employees were hospitalized to treat multiple burns.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 25, 2024, an employee working as a maintenance
technician for a seafood processing facility walked into a spiral freezer to
adjust equipment. The employee attempted to adjust the drive chain tension on
the equipment while defeating an interlock device. The employee was caught in
the equipment and died from crush injuries including head trauma.
At 4:00 p.m. on October 17, 2024, an employee working for a machine shop was
standing on a ladder approximately 13 feet from the ground. The employee was
lubricating the garage door which was squeaking. The employee fell off the
ladder and hit his head on the ground. The employee died from blunt force trauma
to the head, neck, and spine.
At 11:13 a.m. on October 28, 2024, an employee was working on a flat roof
spreading sealant and replacing a skylight. While using a roller, the employee
stepped on the edge of the skylight opening and fell approximately 25 feet to
the gym floor. The employee sustained multiple impact injuries from striking the
ground surface and was transported to the hospital for treatment.  The employee
later died at the hospital.

powered industrial vehicle (PIV) operator for a metal truss manufacturer was
delivering a window to a residential location. As the employee backed the
forklift down a driveway, it pivoted and began cartwheeling down the driveway.
The employee died from multiple blunt trauma when struck by the PIV.
At 2:15 p.m. on October 29, 2024, an employee was directing traffic when a
vehicle from oncoming traffic struck the employee. The employee sustained blunt
force trauma and died as a result of the injuries.
At 8:05 p.m. on October 24, 2024, an employee working as a retail store clerk
for a gift shop followed a robber down the street. The employee died when he was
shot multiple times by the robber.
At 4:00 p.m. on October 28, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a wood
products wholesaler had been tasked with moving lumber off a conveyor cutter.
While the employee moved the material, a coworker saw him reach out as if
grabbing his chest. The employee then fell to the ground. The employee died from
natural causes including dilated cardiomyopathy.
At 5:35 a.m. on October 12, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a farm
labor staffing service was driving to work. The employee crashed into a parked
pipe trailer on farm property. The employee died from multiple blunt force
trauma.
On October 28, 2024, an employee working for a landscaping service was removing
a tree from a property. The tree had fallen during a recent hurricane. The
manner in which the tree fell caused a 5-foot section of the tree to be elevated
off the ground. The crew was cutting the tree up into sections. While cutting
the tree, a section of the tree rolled and pinned the employee's head against a
rock.  A coworker cut the tree to free the employee. The crew started CPR but
was not able to revive the employee who died from blunt force trauma to his
head.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 31, 2024, an employee working as a mechanic for an
automotive shop was standing by waiting to chock a left dump truck tire in order
to pressure wash the vehicle. The truck was being driven into position by a
coworker who is the shop owner. The employee was struck and run over by the
front left truck tire. The employee died from multiple internal and external
injuries including to his torso, arms, legs, abdomen, and chest, from impact
with the tire and the ground.
At 3:00 p.m. on October 30, 2024, an employee working for a performance
promotion company was erecting a stage roof section. The steel frame structure
collapsed to the ground during erection and struck the employee on the ground.
The employee died from crush injuries to his chest and neck.
At 9:45 a.m. on October 31, 2024, an employee was driving a Genie power mobile
scaffold (scissor lift) from the cellar level to the first floor. The employee
became caught between the machinery and a wall, sustaining fatal trauma to the
chest and abdomen.
At 8:30 a.m. on October 31, 2024, an employee working for a sawmill was
attempting to remove a water hose that had become entangled in the conveyor of
the running chip reclaimer. The employee either lost his footing or became
entangled in the hose and was pulled into the machine. The employee died from
multiple trauma including amputations, burns and lacerations to his torso, lower
arms and lower legs.
At 8:57 a.m. on October 30, 2024, an employee working as a sales person for a
water supply and irrigation company was talking to a coworker operating a
WestRock machine. The employee suddenly collapsed and fell onto the coworker.
The coworker initiated an emergency response. The employee was taken to
hospital, where he was declared dead from natural causes related to an
underlying cardiovascular condition.
At 5:30 a.m. on October 31, 2024, an employee working as a truck driver for a
freight service was driving when he suddenly slumped over to his right side. The
employee died from complications of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
At 9:56 a.m. on October 31, 2024, an employee was working as a packaging machine
operator for an asphalt and block manufacturer. The asphalt was located outside
where it was raining, so the production line was not operating at the time. The
employee and a coworker were putting three 60-pound perma-patch asphalt bags
back through the line to be restitched and reflattened. The bags were filled the
prior day but had been set aside due to defects in the stitching process. The
bags had been closed with a Hamer Fischbein Model 400TNS NSR13BVDN34X14049
Sewing Head (serial Number 212876). The team had restitched and reflattened one
shift at the water treatment plant for the City of Cedar Rapids. The employee
did not return to the water treatment plant, and after a search, the fleet
vehicle was located submerged in a river.  The employee could not be found, was
not located by search and rescue personnel, and was later presumed dead. The
available evidence indicated that the employee was driving down the road, lost
control of the vehicle for an unknown reason, and drove off the road and into
the river.
At 12:15 a.m. on May 11, 2022, an employee drove a Western Express Inc Trailer
Truck into a truck yard and attempted to back into a tight parking spot. The
employee spent twenty-four minutes trying to fit the trailer truck into the
spot. While the employee was backing up, he suddenly opened the driver side door
and exited the truck as it continued to move. The employee was killed when he
was ultimately crushed by the truck and a parked J.B. Hunt trailer.

employee  noticed that the boxes were not coming out clean and began to clean

wearing gloves and using a rag to wipe down the printing cylinder to clean it

to know any extension tools available to help clean the printing cylinder.  The
employee's hand got caught between the bed and the printing cylinder, crushing
his hand.  The employee was hospitalized to treat these injuries.

shop for metal parts. The employee was carrying some steel parts that had been

finger and thumb. He suffered the partial amputation of his left thumb in

violations were to be issued.

The employee was hospitalized to treat a spinal injury.
At approximately 2:00 p.m. on February 14, 2022, an employee set plywood on a

left hand. The index finger of the employee's left hand was amputated, and the

At 4:00 a.m. on December 8, 2021, an employee was operating an extruding machine

hospitalization.

Park as part of a five-person work crew that was reducing the flammable fuel
load in the South Grove Burn Unit.   A coworker, the site lead, heard the
cracking of a tree, yelled "tree" out to the crew.  The employee, and his other

his location, he was struck by the top of the tree and landed on his chest/face
in the debris.  The employee was conscious and responsive, complaining of leg
pain.  As his coworkers were carrying him to meet with EMS, he went unconscious
and later pronounced dead at the site. The employee was killed as a result of
internal bleeding from multiple injuries.
At 8:30 p.m. on May 9, 2022, an employee was stocking shelves in a retail store.
The employee collapsed and  died from an unspecified body system illness and/or
injury.
At 9:53 a.m. on May 11, 2022, an employee was performing preparation work for a
new roofing system on a low slope commercial roof.  The employee was part of a
crew that was tearing off the existing roofing system and replacing it with a
new spray foam type of roofing system. The work area included an unguarded dome
skylight measuring 4 ft by 7 ft that did not have fall protection installed
around the opening. The employee was spraying foam and carrying a 5 gal bucket

laying on the roof and fell 18 ft through the skylight opening to the concrete
floor.  A coworker observed the incident, descended from the roof to check on
the employee and called 9-1-1. First responders from the police and fire
department responded to the scene and the employee was taken to the hospital,
where he died from injuries sustained in the fall. The work crew members were
not wearing their provided personal fall arrest systems (PFAS) while replacing
the roof.
At 3:23 p.m. on May 5, 2022, an employee was installing a metal roof on a
residential building.  The employee was popping a chalk line on the metal
roofing panels when he fell off the side of the roof, falling a distance of 12
feet to the ground. The employee was killed from injuries sustained upon impact.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 11, 2022, an employee was climbing a derrick ladder to
prepare stacking pipes in the rack. Two bolts holding the deadman block in
position broke, the deadman block was released and struck the back of the
employee's head, killing him.

carpenter at a ship repair company was assigned to cut DC wood plugs for a
ship's hull with a JET bandsaw, model JWBS-20QT. During the process, a sliver of
wood got jammed between the blade and table.  The employee then proceeded to
remove it without first shutting off the machine. When the employee attempted to
pull it out, the blade pulled the sliver of wood down pulling his left hand
toward the blade, lacerating the left pinky finger. The employee was admitted
and treated at Scripps Mercy Hospital for lacerations to the hand and surgery
for articular abnormality. At approximately 07:17 p.m. on December 01, 2021,
DOSH was notified of the incident and arrived on site on January 19, 2022.
At 5:12 a.m. on May 12, 2022, an employee was pinned between the left tractor
tire and an attachment.  The employee was killed.
At 10:00 a.m. on May 12, 2022, an employee was attempting to remove the top
stack of product that was double stacked.  The 800-pound product fell on top of
the employee, pinning him between the product and the mast of the forklift.  The
employee was killed.
At 2:00 p.m. on May 10,2022, an employee, a heavy machine operator, was
operating an excavator in a building.  A fire broke out at the building and the
employee was unable to evacuate.  The employee was killed due to suffocation.
At 3:45 a.m. on April 7, 2022, an employee was working the front counter.  While
standing there, he stiffened straight up and fell over backward to the floor.
Earlier in the shift, the employee went out of camera view and apparently fell
to the hospital, where he later died.
At 10:40 a.m. on October 21, 2021, six employees were working for a staffing
agency that provided farm workers for agricultural sites. They were not migrant
workers. They were packing grapes at a grape vineyard. At approximately 10:00
a.m., an employee was in the break area located outside the grape packing area
outside the building when she had a medical emergency for a reported preexisting
medical condition. She was transported to a medical clinic by her supervisor.
While the supervisor was offsite, other employees in the indoor packing room and
outdoor break area outside the packing room complained of an unknown odor.
Employees of the staffing agency called emergency medical services. Four local
agencies responded. The building was evacuated by the county fire department.
The building was cleared by a hazardous material agency after an interior entry
and inspection by the hazardous material team. It was determined that the grape
packing room was cooled by a mixture of propylene glycol and water. No abnormal
air readings were found at the time of the incident by the facility plant
manager or first responders. No evidence of a refrigeration leak was found in
the grape packing area or from other adjacent refrigerated areas of the facility
The building was found to be safe and returned back to control of the vineyard
at approximately 4:00 p.m. Packing operations resumed the next day without
incident. No chemical release was found. The workers had experienced chest pain,
headache, and nausea. They were all treated witout hospitalization. This was a
joint employer site, but it was not a multiemployer site. This incident is also
recorded as investigation number 145337, which covers the staffing agency. That
investigation lists seven employees. The UPA is the same for both, 1829092.
At 3:30 p.m. on October 14, 2021, an employee had been directed to replace a
pre-existing 2 ft by 2 ft oriented strand board (OSB) floor-hole cover on the
seventh floor of an building. The employee fell through the hole, breaking
through a piece of drywall and possibly the piece of the OSB . The employee fell
through uncovered floor holes in the floors below until he was able to stop his
fall on the fourth floor. The employee sustained a fractured scapula and was
hospitalized.
At 9:10 p.m. on October 22, 2021, an employee (technician) was verifying a cable
line from one side of a street to a residential house. The employee was
electrocuted and was killed.
Employee #1 was working for a county's sheriff department. It was suspected that
he contracted COVID-19 from another employee during a training course on August

later. In addition, Employee #1 worked in a unit where several individuals
tested positive for COVID-19. The employer thus determined there to be
reasonable suspicion that Employee #1 contracted the virus at work. On September
17, 2021, Employee #1 died due to cardiopulmonary collapse. His conditions
included cardiogenic and septic shock, acute ST-elevation, myocardial

Employees were working as correctional officers in a correctional facility when
they were assigned to transport an inmate to the hospital. One of the employees
developed symptoms consistent with a COVID-19 infection four days later and was

At 5:15 p.m. on April 13, 2022, an employee was inspecting the timing chain on
the green stacker unit. The employee climbed onto the structural frame of the
unit and was struck in the head by the carriage bar. The employee was killed.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 25, 2022, four individuals were moving an ice cream
machine from the back of the building into the ice cream  production room.  The
room was cleared of obstacles and the door was removed to create a clear path
for the machine to go through the door.  Employee #1 was assisting in moving the

At 12:00 p.m. on November 21, 2021, Employee #1 was moving a large refrigerator
using a pallet jack when he stepped on a piece of plastic and slipped. The
employee fell and injured his right leg and broke his right hip. He was
transported to the hospital and admitted to treat his injuries.
At 11:17 a.m. on October 22, 2021, an employee was trimming the top of an oak
tree under a power line using a tree climbing system. The employee had not

employee was hospitalized to treat a back injury.
At 4:11 p.m. on November 2, 2021, an employee was driving 2,000 gallon water

At 12:30 p.m. on April 14, 2022, an employee was moving along a two-section
shingles to a roof during a roofing replacement project for a residential
building. The employee fell 30 feet off the roof onto a concrete surface and was
killed, sustaining fractures to multiple bones.
At 1:45 p.m. on May 19, 2022, an employee was raising scaffold outriggers while
preparing to perform masonry work at a new residential building. The employee
attempted to jump from the east area to the south area of the scaffold but fell
12 feet onto the concrete floor, landing headfirst. The employee sustained skull

At 10:21 a.m. on May 19, 2022, an employee was removing foam from a roof while
performing renovation work on a commercial building. The employee stepped down
into a deteriorated fiberglass skylight which gave way and caused the employee
to fall 34 feet onto a concrete surface.  The employee incurred a head
concussion and was killed.
At 9:31 a.m. on November 21, 2021, Employee #1 was resetting an alarm when they

At 2:45 p.m. on May 18, 2022, an employee was returning from lunch when he fell

The employee was transported to the hospital, where he later died.
At approximately 2:00 a.m. on November 25, 2021, an employee replaced propane on

At 9:45 a.m. on May 15, 2023, an employee suffered a heart attack due to natural

At 4:16 p.m. on May 9, 2023, Employee #1, bartender at the employer's
restaurant, went to take his break in the restroom. Employee #1 was found
