transported him to the hospital, where he was treated and declared dead on May
13, 2023. Employee #1 died of a fentanyl overdose.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 18, 2023, an employee was in an unprotected 10 foot trench,
leveling gravel underneath a 24-inch PVC sewer line. The employee was killed.
At 2:00 a.m. on May 19, 2023, an employee was retrieving a metal sample. The
shear table rotated to an upright position while his head was near the shear
table and shear head. The employee's head was crushed between the shear table
and the shear head bottom half. The employee was killed.  The equipment was
still energized after opening the gate that had an interlock switch.
At 7:35 a.m. on May 16, 2023, an employee was standing on a forklift, holding
onto the back of the mast. The employee slipped or lost his balance.  As a
result, his foot/feet became entangled in the forklift controls, and he was
pulled up between the forklift cab and the back of the mast. The employee was
killed due to crushing injuries.
At 6:30 p.m. on May 11, 2023, an employee was preparing to open the site to the
public. The employee was locked inside a freezer.  The employee was killed.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 19, 2023, Employee #1  and Coworker #1 were preparing to
install spacer rings for a manhole.  Coworker #2 brought a front-end loader to
move the spacers and then parked the front-end loader and exited.  The front-end
loader rolled down a slight incline, running into the manhole. The cone section
of the manhole collapsed, crushing Employee #1 inside.  The employee sustained
crushing injuries to the head and was killed.
At 9:00 p.m. on May 18, 2023, three employees were working at their
workstations, assembling engines. Employee #1 and Employee #2 had a personal
dispute related to their personal lives. Employee #2 brought a handgun to work.
Employee #2 shot and killed Employee #1. Employee #2 shot Employee #3 in the
leg. Employee #2 went out the backside of the building and shot himself/herself
in the head, resulting in a head injury. Employee's #2 and #3 were hospitalized.
At 3:30 p.m. on May 18, 2023, an employee had notched a standing tree and was
making the back cut.  The crew was clearing storm damage from power lines, so
lines could be put back up and re-energized. The tree kicked out and struck the
employee before he had completed the back cut. The employee was killed by the
large oak tree, approximately 74.5 feet tall with a 47-inch diameter at the
point where the back cut was being made.
At 2:00 p.m. on May 19, 2023, an employee was guiding a vehicle (i.e., 1989
Gumman Olson step van) onto the vehicle lift. The vehicle experienced excessive
momentum and the brakes failed to engage. This caused the vehicle to lurch
forward, striking the employee. The employee was killed due to blunt force
trauma.
Employees were working as order pickers in a warehouse and distribution center
when a COVID-19 outbreak occurred. Thirty-four employees tested positive for
COVID-19 and developed symptoms. None of the employees required hospitalization
for treatment of their infections.
At 6:30 a.m. on December 16, 2022, an employee was walking in a parking lot
behind a vehicle that was backing up. The employee was struck by the vehicle,
knocked to the ground and killed.
At 5:45 a.m. on May 17, 2023, Employee #1 was training Employee #2, paratransit
Operator Trainee, in the operations of a paratransit vehicle for the Niagara
Frontier Transportation Authority. Employee #1 was seated behind the farebox and
associated barrier on the passenger side of the vehicle. Employee #2 was at the
interchange of Interstate 190 and Interstate 290. While exiting from the I-190S
to the I-290E, Operator Trainee struck the center barrier, causing the
paratransit van to flip onto the passenger side. Employee #1 was ejected through
the front door of the paratransit van. The paratransit van rolled onto Employee
#1, crushing them between the paratransit van and the interstate roadway. The
operator trainee incurred unspecified injuries and was treated without
hospitalization.
At 8:00 a.m. on May 17, 2023, an employee was standing next to the owner, who
was cutting a tree on a steep slope. The employee ran in the direction of the
falling tree and was crushed by the tree. The employee was killed.
At 5:00 p.m. on May 16, 2023, an employee was dispatched to the Long Beach area
to tow a vehicle. The employee arrived at the location, parked behind the
vehicle to be towed, and passed out. Witnesses at the location found the
employee unconscious, called 911, and the employee was transported to Long Beach
Memorial Hospital. The employee died of a possible heart attack.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 6, 2023, an employee was standing on top of the drywall
ceiling, looking at sprinkler installation build plans. The employee stepped on
the area of drywall unprotected by the steel framing and fell through the
working on the chain saw while Coworker #1 was backing the excavator. Coworker
#1 did not see the employee and struck him with the excavator. A private citizen
witnessed the event from the roadway and observed the employee trapped under the
treads/tracks of the excavator. The witness ran up to Coworker #1 who was still
operating the excavator and shouted, "you ran over your man." Coworker #1 then
moved the excavator forward and exited the excavator. The witness phoned 911 and
summoned EMS. Law enforcement and EMS arrived on scene and performed life saving
measures. At 2:46 p.m. EMS pronounced the employee dead on the scene. The
employee had died from blunt force trauma including crushing injuries to his
back, hip, and abdomen,
At 2:00 p.m. on July 19, 2023, an employee attempted to assist in clearing a
sink drain in the kitchen. The employee poured some drainpipe cleaner into the
sink drain after bleach had already been poured down. White gas began to rise up
from the drain, and the employee attempted to take a plunger to the drain. The
employee began to have trouble breathing shortly thereafter. Loss of
consciousness led to loss of life due to the chemical mixture (gas).  The
employee was killed.
At 3:45 a.m. on July 20, 2023, an employee working as a construction laborer for
an engineering contractor was working on a crew placing bridge decking. The
employee was assisting with the construction of false decking. He was working in
the bucket of an aerial lift underneath an overpass spacing supports when a
semi-truck entered the work zone. The truck struck the lift killing the
employee. The employee died from blunt trauma to his head.
At 11:00 a.m. on March 20, 2023, an employee was working with coworkers, doing
repairs to the feed hopper and main crusher of the Recycled Asphalt Crushing and
Screening Plant. The employee picked up a piece of angle iron approximately 6
inches by 4.5 inches by 50 inches long. He took the angle iron to the asphalt
plant's fabrication area to cut it down to the desired size needed. He walked
between the two large stockpiles of recycled asphalt. While he was walking to
the fabrication area, a CAT 966M front-end loader, being operated by a coworker,
was traveling from the raw recycled asphalt stockpile to the finish stockpile.
While the coworker was moving forward toward the finished stockpile, he raised
the loader bucket and was shaking it to remove any raw material from the bucket
before picking up clean finished product. As the loader approached the clean
finished stockpile, the coworker felt the loader move strangely. The coworker
and the employee had made contact with each other, causing the employee to fall
to the ground, face up, under the front and rear tires of the loader's left
side. As the employee fell to the ground, the rear left tire of the loader
rolled over his face and abdomen, causing immediate fatal injuries. The employee
was killed.
At 1:00 p.m. on July 7, 2023, an employee working as a structural steel worker
for a steel erection contractor was working on a commercial building project.
The employee was sitting in the shade after returning from lunch. The employee
stood up and started walking when he passed out. The employee had died from
natural causes including cardiovascular disease. The narrative indicate that
heat may have been a contributing factor.
At 3:30 p.m. on June 23, 2023, an employee was picking up roof debris at ground
level and then climbed up to the top of the roof to assist in roof tile removal.
The employee began to feel sick. The employee died from hypoxic ischemic
encephalopathy due to complications of hyperthermia, anamnestic, due to
environmental heat exposure while working outdoors.
At 12:00 noon on July 20, 2023, an employee, a tree trimmer, was trimming a tree
when he made indirect contact with a 7.2 KV power line and was electrocuted.
At 12:45 p.m. on June 24, 2023, an employee working for a transmission line
construction company was using a drill. The employee was holding part of newly
installed equipment when the ground wire made contact with a cutout of the
installed equipment. This created a phase to ground circuit, which the worker
contacted with his drill and bare hand. The employee died due to electrocution.
On July 20, 2023, an employee working for a framing contractor was working on a
scaffold installing siding. The employee was not wearing fall protection when he
fell between 18 and 20 feet to the ground below. The employee lacerated his
forehead and went in and out of consciousness while being transported to the
between a forklift and a produce bin.  The employee was using a forklift. He
left the forklift in neutral and walked in front of it to get something.  The
forklift was left on a slight slope. The forklift rolled forward, crushing the
employee between the forklift and an onion bin.  The employee was killed.
At 11:23 a.m. on October 1, 2023, an employee was applying fungicide in a CA
room and died.
At 10:20 a.m. on December 1, 2023, an employee working for a tree service was
working in a tree cutting limbs with a chain saw. The employee inadvertently cut
his lifeline with a chainsaw and fell about 50 feet landing on the concrete
driveway.  The employee died from multiple blunt force trauma.
At 8:40 p.m. on October 3, 2023, an employee was painting the conference room
and was removing tape from the walls while standing on a work platform. The
employee collapsed from the work platform/ladder. The employee suffered three
broken ribs and a head injury. The employee was killed.
At 2:43 p.m. on December 12, 2023, Employee #1 was working for a roofing
below where he was standing, causing fractures to the skull, a concussion, and
potentially broken bones in the head, neck, and back area. The employee was
killed.
At 4:00 p.m. on March 18, 2024, an employee was hired to cut down a tree from a
previous tornado in July. After the tree was cut, it struck another tree,
bounced and struck the employee, crushing the employee. The employee was killed
due to blunt force trauma to the head and body.
At 10:30 a.m. on March 19, 2024, Employee # 1, a driver, was driving and stopped
at a light. He was driving en route to the next delivery. Employee # 1 suffered
a massive heart attack while he was driving his route. He was killed.
At 9:45 p.m. on March 16, 2024, Employees #1 and #2 were inside a basket on an
Elliot truck, repairing a traffic light.  The smokestack of a semi-truck
contacted the arm where the basket is attached, which caused the bucket to spin
and ejected both employees to the ground.  Employee #1 was killed, and Employee
#2 suffered serious, life-threatening injuries and was hospitalized. The
investigation was able to determine that failure to follow industry
traffic-layout practices exposed employees to vehicular traffic hazards while
working from the aerial lift extended bucket.
At 10:45 a.m. on March 19, 2024, an employee was shaking out metal decking for a
second story roof. The employee slipped and fell approximately 29 feet 8 inches
onto concrete.  The employee had a severe laceration to the back of the head and
was pronounced dead at the scene.
At 2:56 p.m. on November 29, 2023, a homeowner had hired a gardener to perform
various gardening tasks at their residence. Of those tasks, one was to trim a
pine tree in the front yard. On the day of the accident, the gardener delegated
the work to a friend, who was a seasoned tree trimmer. The tree trimmer
sustained a fatal injury while trimming the tree, and body retrieval was
performed by the Anaheim Fire Department.  A pine tree branch was caught on the
fall protection system the individual was utilizing. The cause of death was
determined to be blunt force injuries of the torso according to the Orange
County Sheriff-Coroner's office. The employer was cited for 3203(a) and 3241(l).
There were no other violations witnessed at the time of the investigation.
At 3:00 p.m. on March 19, 2024, an employee, the owner of the company, was
installing gutters & downspouts on new residential construction.  The employee
was preparing to relocate a ladder jack scaffold from the rear of the house to
the side of the house.  Branches from a neighboring tree next to the property
were in the way of the relocation area of the scaffold.  The employee climbed up
the tree to cut some of the branches.  The owner slipped and fell approximately
10 feet from the tree branch onto a wrought iron fence and was impaled by the
fence toppers.  The coworkers that were onsite removed the employee from the
fence.  He was later taken by emergency services to the University of Chicago
Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
At 3:30 p.m. on March 19, 2024, an employee was on a 6-foot ladder removing a
piece of ceiling tile that was hanging from the speaker cables that were in the
ceiling. The employee was coming down from the ladder and lost his balance and
fell back onto the wall behind him. After the employee fell back onto the wall,
he walked around to throw away the piece of ceiling tile in the dumpster. As he
was walking to the dumpster, the coworker who was working with him stated the
employee lost his balance again and fell down. The employee died of
heart-related issues.
At 9:00 a.m. on March 19, 2024, an employee was operating a forklift, moving a
welding machine.  He was carrying a 12-foot rope around his neck.  One end of
the rope fell to the ground and was caught at the back wheels of the forklift.
The employee was strangled and killed.
At 7:15 a.m. on March 18, 2024, an employee, a truck driver, was folding his
tarp that he took off his trailer. The employee positioned himself behind
another company vehicle, in a manner that did not allow for another driver to
visually see the employee before backing up his vehicle. The employee was
fatally injured as result of being struck by and runover by another vehicle.
At 12:00 p.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was air leak testing a newly
installed 56-inch drainpipe.  The pipe extended from one side of the street to
the other, roughly 150 feet.  They placed a rubber pressure plug on one side and
another on the testing site across the street. At about 30 minutes into the air
leak testing, they noticed the pressure on the pipe had decreased, so the
employee descended to the bottom of the trench and began to apply soapy water
around the edges of the plug.  The plug gave way, projecting itself and the
employee on to a wall approximately 15 feet from the pipe. The employee was
killed by the force of the pressurized rubber plug.
At 12:30 p.m. on March 18, 2024, employees were disassembling and moving a sign.
Two employees were working inside the sign box, walking on the aluminum framing
and sheet metal, cutting three welds connecting the sign to the beam so that a
crane could shake the box loose. Employee #1 was on the south side of the beam,
preparing to cut the last weld. Employee #1 had climbed up to cut the last weld,
when he fell to the floor of the sign box. He then fell through the sheet metal
to the ground, approximately 64 feet below.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 11:45 a.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was on top of a steel roof truss.
The employee fell approximately 26 feet to the concrete floor.  The employee was
killed due to blunt force trauma.
At 4:00 p.m. on March 15, 2024, an employee working for a residential contractor
was painting a basement during a remodel. According to the medical report, the
employee died from exposure to the paint due to having high amounts of cocaine
and alcohol in his system.
At 12:00 a.m. on March 17, 2024, an employee, a mechanic, was repairing a
hydraulic leak in a refurbished Taylor forklift (model: T360L). The employee was
working under the raised carriage/forks of the forklift. A sudden loss of
hydraulic pressure resulted in the carriage/forks falling on the employee,
resulting in fatal injuries.
At 12:00 a.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was leaning in a machine,
attempting to clean it as the machine was in operation. The employee's ponytail
was caught in a horizontal shaft named the knuckler shaft. The employee was
pulled into the machine by her hair, until the machine became jammed and
stopped.  The employee was caught in the machine and killed.
At 8:53 p.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was operating a stand-up powered
industrial truck. The employee was not authorized or trained to operate the
specific stand-up powered industrial truck that was involved in the incident.
The employee lost control of the powered industrial truck, causing him to become
pinned between the powered industrial truck and a racking system in an aisleway.
The employee was killed due to mechanical asphyxiation.
At 12:00 p.m. on March 20, 2024, Employee #1 was framing a pole-style storage
facility building. Employee #1 was working on the roof near the edge, when the
eave purlin pulled out of the pole, which caused Employee #1 to fall
approximately 10 feet to the concrete ground below, striking his head.  Employee
#1 died of a hinge fracture to the base of the skull.  Failure to utilize fall
protection may have contributed to the incident.
At 2:30 p.m. on March 21, 2024, an employee, a nurse, was walking into a
hallway. The nurse stopped and put her hands up near her chest (palms facing
outward) as a behavior health student ran toward her. The student accidentally
stepped on the employee's foot, causing her to fall backwards and impact the
back of her head against the hard floor surface. The student fell over on top of
her during the incident. The employee died due to head trauma and internal
bleeding.
At 8:17 p.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was going to see if a damper was
open on a fan. The employee was found unresponsive. The employee died due to
cardiac arrest.
At 2:44 p.m. on March 18, 2024, Employee #1 was performing routine maintenance
underneath an eXmark LZS749AKC72400 zero-turn lawn mower, raised approximately
two feet above the ground, using a Budgit 1/2-ton chain hoist that was hooked
directly to the roll-over bar. The hoist chain slipped, shifting the load
downward, and crushing the face of Employee #1. Employee #1 was killed.
At 4:00 a.m. on March 22, 2024, an employee was sweeping the facility and eating
her lunch/dinner.  She died of natural causes.
At 1:08 p.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee died of silicosis from occupational
order.  He then looked down the road and noticed that the employee's forklift
was pulled to the side, facing the shingles along the westside fence-line.
About 15 minutes passed, and the other forklift driver went to check on the
employee to make sure he was not stuck.  The other forklift driver noticed that
the employee's forklift had the left-side door latched open and he was hunched
over to the right side of the steering wheel. The forklift operator and the
manager noticed blood around the mouth of the employee, as well as on the
floorboard and right-side door and window. The employee was unresponsive.  They
performed CPR, and EMS was called.  The employee was taken to the hospital,
where he died.  The medical examiner report determined that the fatality was due
to cirrhosis of the liver.
At 12:00 a.m. on January 13, 2024, an employee was cleaning the car wash tunnel
and equipment. The employee was cleaning the passenger side exit Top Mount Side
Washer referred to as a "wrap." The wraps are 6 feet tall and 42 inches in
diameter (decreasing diameter from top to bottom). The wraps weigh 300 pounds
and spin at 300 rpm. The employee was cleaning the wrap as instructed (while
spinning), using a pressure washer hose which became entangled in the wrap and
around the employee. The employee was trapped in the spinning wrap with her wet
hooded sweatshirt wrapped around her head. The employee was killed due to
multiple blunt force trauma injuries and strangulation. The employee was not
trained as an authorized employee and was not instructed to lockout the
equipment in the tunnel during cleaning activities.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 15, 2021, an employee working as an installer for a solar
panel contractor was marking a roof with chalk line in preparation for solar
panel installation. The employee tripped and fell to the concrete surface below.
The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured leg and wrist.
At 4:30 p.m. on January 22, 2024, Employee #1, a 37-year-old male landscaper,
was operating a track mounted, remote controlled stump grinder. Employee #1 was
in the process of moving the grinder from one location to the next, with the
grinder still fully engaged. At one point, Employee #1 fell in front of the
stump grinder's wheel and sustained fatal injuries from the cutter wheel to the
head and face.
At 1:15 a.m. on January 22, 2024, an employee had picked up a load and was
driving a truck.  The truck slipped and rolled into a ditch, resulting in a
motor vehicle accident.  The employee was killed.
At 8:47 a.m. on January 22, 2024, an employee went to the break room, after
working on a lathe machine for 1.5 hours. The employee laid his head in his arms
on the table while sitting and fell to the ground later when approached by a
coworker.  The employee died of a heart attack/atherosclerotic cardiovascular
disease with thrombosis.
At 11:00 a.m. on January 9, 2024, one of the owners of a mobile home park found
an employee in the back of a work/utility truck. Sheets of oriented strand board
(OSB) had fallen over, pinning the employee by the neck. The employee was
killed.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 21, 2024, an employee was walking to the main entry way
to open the door for a coworker, when he fell.  The employee suffered head
trauma and was killed.
At 6:00 a.m. on January 11, 2024, a sleeping driver was awakened by a forklift
operator, who gave him his unloading directions and took the driver's paperwork.
The forklift operator went back in the warehouse, waiting for the driver to back
up to the dock.  At 6:35 a.m., the forklift operator realized the driver had not
yet docked the trailer. The forklift operator approached the trailer to find the
driver on the ground, four feet from the cab and not moving.  The driver was not
responding to touch, and there was a lot of blood on the ground around the
driver's head.  911 was called, but the driver was pronounced dead in the
ambulance at 7:45 a.m.  It was believed that the driver slipped and fell on an
icy patch, hitting his head.
At 10:00 a.m. on November 24, 2023, an employee was operating a forklift outside
the facility. The employee was found slumped over in the forklift cabin by
customers. The employee died of heart failure.
At 11:20 a.m. on January 19, 2024, an employee was sanding the drywall near the
12-foot ceiling, using a ladder. The employee fell off the ladder to the paved
ground.  The employee was killed due to blunt force head injuries.
At 7:00 p.m. on January 15, 2024, an employee tripped and fell forward, striking
her head on a parked car. The employee was killed.
At 12:10 a.m. on August 29, 2023, an employee, a Night Operator, was releasing
pressure from the compressor cooling coils (blow-down), using a 10-inch crescent
wrench to turn the blow-down valve to the open position, releasing the trapped
gas through a blow-down pipe mounted vertically on the compressor. The blow-down
pipe came loose from the mounting brackets under the high pressure, bending and
striking the operator in the head and hand. The employee suffered a fatal head
injury. The blow-down pipe was  approximately 11-feet 9-inches long and
approximately 2-2.5-inches wide.  The pipe came loose from the U-bolts that
anchored the pipe to the compressor.
At 2:30 p.m. on January 22, 2024, an employee was welding sounding tubes inside
a double-hulled vessel of a new construction ship (i.e., confined space). The
employee was found unresponsive inside the confined space. The cause of death is
unknown.
At 7:05 a.m. on September 27, 2023, an employee was attempting to move a piece
of a heavy equipment trailer with a John Deere excavator.  The trailer struck
the employee, who suffered blunt force trauma to the chest and abdomen.  The
employee was killed.
At 9:15 a.m. on January 18, 2024, Employee #1 was working inside a 7,000-gallon
tanker trailer. Employee #1 was tasked with inspecting the damage of the
interior of the tanker. Employee #1 was in the early stages of the tank
inspection when he lost consciousness. A coworker noticed that Employee #1 lost
consciousness, and s/he called the foreman to call 9-1-1. The coworker climbed
into the tank to try and rescue Employee #1. The foreman arrived at the tank and
realized the attendant wasn't on the ladder. The foreman grabbed an air hose and
began to spray air into the tank.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 9:00 a.m. on January 5, 2024, an employee was working at home. The employer
was not getting a response from the employee. A family member went to the
apartment and discovered the employee was unresponsive and dead.  The employee
suffered an unspecified medical event.
At 2:30 p.m. on January 23, 2024, an employee was pouring concrete into a new
built wall. He fell 19 feet from an extendable 24 feet ladder to the concrete
floor.  The employee suffered a concussion and broken ribs and was killed.
At 1:30 p.m. on November 27, 2023, an employee was at a site location fulfilling
insurance adjustment. The employee was killed due to blunt force trauma to the
station. The employee was electrocuted and suffered arc blast burns to the
chest, neck and face.  The employee died.
At 5:00 p.m. on April 2, 2024, an employee and a coworker (foreman) working for
a utilities service were treating a utility pole with chemicals for to prevent
pests. The crew was preparing the pole for the installation of a steel support
truss. They had finished excavating the hole and applied the chemical treatments
at the base of the pole. At this time, the employee was carrying the truss in
order to place it into position by the pole for a second crew to install it. As
the employee carried the pole vertically, it contacted a live overhead power
line. The employee died due to electrocution.
At 12:15 p.m. on April 5, 2024, an employee working for the U.S. Customs and
Border Patrol was working from an 80-foot tower. The employee had completed
installation of some equipment at the top of the tower. The employee had a
medical emergency while descending the tower at approximately 20 feet from the
ground level. Coworkers onsite noticed he was not responding, so they proceeded
to climb the tower and lower him to the ground. The employee was transported to
a hospital, where staff reported he had experienced cardiac arrest.
At 10:30 a.m. on April 5, 2024, an Employee #1 and Employee #2 were working for
a window and door contractor were installing a metal awning on the front of a
commercial building. At the time, two drivers in two separate cars were racing
down the road. One of the drivers lost control of the car coming around a curve.
The car careened off the road and struck both employees running them over.
Employee #1 sustained multiple blunt force trauma of his chest, back and abdomen
and died. Employee #2 received medical treatment without hospitalization for
head injuries.
At 9:49 a.m. on April 8, 2024, an employee working for a fast food restaurant
was clocked out while taking his morning break. At 10:10 a.m., he was called
over to a vehicle by the boyfriend of a coworker. When he arrived at the driver
side window, the boyfriend shot the employee in the chest with a firearm. The
employee fell to the ground and the perpetrator drove away. The employee died
from a gunshot wound to the chest.
At 2:23 p.m. on March 29, 2024, one of the owners of Top Rock Trucking LLC was
run over and killed by a dump truck while hooking up a trailer. An employee was
also run over during the incident, but the employee survived and was
hospitalized to treat unspecified serious injuries.
At 2:30 p.m. on August 7, 2023, an employee was trimming trees.  The employee
was preparing to descend a tree after completing trimming. The employee
connected the descent line to his body belt and then proceeded to disconnect his
investigating and fixing the problem when he told the employee to back up as he
began to operate the bucket. The employee stepped out of the way as the coworker
moved the bucket. But the employee decided to walk back into the operation zone,
presumably to observe the pin alignment on the bucket. At the same time, the
coworker moved the bucket striking the employee in the chest and pushing him
against a loader. The coworker immediately disengaged the machine and aided the
employee. The employee collapsed at which time the coworker called 911. CPR was
performed following the instructions of the 911 dispatcher. The employee was
transported to the hospital via ambulance, where the employee later died from
crushing injuries to the chest and abdomen.
At 3:00 p.m. on August 24, 2024, an employee working as a heavy equipment
operator for a construction contractor was checking on the status of a piling
machine. The piling equipment engaged while the employee was positioned in the
equipment. The employee died from crushing head injuries.
At 1:03 p.m. on August 22, 2024, an employee working as a steel worker for a
construction contractor was wrapping a synthetic sling around a steel beam. A
coworker operating a rough terrain forklift adjusted the forks stabilizing the
beam in an upright position. This caused the beam to fall over onto the employee
as he was wrapping the beam. The employee died from crushing injuries to his
chest.
At 7:54 a.m. on August 23, 2024, Employee #1, a co-owner of a tree trimming

flange to interconnect three battery tanks from the tank roof.  Two days prior
to welding, there was a liquid leak from one of the tanks. The supervisor was
instructed by the plant manager to open the vessel to purge the mud. The
supervisor instructed his employees to shut off the valves once they were
installed. However, there still appeared to be fluid leaking from the tank, as
stated by the plant manager. The supervisor's crew installed the valves upside
down, thus leaving the valves open. This occurrence led to gas leaking into the
tanks. There were three employees working on top of the tank. The supervisor did
not conduct any flammable testing prior to welding. There was an explosion.
During the explosion, the lid and two of the employees were thrown. Employee #1
and Employee #2 were pronounced dead at the scene. A coworker jumped over to the
other tank prior to the explosion; he was rescued alive with no injuries. Only
one of the three employees was utilizing fall protection at the time of the
incident. The aerial lift that was being utilized had a burned and wilted basket
with a missing gate. The tank that the employees were installing flanges on was
missing the lid.

to the ground.  He was crushed by the counterweight and the inner frame of the
base and later died.

At 6:00 a.m. on November 13, 2023, a firefighting crew responded to a building
fire. Engine 55 performed suppression operations, while Truck 44 (T44) performed
forcible entry and ventilation operations. A crew of two from T44, including
Firefighter 1, went to the flat roof of the four-story building to perform
vertical ventilation. A crew of two from Squad 1 joined the crew to assist in
ventilation operations. Firefighters operating on the roof identified two light
shafts covered in corrugated plastic. The plastic covering over one shaft was
removed by a firefighter to aid in ventilation. The firefighter left a
flashlight near the open shaft to identify the location and announced this. The
T44 crew used a power saw and axe to open the roof for additional ventilation. A
firefighter on the T44 roof crew asked a firefighter from the Squad 1 crew where
the other crew member (Firefighter 1) from T44 was. The firefighter from Squad 1
looked down the open shaft and heard a firefighter distress alarm sounding
(PASS). This was communicated to command and a mayday response was requested by
the incident commander. Firefighter 1 fell down one of two light shafts to the
basement of the four-story building. Firefighter 1 struck I-beams that spanned
the floors and landed on his back/bottle. Due to limited access, crews
determined that it would be best to breach the light shaft on the second floor,
descend to package Firefighter 1, and raise him to an opening that was breached
on the first floor. Firefighter 1 remained conscious until the time he was
removed from the shaft and placed on the cot. Lifesaving efforts commenced and
Firefighter 1 was transported to a hospital, but he died from his injuries. The
cause of death was multiple blunt force injuries due to a fall from height.

stuck in the line.  Employee #1 proceeded to the receiver location and directed

attempt to push the PIGs back to the launcher.  He then returned to the launcher

concussion and was hospitalized.

colleagues, which led to a tow truck being called for roadside assistance. With
the tow truck being close by, the employee stepped out into oncoming traffic and
was struck by a motor vehicle.  Emergency authorities were called to the scene,
and EMS officials transported the injured employee to a nearby hospital, where
he was pronounced dead.
At 10:00 a.m. on June 26, 2024, Employee #1 was mowing the lawn next to a
retaining wall on a slope greater than 15 degrees when he fell to the lower
level. The lawn mower landed on top of the employee, crushing him. The employee
was killed.
At 8:51 a.m. on July 12, 2024, an employee was assisting with loading an
oversized door frame onto the flatbed of a truck. The employee was standing on
the forks of a forklift, holding an oversized French door frame to stabilize it.
The forklift was driven into the side of the flatbed truck, pinning the
employee between the oversized door and the flatbed of the truck. The employee
was killed due to traumatic asphyxia and blunt force trauma.
At 3:00 p.m. on July 16, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was holding a tape measure while taking measurements for the spacing of soil
nails at the top of a soil pile. He suddenly gasped, fell to the ground, and
appeared to lose consciousness. The employee then rolled down the soil pile and
struck a fence post with the bottom part of his body. Emergency services were
called, and the employee was transported to the hospital, where he was declared
dead later the same day due to a heart attack.
At 9:30 a.m. on July 17, 2024, an employee was cutting branches.  The branch
that the employee was tied off to broke, and the employee fell to the ground and
was killed.
On July 17, 2024, an employee was performing groundskeeping work, mowing greens
in the afternoon. At 3:15 p.m., the employee finished his work and entered a
coworker's car due to being delirious from the heat. The employee was found
unconscious at 5:00 p.m., removed from the car, and pronounced dead a few
minutes later when EMS arrived.
At 12:00 p.m. on July 17, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a roofing company, was
standing on a roof installing material. While bending over, the employee lost
balance and fell off the roof. The employee sustained a fatal head fracture upon
impact with the ground. Emergency services were called to the scene, but the
employee was pronounced dead at the location.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 15, 2024, an employee was operating a skidder to dump
debris to clear the ramp.  The employee was attempting to back up to retrieve
more debris. The employee was backing up the skidder, when he ran over a tree
limb with the left tire, causing the limb to spring up and penetrate the cab and
strike him in the head with enough blunt force to cause fatal results.
At 4:30 p.m. on April 9, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was leaning against a guardrail on the 3rd level balcony of an apartment
building. The guardrail failed, and the employee fell to the ground. The
employee sustained internal injuries, including fractured ribs and pelvis, as
well as lacerations to the spleen and pelvic vessels. Emergency services
transported the employee to the hospital, where he was admitted. Unfortunately,
the employee later died from his injuries on August 9, 2024. The direct impact
from striking the ground and metallic materials contributed to the fatal
injuries.
At 6:25 p.m. on July 15, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a masonry company, was
mixing buckets of masonry cement and handing them to workers on scaffolds. The
employee suddenly passed out and was immediately attended to by coworkers.
Despite efforts to revive the employee, the employee was pronounced dead at the
scene. The cause of death was determined to be a lack of climatization to the
heat, contributing to a heat-related illness.
At 2:42 p.m. on July 19, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a utility company, was
working to reconduct new conductor lines. The employee failed to use a rubber
insulated hose/cover on a nearby energized electrical conductor, which led to
electrocution. Emergency services responded to the scene, but the employee was
pronounced dead from the electrocution.
At 12:30 a.m. on July 12, 2024, an employee was reeling out a refueling hose and
nozzle from the end of the truck bed on a Ford F350 truck (serial number 22300)
to fill a tank of diesel on a refrigerated trailer. The employee parked his
truck in row 5 near the third trailer closest to the fence and then pulled the
hose approximately 25 feet from the end of the truck bed into the vehicle
traffic area. As the employee was pulling the refueling hose, a terminal tractor
driven by a coworker made a right-hand turn and struck the employee. The
coworker had just parked a trailer in row 4. The employee suffered fatal trauma
to the head and torso.
At 8:30 a.m. on July 13, 2024, an employee was walking to his work post after
returning from break. The employee suffered from hypertensive and
atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and complications.  The employee died
from natural causes.
At 12:00 a.m. on July 15, 2024, an employee was going into a trench to assess a
natural gas pipe.  The employee then exited the trench and turned white.  The
employee then collapsed.  The employee suffered a heart attack.  The employee
was in a work truck with A/C most of the morning, and the trench had
tents/plastic sheeting which had A/C flowing through the tented areas.
At 1:30 a.m. on July 2, 2024, an employee was attempting to break up a bar
fight. One of the patrons involved in the fight hit the employee in the head,
and the employee fell unconscious to the floor.  The employee was killed due to
the blunt impact to the head and neck with lacerations of vertebral arteries and
subdural hemorrhage.
At 1:00 p.m. on July 17, 2024, an employee was mowing grass, when the riding
lawn mower flipped over into a ditch and crushed the employee. The employee was
killed.
At 1:00 a.m. on July 9, 2024, an employee collapsed while performing managerial
duties.  The employee died.
At 2:35 p.m. on July 18, 2024, Employee #1, a newly hired drywall subcontractor
for Soltek Pacific Construction, was working at a multi-employer construction
site in Fresno, California. Employee #1 and his supervisor began their day at
7:00 a.m. with an orientation, after which they worked on the upper floor and
later moved to the lower floor for additional tasks. At approximately 1:30 p.m.,
Employee #1 informed the supervisor that he was feeling unwell and needed a
break. The supervisor directed Employee #1 to rest under a tree nearby. At 2:40
p.m., a coworker, a scaffolding subcontractor, found Employee #1 unresponsive
and gasping for air.   The coworker, trained in First Aid and CPR, initiated CPR
while the supervisor called for assistance. Paramedics arrived shortly
thereafter and took over CPR. Employee #1 was transported to a nearby hospital,
where he was pronounced dead. The cause of death was cardiac arrest, with
Employee #1 having a history of prior heart-related medical conditions.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 17, 2024, an employee had been feeling unwell and collapsed
in the vineyard. The employee died due to acute methamphetamine toxicity and
chronic illicit drug use.
At 7:15 p.m. on July 18, 2024, an employee was rigging crane weights to make a
stack. The crane weights became unstable and fell on the employee as he was bent
over. The employee was killed.
At 8:00 p.m. on July 12, 2024, an employee was attempting to add sodium
hypochlorite to a bulk supply container to recharge the swimming pool. The
employee added sodium hypochlorite to a container of sulfuric acid and was
overcome by vapors generated by the mixture. The employee was killed due to the
inhalation of chlorine gas vapor generated by the mixture.
At 10:39 a.m. on July 17, 2024, a full-time regular employee (Employee #1), a
heavy equipment operator, was grading a worksite using a dozer. During the
operation, the employee sustained fatal crushing injuries due to contact with
the dozer. Emergency responders were called to the scene, but the employee was
pronounced dead at the site. The incident is being investigated to determine the
exact cause of the crushing injuries.
Between 11:00 and 12:00 p.m. on July 18, 2024, Employee #1, a laborer, was
collecting garbage along the routine route. When Employee #1 got out of the
garbage truck to collect garbage from the side of the road, a gunman fired shots
at Employee #1. Employee #1 got back into the garbage truck to evade the gunman.
While Employee #1 was driving, s/he lost control of his/her vehicle and crashed
the garbage truck into a utility pole and palm tree.  The glass was shattered on
the driver's side of the garbage truck. There were also approximately two bullet
holes in the driver's door of the garbage truck. Employee #1 succumbed to
employee. Emergency services transported the employee to St. Francis Hospital,
where he was pronounced dead from blunt force trauma to the head.
At 11:00 a.m. on December 14, 2024, an employee was applying thermoplastic
polyolefin (TPO) roofing material near the edge of the roof. The employee stood
up and lost his balance falling off the roof to the ground level below. The
employee died from multiple fractures.
At 3:15 p.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee working for an electrical
contractor was working inside a commercial building installing wiring for
lighting fixtures. The employee was working from a ladder when he fell and
grabbed energized electrical wires trying to stop his fall. The employee died
from electrocution as a result.
At 2:20 p.m. on April 10, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was throwing old window screens into a dumpster at a worksite. While moving, the
employee tripped and struck his head against the concrete. The employee was
transported to a local hospital, where he was treated for head trauma.  The
employee died while at the hospital.   A second employee was also present but
was not injured.
At 3:14 p.m. on October 7, 2024, Employee #1, a mason worker, was using a
pressure washer to clean a masonry wall in a shaded area of the worksite. After
completing the task, he went to take a break and subsequently collapsed. A
coworker performed CPR, and emergency medical services were contacted. The
employee was transported to a hospital, where he later died.
At 2:54 p.m. on November 7, 2024, a supervisor and two employees were removing a
pipe valve and actuator from the third-story platform of a heat recovery steam
generator with the assistance of a crane contractor. As the crane lifted the
load, the signal person gave a hand signal that was interpreted by the crane
operator as a signal to boom down. The load was lowered onto the platform, at
which point the valve and actuator began to tip toward the supervisor. As he
turned to run out of the way, he tripped over a wooden block and fell over an
approximately 31-inch-tall guardrail. He fell about 18 feet to a second-story
metal platform below. Emergency medical services were contacted, and the
supervisor was pronounced dead at the scene. The cause of death was blunt force
trauma to the head, torso, and left lower extremity.
At 11:06 a.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee working as a construction
laborer for a roofing contractor was installing shingles on a decorative eye
brow roof. The employee was working from a height of 27 feet from a Werner
40-foot aluminum extension ladder.  A coworker (foreman) was standing at the
base of the ladder holding the ladder secure while the employee was working.
After working for approximately 30 minutes, the employee attempted to move the
extension ladder while still standing on the ladder. This caused the ladder to
shift unexpectedly causing the employee to lose his balance and fall. In the
process of falling, the employee initially landed on the front door overhang
causing the overhang to break free. The employee then fell to the concrete
driveway below. The employee died from multiple blunt trauma including fractures
and lacerations to his head and neck.
At 11:45 a.m. on June 12, 2024, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were backfilling a
trench 11 feet from the end of an active roadway. A vehicle drove through the
temporary traffic control devices that were diverting traffic onto a detour
route. The vehicle disregarded traffic control measures, increased speed, and
drove past a coworker (flagger) and signage. The vehicle continued through the
worksite, jumped the trench, and struck both employees. Employee #1 sustained
fatal injuries. Employee #2 was hospitalized to treat multiple injuries.
On December 9, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a power washing
service had soaked one barn and was getting ready to wash another barn. The
employee prepared the equipment in order to clean and wash the barn. He then
entered a barn that was being pumped out when he lost consciousness in the
corridor. The employee died from possible overexposure to chemical vapors from
the manure being disturbed during cleaning.
At 6:00 a.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee was working as a trash collector
for a waste collection and disposal service. The employee was emptying trash and
solid waste out of waste bins set outside residential homes into a garbage
truck. The coworker driving the truck drove the vehicle up a residential
driveway where the employee proceeded to collect the trash. The driver of
another motor vehicle failed to realize the garbage truck had been stopped and
ran into it pinning the employee between the two vehicles. The employee died
from crush injuries to his abdomen and lower legs.
At 2:44 p.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee was working as a laborer for a
third party contractor at an egg processing facility. The employee was working
with a crew tasked with loading chickens onto semi trailers for relocation from
the one farm to another. Once a trailer is full, the employee uses a truck to
relocate the trailer to the next location for offloading. At this time, a
different truck and trailer arrive to continue the loading process. When
trailers are being exchanged at the origin farm, the crew is permitted to take a
break to eat, drink, or use the restroom. At the time of a full trailer was
leaving and a new trailer arriving for loading, the employee began to walk
across the road to the restroom. As he was walking, the employee slipped or
tripped and fell beneath an empty trailer that was being positioned for loading.
The driver did not see the employee and ran over him with the trailer. The
employee was crushed from his hip area to his chest diagonally across his body
by the rear wheels. The employee died as a result of his injuries.
At 6:45 p.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee working as a laborer for a grain
wholesale supplier was opening lids on top of rail cars prior to loading. The
employee stepped from the catwalk onto the railcars while they were stationary.
He was standing on top of one of the railcars with a self-retracting lifeline
(SRL) hooked to his harness on one end and the anchor on the trolley on the
other. The employee instructed a coworker operating the locomotive to move East
to position the car under a spout. The trolley hit the spout and stopped it from
moving East horizontally. The employee was still standing on top when it was
moving and he continued travelling Eastward with the railcars. The lifeline in
his SRL began to pull out and when it reached the end causing the employee to be
dragged along the top of the railcars. The employee fell into a gap between the
railcars as he was being dragged. Initially, the employee hit a railcar from
behind and bounced back up onto the top of the railcars. But the second time,
the force of the impact with the railcar from behind was too much and it snapped
the lifeline. The employee fell between the railcars to the ground below
underneath the moving railcars. The employee died from multiple injuries
including trauma to his abdomen.
At 7:30 a.m. on December 11, 2024, an employee was working for a non-slaughter
meat manufacturing warehouse. The employee was a permanent employee of the
employer. A coworker, the plant operators manager, was her immediate supervisor.
The employee had climbed an exterior fixed ladder to the roof of the building
when she jumped off the roof. The employee died from blunt force trauma due to
suicide.
At 10:45 a.m. on December 13, 2024, an employee working as a purchasing manager
for a supermarket was providing directions to a coworker operating a 8FCU20
Toyota Forklift powered industrial vehicle (PIV). The employee was guiding the
PIV as they unloaded palletized walk-in freezer components from an enclosed
delivery truck. The coworker positioned the PIV forks under a palletized load of
wall panels which weighed approximately 3,000 pounds. The employee provided
manhole. The Faribault Fire Department responded to a report of a person down
and found the employee not breathing but with a strong pulse. High levels of
hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide were detected inside the manhole. It took
45 minutes to extricate the employee using the Fire Department's equipment. The
employee died enroute to the Life Flight helicopter due to overexposure to
hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide.
At 8:24 a.m. on October 5, 2024, Employee #1 was preparing a concrete mixture
and installing concrete blocks on the unfinished second story of a single-family
frame home under construction. The employee was riding on the forks of a bobcat
that was elevated approximately 10 feet above the ground. The employee fell from
the forks to the ground surface, sustaining a crushed chest and broken hips,
resulting in a fatality.
At 1:30 p.m. on September 26, 2024, Employee #1, employed at a job site, was
collecting trash and placing it into a trash bin when the employee suddenly
collapsed. A coworker notified management, and the onsite emergency medical
technician (EMT) arrived to assess the employee, who was unconscious,
unresponsive, and pulseless. The onsite EMT performed CPR and used an AED. The
employer called 911, and EMS paramedics took over but pronounced the employee
dead at the scene.
At 3:18 p.m. on October 2, 2024, Employee #1, employed as a shellfish fishing
diver near Sisters Island, was diving for Geoducks in an area experiencing
strong tides and rough seas. After starting his second dive of the day, Employee
#1 radioed the tender aboard the vessel to request to be brought back in.
Shortly after, he radioed the tender to stop bringing him in. At the same time,
the captain of the vessel, who was also diving, requested to be brought in. The
tender cleated Employee #1 off to the boat and began assisting the captain. Once
belt. The belt moved and caught his fingertip between the belt and a pulley,
resulting in an amputation of the employee's left index finger. The employee was
hospitalized to treat these injuries.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 15, 2022, an employee was MIG welding nipples onto the top
of a fuel tank truck.  The purpose of the nipples was to facilitate a steam
cleaning process for the tank, and the work was being performed in an indoor bay
of a building.  The employee was welding when the tank exploded, blowing the
employee through the building roof and a considerable vertical distance above
the building itself.  The employee was killed, sustaining blunt force trauma to
the head and torso from the explosion itself, the impact with the building roof
and landing on the ground outside the work bay entrance.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 4, 2022, an employee was removing structural supports from
a garage.  The building collapsed and fell on him. The employee broke his neck
and was killed when the entire roof of the garage being demolished unexpectedly
collapsed. A coworker was also injured. An engineering survey was not performed
by a competent person prior to allowing garage demolition operations to begin.
The walls and attic floor of the garage were not braced and the employee and
coworkers were allowed inside the garage, after the wall sheathing, iron pipe
supports and house connections had been removed or cut.
On June 14, 2022, an employee who worked as a Piperfitter was engaged in the
demolition of 36-inch pipe section. The valve pipe separted from the wall during
demolition of the pipe.  The employee was working on a crew with three coworkers
cutting the section of pipe. The goal was to lower the pipe to a metal cart
using rigging. The employee was attempting to secure the pipe to the cart when
an overhead valve pipe section fell onto the pipe. The falling section caused
the pipe to push forward and pin the employee between the pipe and another pipe.
The employer had failed to ensure the crew was clear of a load suspended aove
them by slings. The employee incurred head injuries and was killed.
At 1:30 p.m. on December 20, 2021, an employee was tasked with "tempering" a
steel assembly using an oxygen and acetylene torch to straighten areas deformed
due to welding stresses. The employee worked outdoors while heating an assembly
with the torch. Once the employee competed work on the first assembly, the
employee turned around and worked on a second assembly directly behind them.
While working on the second assembly, the employee got too close to the
previously heated assembly and the employee's clothes caught fire. The employee
received first aid at a nearby clinic for second degree burns to the torso and
hand but was then transferred to a hospital and admitted for further treatment.
At 11:30 a.m. on December 21, 2021, an employee moved rebar from a work truck to
their truck to drive it to the work site. While working, the work truck rolled
backwards and struck the employee, who received a right leg (femur) fracture.
The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 6:17 p.m. on May 25, 2022, an employee was lowering a JLG lift to the ground
in preparation for an impending lightning storm.  The lift was tipped over by
high winds, killing the employee.
At 4:45 a.m. on December 2, 2021, an employee, a maintenance worker, was
adjusting a machine that applies starch to paper. The machine had to be running
to perform the adjustment. While making the adjustment, the employee's hand was
pinched between two rollers causing a contusion to his hand.  The employee was
treated without hospitalization.
At 3:30 p.m. on June 9, 2022, an employee was driving a spreader to spread
fertilizer. The spreader malfunctioned and ran into a ditch, causing the
employee to hit the windshield of the spreader. The employee was killed,
sustaining fractures and lacerations to the face and neck.
At 5:40 p.m. on May 31, 2022, an employee was standing inside a moving mail
carrier box truck in a parking lot when the driver made a left turn. The
employee lost her balance, was slung out of the truck, and struck her head
against the ground. The employee died from her injuries.
At 9:15 a.m. on June 14, 2022, an employee was directing the driver of a dump
trailer.  The employee opened the gate and directed the dump trailer operator to
back up.  The employee was struck by the dump trailer door and impaled by the
protruding gate latches. The employee was killed by blunt force trauma.
At 2:15 p.m. on February 3, 2022, an employee was organizing a stack of sheet
metal.  While the employee was adjusting the stack, the separator fell, causing
the sheet metal to fall and crush his finger.  The employee sustained a finger
amputation and was treated without hospitalization.
An employee was working in a hospital as an orderly, moving patients around the
hospital, but wore a mask and ate alone at lunch. The employee was pregnant and
was off work at home when complications arose. The employee called her doctor
who said get to an emergency room to get checked.  At 8:15 a.m. on May 16, 2022,
the employee was admitted into the labor and delivery area of a different
hospital than her work for observation of a pulmonary embolism from a blot clot
in her leg traveling to her lungs. While in the hospital, the employee was
tested and it was discovered that she was positive for COVID-19. The employee's
husband had tested positive 3-4 weeks prior and was isolated at home for 9 days
in his own room. The employee and her children home-tested for COVID-19 after
her husband's illness but tested negative. The employee remained in the hospital
for three days, was sent home to isolate, and was released back to work 11 days
after the positive test.
At approximately 12:00 a.m. on February 14, 2022, an employee drove a golf cart.
The golf cart became stuck between security bollards. The employee was trying to
set it free by putting it in reverse with his left leg hanging outside the body
of the golf cart. The golf cart became free and suddenly moved, pinching the
employee's lower left leg against the bollard.  The employee sustained bruises,
including the supervisor, were around the area at the time so there was no
witness. The employee continued working until September 13, 2021. He then went
to the hospital, where he was admitted to treat a fractured right foot.
At 3:26 p.m. on September 2, 2021, an employee who had worked as a Licensed
Vocational Nurse (LVN) in a detention facility for a County Sheriff's Department
was hospitalized for treatment for COVID-19.  The employee worked as an (LVN)
performing medical care for inmates at a central jail downtown. Two workers at
the same location developed COVID-19 around the same timeframe as the employee,
but they worked in different areas of the facility as Deputy Sheriffs. The
employer did not have Adequate Aerosol Transmissible Diseases policies and
procedures in place.
At 1:13 p.m. on December 15, 2021, an employee was using a manual control to
walk tail stock into a plug used to help hold the part in place on a lathe. The
employee walked the stock in too far with his left hand between the plug and the
part. The tail stock made contact with the plug and pressured in place, striking
the employee's hand. The employee amputated his middle finger as a result,
requiring medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 4:30 p.m. on October 8, 2021, an employee was retrieving a set of totes on
rollers from the backroom to take to the floor of a clothing retail store. When
the employee turned left to take a step, her left foot caught the corner of the
rolling apparel rack causing her to trip and fall. The employee landed on her
left leg resulting in a fractured femur, and she was hospitalized.
At 07:15 a.m. on February 22, 2022, an employee was assisting a coworker with
cleaning dust on a machine. The employee grabbed a rotating chain and lifted it
off the surface of the machine while the machine was running. The employee
reached under the chain to wipe the surface clean. While reaching under the
chain, the employee's right pinky finger became caught in between the chain and
the rotating sprocket. The employee was treated for a fingertip amputation but
was not hospitalized.
At approximately 12:45 p.m. on February 10, 2022, an employee measured wood
pieces that were stored underneath the outfeed roller conveyor. The employee set
a wooden block on top of the conveyor activation control, which requires
continuous pressure to keep the outfeed roller conveyor running. The employee
measured wood pieces and then grabbed onto the underside of the conveyor to
stand up, and the employee's fingers were caught on the conveyor drive chain.
The employee sustained an amputation to the right index fingertip and middle
finger at the base of the nail. The employee was treated without
hospitalization.
At 3:30 p.m. on February 4, 2022, an employee was running a one and a half miles
followed by push-ups as part of a cadet training exercise.  After completing the
run, the employee was doing push-ups when she became incoherent and dizzy.
Emergency medical services was called, and the employee was transported to the
hospital for heat exhaustion and liver failure.  While hospitalized, she was in
a coma awaiting a liver transplant.
At 2:30 a.m. on March 5, 2022, an employee, a part owner of the bowling center,
was working alone after hours.  The employee was replacing a cracked bowling pin
rack frame on an AMF Bowling Pin Machine, Serial Number 3123500. While removing
the frame, the employee's body was positioned between the frame and the main
assembly. The machine's electrical plugs were connected and only the pit motor
switch was turned off.  The machine began to retract the bowling pin table and
frame, trapping the employee in between the frame and main assembly, killing him
ankle, and foot.
Employees were working for a family services provider when a COVID-19 outbreak
occurred. Ten employees were infected with COVID-19 but did not require
hospitalization for treatment of their infections.
At 9:15 a.m. on December 16, 2021, an employee was returning to her regular
office building after a meeting with coworkers from another building. The
employee worked as an Executive Secretary for a public school district and had
been delivering items to the other building. While walking on a pathway she had
to step on round cobblestones when her right ankle buckled underneath her. The
employee attempted to control her bodily motion but eventually fell onto her
rear end onto the parking lot. The employee reported that she raised her head to
check her feet and noticed her left foot was twisted outward. A coworker came to
her aid and called for help. The employee suffered a fracture to her right foot
and a compound fracture in three places on her left leg. The employee was
treated at a local hospital and released on the same day, but required surgery
on December 22, 2021.
At 10:31 a.m. on May 13, 2022, an employee was lowered into tanker truck to
perform cleaning operations with a pressure washer.  A piece of tobacco became
lodged into the employee's trachea and he began to choke and lost consciousness.
A coworker, the manager of the wash bay area, found the employee inside the
tank unconscious and called for assistance. After emergency personnel attempted
to resuscitate the employee, he was transported to a hospital where he was
pronounced dead.  The employee died from asphyxiation.
At 10:00 a.m. on May 13, 2022, an employee was removing rigging from catwalk
that had been loaded on a flatbed trailer.  The catwalk fell off the trailer and
struck the employee in the head.  The employee was hospitalized for a head
him through a walkway, located between Tank 304 and Tank 201. Within this
walkway was a row of trench plates that he had to cross. Earlier that day, rainy
weather had caused rainwater to accumulate directly over the trench plates.
Underneath the trench plates was a steam line. This steam line was heating up a
large tank to fulfill a customer request. Subsequently, the steam line was
completely submerged in the accumulated rainwater. The standing rainwater was 4
inches deep and had been heated to approximately 172 degrees Fahrenheit. The
employee was wearing rubber rain boots. As he walked through the standing
rainwater he slipped and fell backward into the water. The employee landed on
his hands, wrists, and forearms incurring 2nd and 2nd 1/2 degree burns. He also
incurred burns on his back. The employee was hospitalized until his release on
Sunday, December 26, 2022.
At 8:30 a.m. on February 15, 2022, an employee was performing an annual tank
inspection on a pressurized air tank mounted on a welding truck bed when,  while
dismounting the rear of the welding truck, her wedding ring got caught on an
extension cord bracket. The employee was not wearing hand protection during the
incident since the inspection equipment required tactical precision. The
employee suffered a fracture and degloving of her left ring finger requiring
inpatient hospitalization and surgery the following day. The employee's injured
finger eventually required amputation.
At 8:13 a.m. on June 11, 2022, Employee #1 was about to start weeding the
client's backyard. The employee collapsed and was non-responsive. According to
the coroner's report, the employee suffered cardiac arrest and was killed from
natural causes.
At 3:45 p.m. on June 17, 2022, three employees were hired to perform trenching
duties and install sewer pipes leading to a newly constructed apartment
building.  There were two trenches dug, and the second trench collapsed with two
of the three workers inside, leading to their deaths.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 22, 2022, Employee #1 was walking next to a moving tree
harvester. The employee fell to the ground and was run over by the tree
