At 4:30 p.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee was assembling a New Holland
Hayliner 275 Plus model bailer. The employee was laying under the bailer, which
was supported by two 3-ton jack stands, when the jack stands kicked out, causing
the bailer to fall on top of the employee.  The employee was killed due to
suffocation.
At 6:40 a.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee turned on and moved a
gasoline-fueled vehicle approximately 20 feet from under the vehicle lift to
near the overhead door within an unventilated workspace. The vehicle was going
to be delivered to the customer the following day. The employee was exposed to
hazardous levels of carbon monoxide, possibly from the vehicle while it was
running during moving. The employee was killed due to carbon monoxide poisoning
from vehicle exhaust.
shortness of breath and coughing. The employee was admitted on December 4, and
had a bronchoscopy on December 6. The employee's lungs continued to deteriorate
and he died on December 9, 2022, from respiratory failure due to the smoke and
chemical fume inhalation.
At 4:20 p.m. on December 8, 2022, an employee was performing clean-up duties at
the end of the day in the parking lot and work area where he and his crew were
performing trenching work at a construction site. The foreman was moving a pile
of dirt to a dump truck using a Caterpillar CAT 440 Backhoe when he struck, ran
over, and then backed over the employee. The site foreman did not see the
employee prior to running into him because he was not looking in the direction
he was traveling and was looking toward the dump truck and the other crew
members. The employee died due to his injuries.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 31, 2022, Employee #1 and Coworker #1 were wrapping 12
large boxes weighing 70 pounds each on a loading dock. Coworker #2 was holding
the stack with a clam attachment lift truck. Coworker #1 was holding the stack
on the other end. Coworker #2 pulled away. Employee #1 continued wrapping the
stack. When Employee #1 passed around to the other side, Coworker #1 lost
control of the stack, and the boxes fell over, striking Employee #1 on the right
shoulder, knocking Employee #1 to the ground. Employee #1 suffered head trauma
and passed away on November 7, 2022.
At 8:45 a.m. on November 3, 2022, an employee was cleaning the roof and roof
drains at a shopping center. The employee's employer provides cleaning and
maintenance services for the shopping center. Cleaning the roof and drains was
planned as an annual task, but often conducted less frequently. The employee and
two coworkers accessed the roof using a fixed ladder. Coworker #1 instructed and
directed the employee and Coworker #2 to climb over a parapet wall which was the
only means of ready access the drain on the southern portion of the roof.  The
wall measured 56.5 inches in height and was sloped on the north side by
approximately 32 degrees. Coworker #2 successfully climbed over the wall to the
southern portion.  When the employee attempted to climb over the wall, he lost
his footing and fell through the unguarded skylight immediately adjacent to the
wall.  The employee received medical treatment for fractures and contusions to
the back, chest and wrists.  While undergoing continued rehabilitation treatment
on December 5, 2022, the employee suffered a medical emergency and was
hospitalized. The employed died at the hospital on December 10, 2022.
At 10:00 a.m. on December 10, 2022, an employee was drilling and installing rock
anchors on a near vertical cliff along side a road approximately 45 feet in the
air in a man-basket with a drill attachment. While drilling, the employee
noticed a shift of the rock above him. The employee called down to his
supervisor on the ground and told him what he saw. The employee's supervisor
told him to shut down the drill and get out of there. As soon as the employee
shut down the drill, the rocks above him gave way and landed on top of him,
crushing him to death.
At 1:00 p.m. on December 12, 2022, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were sitting
inside a six-foot deep trench working on damaged fiber optic cable. The crew
began working in the trench around 10:30 a.m. Employee #1 and Employee #2 were
sitting inside the trench with their legs crossed, locating damaged fiber optic
lines. Employee #3 was in the trench handing tools back and forth to Employee #4
outside the trench. The employees had been working in the trench for
approximately three hours when the trench caved in the first time at
approximately 1:00 p.m. A second cave-in occurred approximately five minutes
later. Employee #1 was killed due to asphyxiation and crushed ribs. Employee #2
was hospitalized for his injuries. Employee #3 escaped with minor injuries that
did not require hospitalization.
At 5:00 p.m. on December 12, 2022, two employees were working in a trench
excavation during a sewer line construction project in the front yard of a
single family residential structure. Employee #1 and Employee #2, a co-owner of
the company, were in the trench at a depth of approximately 7 feet attempting to
fix a water line damaged during excavating operations. The employees were
working at the bottom of the trench without cave-in protection when the cave-in
occurred. Employee #2 was crushed by the soil and killed. Employee #1 was able
to escape physically unharmed from the trench cave-in.
At 10:58 p.m. on December 13, 2022, an employee was working in the shrink wrap
area of a warehouse and had finished wrapping a pallet. He was crushed between a
pole and the center rider and subsequently died from his injuries.
At 12:00 a.m. on November 15, 2022, an employee was preparing a John Deere X734
lawn tractor to perform grounds work at a church. The employee was a property
supervisor for the church.  At approximately 11:30 a.m., the employee went to
the equipment shed to mount a rotary broom on the gasoline powered lawn tractor.
The employee was working alone, and was found dead at 3:26 p.m. in the shed with
both the personnel and garage door closed. At the time the employee was found,
the rotary broom was partially attached to the lawn mower and the outside
temperature was 30-31 degrees Fahrenheit. The fire department measured a carbon
monoxide concentration of 354 ppm in the shed, and determined that the gas tank
on the lawnmower was empty.  Although other gas powered equipment was stored in
the shed, it did not appear to have been operated the day of the incident. The
employee's cause of death was determined to be carbon monoxide toxicity, as the
autopsy report indicated a 62 percent carboxyhemoglobin blood level.
At 2:30 p.m. on December 7, 2022, an employee was hauling limestone with a dump
truck from a rock quarry to a stock pile at a maintenance garage. The employee
dumped the rock at the garage and was cleaning out the remaining rock to prepare
the truck for an upcoming storm so that it could be used to spread salt and
sand. The employee's arm became caught in the truck's cross auger, and he was
pulled into the tailgate spreader. The employee died due to his injuries.
At 10:00 a.m. on December 14, 2022, an employee was riding on the back of a
garbage truck collecting recycling from homes when he leaned back to activate
the hydraulic handles and hit a telephone pole as the truck was passing it. The
contractor was installing roofing material. The employee received a load from
the crane when the crane was overextended and tipped over, striking the
employee. The employee sustained severe head trauma and died.
At 5:30 p.m. on January 11, 2023, an employee was welding a roofing membrane on
a flat roof when he fell approximately 45 feet to concrete ground below.
Employee was wearing a fall protection harness but it was not connected to a
lifeline. Employee was pronounced dead at the scene.
On March 6, 2023, an employee working as a laborer for a construction contractor
was screwing in a track above his head on the 7th floor ledge of a multifamily
residential building. The employee fell off the ledge to the 1st floor covered
garage below. The employee died from multiple fractures.
At 4:00 p.m. on March 4, 2023, an employee was pulling dead trees out of a
field, working alone. He was found unconscious between the tractor's rear tire
and a tree.  The coworker who found the employee stated that it was raining, and
the tractor was on a gradient of 15 degrees, but that when he went into the
tractor to move it away from body, the brakes were set. The employee was killed
due to traumatic asphyxia.
At 10:15 a.m. on March 6, 2023, an employee was climbing on top of a forklift
and down in between the mast and cab of the forklift. The employee struck the
control levers with his body, which activated the forklift mast to move towards
the cab, and the employee was caught in between the mast and cab.  The employee
was killed.
At 11:09 a.m. on March 6, 2023, Employee 1 was in the process of  manually
trimming a tree. Employee 1 cut a branch with a handsaw, approximately 16 feet
in length by 1 inch in diameter, and received an electrical shock from the
direct contact with a primary electrical line (12.5kV).  The employee was killed
when electrocuted.
At 11:20 p.m. on March 5, 2023, an employee was walking the parking garages,
performing his duties of cleaning the garage, identifying maintenance issues,
taking out the garbage, and addressing loitering within the parking garage. Two
individuals from the local neighborhood watch organizations encountered a person
loitering within the parking garage and contacted the employee. The employee
asked the person loitering to move on and leave the parking garage. The
individual did not comply, and the employee called 911. As the employee called
911, the individual pulled a firearm and shot the employee, and then fled the
scene. The employee was fatally wounded by a gunshot wound.
At 8:15 a.m. on March 3, 2023, an employee working as a construction laborer for
a county roads department was flagging traffic. The employee was struck by the
brush guard of an oncoming vehicle and pinned to the tailgate of road work
vehicle. The employee was crushed between the vehicles and died.
At 12:00 a.m. on February 5, 2023, a roofing contractor employee fell
approximately 20 feet to a concrete floor when he walked backwards onto a
skylight and went through it.  He was airlifted to the hospital, but died about
5 hours after the fall.
On February 11, 2023, an employee working as a front desk clerk for a hotel was
shot by a hotel guest. The employee died as a result of the shooting.
At 12:50 p.m. on March 7, 2023, five employees were demolishing a brick wall
employee was killed due to head injuries.
At 1:30 a.m. on October 8, 2022, an employee was performing GPS mapping to shoot
specific points along a highway lane that crews were paving. The driver of a
White Ford F-150 Pickup Truck clipped two center line traffic cones, swerved and
struck the employee who was standing in the closed lane. The employee was killed
due to being severed in half at or just above the hips.
At 8:00 a.m. on August 11, 2022, an employee was working at the New York
Metropolitan Transit Authority's Mosholu train yard. The employee was a train
operator who was boarding a train to place it into service. The employee fell
down for an unknown reason and was found unresponsive by a coworker. The
employee died from a suspected medical episode. No one witnessed the incident,
and no information is available as to the nature of the condition.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 11, 2022, an employee who was in training and Coworker
#1 (employee trainer) were sitting inside the cabin of a CAT Caterpillar 740
Off-Highway Truck (Unit 285) at the bottom part of the hill. They were waiting
for Coworker #2, who driving a CAT 740E Truck (Unit 366), to finish dumping dirt
on the other side of the hill. Coworker #2 was working at a 12-degree angle as
he dumped the dirt from the truck. When Coworker #2 maneuvered his truck to the
top of the hill he lost power. Coworker #2 had no control and could not stop the
truck causing it to roll backwards until it hit the other vehicle. Coworker #1
panicked and got out of the vehicle on the left side. The site believes that
when the vehicles collided, the employee was run over by the truck. EMS was
called and an ambulance arrived on site, The employee opened his eyes as he was
carried out on a gurney, but he was pronounced dead at the hospital. The Deputy
Coroner reported that the cause of death was traumatic crushing injures due to
partial ejection from vehicle after collisions between construction equipment
and motor vehicles.
At 3:30 a.m. on October 13, 2022, an employee sat in a chair after experiencing
chest pain. The employee suffered a massive heart attack due to preexisting
cardio/pulmonary conditions.
At 1:20 p.m. on October 7, 2022, a library employee was found unresponsive at
her desk due to a cardiac event.
At 2:00 p.m. on October 13, 2022, an employee was standing on a ladder when he
removed a ceiling tile to replace a bulb ina light fixture. As the employee
attempted to complete his task, he was electrocuted and died.
At 9:30 a.m. on October 13, 2022, an employee was standing on top of soybeans
while wrapping a chain around the grappling arm of the saw. The grappling arm
had a hydraulic failure which caused the left side claws to close crushing the
employee between the claw arms of the saw. The employee died due to his
injuries.
At 10:15 a.m. on December 9, 2022, an employee was repairing overheard power
lines and was electrocuted.
At 10:30 a.m. on December 23, 2022, an employee was working from the top of a
Zimmerman mixer truck at a silo station when the truck began to pull out of the
station. The employee fell approximately 11 feet to the concrete surface below.
The employee died due to internal injuries.
At 4:30 p.m. on January 1, 2023, an employee was checking out customers at a
cash register when another customer approached her from behind with a machete
and  struck her multiple times. The employee died from her wounds on the scene.
An employee was working as an operations supervisor in an ambulatory care
facility when she tested positive for COVID-19 on June 29, 2022, then
hospitalized on July 4, 2022, for treatment of her infection.
At 2:45 p.m. on December 27, 2022, an employee was in a trench installing
underground plumbing conduit when the trench walls collapsed and he was engulfed
by soil. The employee died due to asphyxiation.
At 5:15 p.m. on December 30, 2022, an employee ended her shift, left the
building and was approaching her car in the hospital parking lot when an
attacker, an ex-boyfriend, ambushed her and shot her. The employee was shot
multiple times in the chest and head, resulting in death. The attacker later
killed himself while driving after the attack.
At 12:00 a.m. on August 7, 2022, an employee was operating a harvester machine
that tops tobacco plants. When the machine became jammed with tobacco leaves,
the employee exited the harvester to clear the jam. The employee was tangled in
the belt and pulled up into the harvester machine. The employee was killed by
pinch point injuries to the neck.
At 12:00 noon on December 1, 2022, an employee, the sole owner and employee of
the cabinet company, was trying to pull a hardwood cherry board off a rack that
was over his head in his woodworking shop. As the employee removed the board, it
struck him in the head. The employee tried to walk back to his adjoining office
and bathroom in the building that housed his woodworking shop. The office and
bathroom were approximately 20 feet away from the lumber rack where the employee
was initially injured. When the employee made it to the bathroom to tend to
himself for the initial laceration, he fell and hit his head on the concrete
floor in the doorway between the bathroom and his desk in the office. The
employee was found unresponsive by his wife.  She called for emergency services
but he was pronounced dead at the scene.
At 12:50 p.m. on August 26, 2022, Employee #1 was driving a pickup truck on a
highway and Employee #2 was riding in the passenger seat.  Both employees worked
for a landscaping service. The employees were involved in a single vehicle crash
when the vehicle driven by Employee #1 went into a ditch, through a fence,
exited the roadway, and collided with a tree. The pickup truck was heavily
damaged in the crash, and emergency personnel responded to the scene of the
accident. Both employees sustained blunt force trauma injuries. Employee #1 was
killed at the scene of the accident, and Employee #2 was transported to the
hospital and admitted.  Alcohol was suspected to be a factor in the crash.
At 12:50 p.m. on November 9, 2022, an employee was working on a construction
project when he was caught between the boom and the outriggers of a backhoe. The
employee was crushed and killed.
At 10:56 p.m. on October 11, 2022, an employee and two coworkers were working on
a state route installing road signs. Traffic warning cones and a construction
vehicle were used to close all lanes of the route directing traffic onto an exit
ramp. A motorist drove into the work zone, running over multiple traffic cones
and struck the employee and the jersey wall barrier. The vehicle then spun
around and struck another motorist traveling on the exit ramp. The employee
suffered fatal injuries.
At 11:00 a.m. on December 30, 2022, Employee #1 was putting air into the tire of
a military truck that was mounted on a multi-piece rim. When the tire pressure
got to 85 psi, the top part of the multi-piece rim flew off and struck Employee
#1 and Employee #2 who was walking by at the time. Employee #1 was pronounced
dead at the scene due to blunt force trauma. Employee #2 was hospitalized to
treat three broken bones on both hands.
At 3:15 p.m. on January 1, 2023, an employee, a migrant farm worker, was placing
wooden stakes in the ground to support bell pepper plants at a farm. The
employee was on his first day on the job and he was struggling to keep pace with
more experienced farmworkers. The employee complained of fatigue and leg pain as
the area's heat index neared 90 degrees. Sometime later, coworkers found the
employee unresponsive in a shallow drainage ditch. The employee died due to
symptoms related to heat illness.
At 10:45 a.m. on January 2, 2023, an employee was riding a ski lift when a tree
fell onto the lift cable and bounced him out of the lift chair and onto the
ground approximately 30 feet below. The employee died due to blunt force trauma
injuries.
At 11:30 a.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee was crawling over a liftgate when
a tenant called for the freight elevator. The employee was crushed by the
freight elevator and died.
At 10:5 p.m. on December 31, 2022, an employee was clocking in at the time clock
when she turned and tripped and fell and suffered an arm injury. The employee
was transported to a local medical center via ambulance at her request. The
employee died on January 3, 2023, at the medical center.
At 7:00 p.m. on December 19, 2022, an employee, a semi-truck driver, was stopped
on the northbound shoulder of a highway and attempted to cross five lanes of
traffic for an unknown reason. The employee was struck and killed in the right
lane of southbound traffic by a passenger vehicle.
At 7:30 a.m. on July 13, 2022, an employee was working installing insulation,
when he fell approximately 34 feet to a compacted rock floor.  The employee was
killed.
At 9:20 p.m. on May 25, 2022, an employee was either climbing a ladder or
getting on the roof.  The employee fell from the ladder or the roof,   directly
onto a steel stake.  The employee was killed due to impalement.
At 12:30 p.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee and two coworkers were installing
sewer pipe in a 6-foot, 7-inch trench. The employee and a coworker were working
inside a steel trench box connecting the pipe. When the pipe was installed,
another coworker, the excavator operator, covered the pipe with fine aggregate
material, dumped 2-3 loads of stone, and then used the back of the bucket to
smooth the material. The coworker facing the excavator with his back against the
spreader bars was using hand signals to inform the excavator operator when to
stop moving the bucket forward. While the coworker was giving the forward
signal, the excavator operator continued to move the machine's bucket towards
heat-related incident.
At 6:30 a.m. on August 10, 2023, an employee, the owner of the company, was
working alone and was offloading a Komastu PC228USLC - 8 excavator from a
Trailboss trailer at a storage yard. After offloading the excavator, the
employee was raising the ramps of the trailer into the travel position using
chains connected to the bucket of the excavator. The employee exited the
excavator to secure the ramps in the travel position.   The chains connected to
the ramps became dislodged causing them to fall and fatally crush him.
At 8:15 a.m. on August 9, 2023, an employee was on the ground guiding an
excavator operator when it came into contact with a 1247 kV overhead power line.
The current from the power line passed through the employee to the ground, and
he was electrocuted.
At 10:45 a.m. on August 10, 2023, two employees were within a trench box,
arranging the workspace to commence the installation of sewer lines when the
surrounding dirt collapsed and buried them under the debris. Employee #1 was
killed and was found submerged face down in the water and his back was covered
by dirt.  Employee #2 managed to avoid complete submersion but suffered numerous
injuries to his shoulder, pelvis, and legs.  Employee #2 was hospitalized for
treatment.
At 9:27 a.m. on August 10, 2023, an employee, a subcontractor, was replacing
elevated light fixtures on the exterior of a rental equipment repair facility.
The employee was using a JLG 340AJ Mobile Elevating Work Platform to access the
fixtures and was maneuvering the lift around the southwest corner of the
building. The employee was facing the base of the lift with his back to the
direction of travel. The boom of the lift was raised so that the floor of the
basket was approximately 23 feet above the ground. As the employee moved, he
came in contact with a 12kv overhead electrical power line that was
approximately 28 feet above the ground. The employee was fatally electrocuted
when electricity from the power line passed through his body and the lift to the
ground. Workers of the rental equipment repair facility responded and
extinguished the fire that had started on the lift and were able to lower the
basket the ground. The branch manager contacted emergency services. Police and
fire units responded and the employee was pronounced dead at the scene.
At 12:00 midnight on August 8, 2023, an employee, the crew leader, and his crew
were installing new power poles when, while attempting to reconnect the line, he
made contact with a live wire and was electrocuted.
At 12:00 noon on August 9, 2023, an employee was cleaning a moving conveyor with
a hand scraper when his hand became caught in the rollers of the conveyor and
his right arm and shoulder were crushed in the machine. The employee was
pronounced dead at the scene.
At approximately 8:13 a.m. on May 26, 2023, an employee and a coworker were
tasked with trimming and removing some oak trees in a resident's backyard. The
employee got into the bucket on the company bucket truck without a body harness
and began cutting an oak tree closest to the fence line. The employee was
operating the bucket from the control panel inside the bucket. The employee hit
a fork in the tree limbs and tried to maneuver the bucket around the fork. The
bucket scraped one tree limb and then dropped suddenly. The bucket then sprang
back up suddenly ejecting the employee from the bucket. The employee fell
approximately 40 to 45 feet and landed on his head approximately 3 to 4 feet
from the base of the tree. The employee died from head trauma at the scene.
At 4:00 p.m. on July 14, 2023, a maintenance worker was found dead in a tool
storage shed by a coworker.  The use of narcotics had been indicated as the
cause of death.  The employee died of an overdose.
At 7:30 a.m. on July 20, 2023, a homeowner asked an employee for assistance in
guiding a vehicle. While the employee was guiding the homeowner, the homeowner
accidentally pressed on the gas instead of the brake, pinning the employee
against a tree. The employee was initially hospitalized and later pronounced
dead on July 21, 2023.
At 1:22 p.m. on August 10, 2023, Employee #1 and four coworkers, including
Employee #2, were pulling on a rope while another coworker, the chainsaw
operator, was cutting a pine tree that was about 70-feet tall and 14-inches wide
to make it fall away from a residential home. The workers pulling on the rope
were in the drop zone of the tree and as the tree started to fall, they
scattered into a bushed area. Two employees were not able to get out from drop
zone in time and were struck-by branches of the tree. Employee #1 received fatal
blunt force injuries to the head and torso. Employee #2 was admitted into the
hospital to treat a fractured left hand and a concussion.
At 11:21 a.m. on August 9, 2023, an employee, the company owner, was applying
grass seed around the exterior of cul-de-sac while following to the right rear
of a hydroseeding truck.  The employee's best friend of 40-plus years was
operating the truck and they were finishing up and he was getting ready to back
up the truck. The employee usually walked back and forth on both sides of the
truck to give the friend a signal. The operator was moving forward approximately
3-5 mph when he lost contact with the employee. The operator immediately
stopped, put the truck in park and got out to look for the employee.  The
operator found the employee lying on the ground where he had been crushed by the
truck wheels.  The employee was lying on top of the hose with the hose between
his legs. The employee died due to crushing injuries.
At 10:30 a.m. on August 7, 2023, an employee was operating a XL Tire Hand Boom
Truck performing tire demounting on a hoist lift truck. The employee was
watching a coworker change a multi-piece, 6-foot Michelin 18.00 R25 industrial
tire on the hoist lift truck when the coworker climbed inside the tire hand boom
truck tire manipulator claw to help manipulate the tire and it exploded. The
employee was struck by tire debris and suffered chest trauma and died.
At 2:15 p.m. on June 29, 2023, an employee was found in the portable toilet,
unresponsive.  The employee died due to a suspected drug overdose.
At 5:30 a.m. on August 8, 2023, an employee was making repairs to the bend gates
of a blow molding machine and welding a metal plate onto the sand bin door. A
coworker was assisting by using a chain hoist to lower a bucket with equipment
and the tools down to the employee. The employee instructed the coworker to plug
in the air hose which caused the bend doors to close on his neck. The coworker
ran down and saw the bend gates had closed on the employee's neck and ran to get
help. The employee suffered lacerations and blunt force trauma to his head,
neck, left ear, and right jaw and subsequently died due to his injuries.
At 11:15 a.m. on August 7, 2023, an employee was eating lunch on a break when an
employee from another work area came through the back door and kitchen, into the
dining area and stabbed the employee to death with a knife.
At 9:00 a.m. on August 8, 2023, an employee was walking behind a cart pulled by
a tractor laying out sugar cane on the ground for planting in rows in an open
field. The employee reported he was not feeling well and shortly thereafter
passed out. The employee died due to hyperthermia.
At 1:30 a.m. on August 5, 2023, an employee was operating a Crown TR4500-250
electric tug to line up empty baggage carts in the storage area located in the
back of the warehouse. The electric tug had an open front from the waist up
where the employee was standing while operating. As the employee drove into the
open side of an empty cargo plastic container box, the top frame of the box
pinned the employee to the back side of the tug and caused a traumatic
asphyxiation. The employee was killed.
At 2:20 p.m. on June 27, 2023, an employee was using a combination ladder to
conduct repairs on the chimney of a dwelling. The employee was stepping off of
the combination ladder toward the eave of the roof when the ladder became
unbalanced. The employee and the ladder fell approximately 25 feet to the
ground. The employee was pronounced dead.
At 9:09 a.m. on August 2, 2023, an employee, a roofer, was laying sheet decking
on the roof of a new commercial structure when he fell with a decking sheet 50
feet onto a concrete floor. The employee died due to traumatic injuries.
At 6:16 a.m. on August 10, 2023, an employee was found dead in a temporary
construction trailer. The prior day, the employee remained on site as coworkers
left for the day in order to work on engineered plan drawings. The employee had
spent the week taking measurements indoors and designing plans for the final
pipe installation. The employee had a pre-existing heart condition and his heart
functioned at only 14% efficiency.
At 12:00 noon on August 3, 2023, an employee, a roofer, was performing repairs
for a regional hospital was assigned to watch a patient inside an isolated
patient room for approximately two twelve-hour shifts. The patient was positive
for COVID-19. The employee wore an N95-mask, gown and gloves. The employee
should have also worn eye protection but did not since there was none available
in the caddy outside the door. The employee did not ask the employer for any eye
protection. It is highly suspected that the employee contracted the COVID-19
virus from the patient. In addition, the employee had pre-existing health
conditions such as but not limited to cellulitis and was known to have sepsis.
The employee contracted COVID-19 and was hospitalized.
At 7:00 a.m. on October 10, 2023, an employee was driving a New Holland TB 120
tractor, towing two flatbed trailers with bins of brussel sprouts, down an
inclined dirt road. At 7:43 a.m., the employee was found on the ground next to a
heart disease, i.e., not work-related.
At 9:33 a.m. on October 11, 2022, Employee #1 was scanning boxes while they were
being unloaded onto a loading dock from a truck. Employee #1 was scanning boxes
being unloaded from a truck onto a flexible conveyer. Employee #1 walked to the
truck and flexible conveyor in the dock area, and, while pushing a box onto the
flexible conveyor, her right foot fell through a gap between the dock and truck.
Employee #1 pulled herself up and continued working. Employee #1 notified her
employer of the the accident and ankle injury on the same day after completing
her shift and stated she would be visiting an urgent care. On June 27, 2023 the
Division was notified by the Kern County Coroner's Office of a death involving
Employee #1, who died on March 16, 2023 at the hospital after undergoing
elective surgery. Employee #1 sustained a spinal fracture.
At 9:17 a.m. on June 23, 2023, an employee was using a guide rope to help
maneuver/hold in position a prefab concrete slab, as the slab was being lifted
off of a semi-truck trailer. The pivot point pin at the boom hinge where the
boom is attached to the crane broke on one side. Further inspection revealed the
bolts and keeper plate were unattached and found in the bottom of the boom. The
employee was hit by the falling extended boom and killed.
At 3:40 p.m. on June 27, 2023, Employee #1 was retrieving a water hose to place
in the back of the pick-up truck. Employee #1 was struck by the pick-up truck

pinched and lacerated by the crimping portion of the machine.  The  employee was

At 5:00 p.m. on August 7, 2022, an employee was sweeping the stairs on a cargo
ship when he slipped and fell into the cargo hold. The employee was found dead
at the bottom of the cargo hold.

County Employment and Human Services Department was hospitalized with COVID-19.

been hospitalized and was in the intensive care unit (ICU). The employer called
the employee's spouse to check on her status on March 11, 2022, and was told

At 6:30 p.m. on February 21, 2022, an employee was working as a driver/ground

walker was loaded onto a Braun mobility lift. The employee engaged the lift to

At 10:15 p.m. on September 26, 2022, an employee was working as a flagger on a
public road construction jobsite where employees were working in a trench, dug
across a road, installing gas line service to a residence. The construction zone

contractor.  Employee #1 was installing roofing insulation and metal sheeting

Employee #1 suffered a fatality due to multiple blunt force traumas including

At 1:47 p.m. on December 14, 2023, an employee working as a farm laborer for a
farm labor contract staffing company was working at an agricultural field
(temporary place of employment). The employee was working with a crew engaged in
peach tree pruning activities from mobile elevated work platforms. While working
in the field, the employee suddenly became ill and experienced a possible
stroke. The outdoor temperature on the day and time of the incident was

feller and assisting the tree feller with packing jacks. The tree feller was
using jacks to fell a seven-foot-wide, 200-foot-tall redwood tree uphill. The

ran to safety, and the employee ran to the tree to get the jack. The employee

Coworker #4 went to his vehicle, grabbed a firearm and started shooting towards
the employee, which caused the group to start to disperse. The employee was hit

hours when he told Coworker #1 (immediate supervisor) that he was feeling ill

Coworker #5, the employee's relative (brother-in-law), that were on their way to

Coworker #5 and the other coworkers approached and knocked on the employee's car

instructions to break the car window. Once they could get into the car, Coworker

On Monday, May 22, 2023, an employee working for a freight transportation
company was dropped off at a stone distribution facility at a different
location. When a coworker (owner) did not hear from him and couldn't contact
him, he reported the situation to the police department. The police called back
to tell the coworker the employee was found dead slumped over the wheel of his
vehicle. Later, the coroner contacted the coworker at 5:07 p.m. on May 23, 2023,
to report the employee died of natural causes.
At 10:00 a.m. on March 1, 2023, an employee working as a fire fighter for a city
fire department was performing firefighting duties on an interior structural
fire. The crew had responded to a 4-alarm fire and the employee was assigned the

became unaccounted for, and rescue attempts were hampered by a fully involved
fire and partial building collapse.  Some hours later, the employee was located

At 11:15 a.m. on November 23, 2022, an employee who worked for a City streets
and sanitation department was walking in the middle of a street behind a
payloader. The payloader was working on removing snow and had just begun to back
up when its bumper struck the employee in the back.  The employee fell face

struck and rolled over him. The employee's head and upper body were crushed,
killing him.
At 5:45 p.m. on May 26, 2023, an employee was working as a material handler at a
distribution warehouse handling goods for transport in the Put-to-light
department. The employer temporarily stores goods until they are transported to
stores. The employee's immediate supervisor was the Assistant General Manager.
The employee had returned from a break approximately 10 minutes before
experiencing a medical emergency. The employer contacted emergency services and
immediately began performing chest compressions as instructed by the dispatcher.
Emergency personnel arrived within 10 minutes. The employee was transported to
the hospital, where he died in the emergency room due to cardiac arrest, which
was not work related.
At 11:19 a.m. on May 19, 2023, an employee working for a tree care service
trimming branches while suspended in a saddle on the tree. The employee was
using a 21-foot aluminum pole saw to cut the branches. The employee's main tools
and equipment for this task included the saddle, which is a harness-like device
worn around the waist, and pole saw, which is a long pruning tool with a saw
blade at the end. The employee was cutting the branches away from overhead
powerlines. He was positioned on a branch approximately 10 feet above the ground
with the pole saw fully extended. While cutting he was holding the saw at the
center of its base when the back end of the tool made contact with the
powerlines. As a result, the employee was electrocuted with a 7,200-volt line.
The employee died after being admitted to the hospital following electrocution
and a brain injury.
At 7:00 p.m. on May 25, 2023, an employee working as a truck driver for a
wholesale supplier was getting ready to load a truck. The employee fell
approximately four feet from the ledge of the dock area to the concrete floor
below sustaining a skull fracture and intracerebral bleeding. The employee died
as a result of his injuries two days later.
At 10:15 a.m. on May 27, 2023, an employee working at a waste handling transfer
facility had just emptied a dumpster load. The employee stepped out of the
garbage truck to secure the dumpster doors before leaving the facility. A Doosan
Model DL300 articulated wheeled front end loader was backing up and struck the
employee. The employee broke his spine and multiple ribs and sustained internal
injuries including punctured organs. The employee was transported to the
hospital, where he died.
At 10:00 a.m. on May 20, 2023, an employee was troubleshooting internet service
at a residential site. The employee's vehicle was parked on the shoulder of a
residential street, under the telephone lines with an extension ladder hanging
over the lines, approximately 18-feet above the ground. This location,
identified as the mainline, is connected by a cable that stretched across the
street and connected to the ted to the customer's house. The placement of the
ladder is critical to the safety of the employee, as the correct position for
hanging the ladder on the mainline should be facing the service home. However, a
4-5 foot snowbank was blocking ladder access, and the employee placed the ladder
in the opposite direction facing away from the house. While the employee was on
the ladder, the cable separated from the mainline, causing the ladder to fling
backwards.  The employee was catapulted on the street, more than 15 feet away.
The employee sustained blunt force head trauma.  Emergency responders arrived,
treated, and transported him via air flight but he died on the way to the
hospital.
At 11:30 a.m. on May 23, 2023, an employee working as a security guard for a
security service was walking to his personal vehicle when he collapsed. The
employee died from unknown causes.
At 9:00 a.m. on May 28, 2023, an employee was unloading materials from a box
attached to a forklift. The employee entered the box to gather materials and the
box fell approximately 20 feet from the forklift to the ground. The employee
fractured his skull and was killed.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 30, 2023, an employee who owned the company, was operating
a bulldozer to flatten sand at a beach construction site.  The employee was
identified heading into the water by the owner. The employee became trapped in
the bulldozer underwater and was found 30 feet from the shore and 40 feet under
the water's surface. The employee was killed due to drowning.
At 10:00 a.m. on May 30, 2023, an employee and a coworker working for a cattle
flat hose used for water transfer during fracking operations. While rolling up
the hose, it swung behind the skid steer, broke the window, and the metal head
attached to the hose end struck the employee in the head. The employee was
killed by severe head trauma.
At 11:00 a.m. on April 10, 2023, Employee #1 was performing maintenance on the
refrigerant lines of a Carrier 30 GN/GT Liquid Chiller used for air conditioning
an airport terminal. Employee #1 was removing the Electronic Expansion Valve
(EEV) from the hot gas bypass line. The line contained R-22 refrigerant and
compressor lubricating oil at a pressure of approximately 100 pounds per square
inch.  A coworker was summoned to assist in the process of separating the pipe
joint.  The coworker placed a set of pliers on the pipe joint, as Employee #1
applied heat with an acetylene torch. As the pipe joint heated, the brazing
material melted, and the joint was separated by the coworker with pliers. The
pipe joint opened to the atmosphere, causing a pressure release of R-22
refrigerant and compressor lubricating oil. The compressor oil ignited from the
heat of the pipe joint.  A flame front expelled into Employee #1, causing burn
injuries. Employee #1 was killed.
At 6:00 p.m. on April 5, 2023, an employee was driving a mobile crane down a
hill on a public road after completing work and leaving a jobsite. The mobile
crane crossed the road and struck a K-rail and overturned. The employee was
fatally injured (i.e., traumatic injuries as described by the coroner's report).
At 7:15 a.m. on April 11, 2023, an employee was walking with a forklift carrying
granite stone. The stone hit the ground, causing it to be released from the
clamp and strike the employee against another stored slab.  The employee was
killed.
At 9:30 a.m. on March 29, 2023, an employee was trimming a tree while in an
aerial lift. The employee may have been struck by a cut branch and knocked out
of the aerial lift. The employee was killed due to blunt force trauma.
At 3:30 p.m. on April 10, 2023, Employee #1 was operating the sand line controls
on the truck, while Employee #2 was removing the slack from the sand line to
avoid tress and water troughs in the area. When Employee #2 was removing the
slack in the sand line, s/he struck a nearby power line in the area.  Employee
#2 was thrown a distance.  Employee #1 reported feeling pain in his right arm,
then a few minutes later, lost consciousness.  The employer immediately provided
aid to Employee #1 and instructed Employee #2 to call Emergency Medical
Services.  Employee #1 later died from his injuries due to electrocution.
Employee #2 was hospitalized but received no lasting injuries.  The power
company stated the power line was approximately 7,200 volts phase to ground.
At 3:45 p.m. on April 10, 2023, an employee was working inside an unprotected
trench, performing sewer line tap and installation into the city sewer line and
a residential home. The employee was working in a trench at a depth of 12 feet.
The soil collapsed onto the employee, killing the employee.
At 10:30 a.m. on April 7, 2023, an employee was laying seed and straw. The
employee suffered from a medical event, possibly a heart attack.
At 7:00 a.m. on April 11, 2023, an employee was operating a tractor. The
employee was discovered lying on the ground dead from blunt force injuries.
At 8:15 a.m. on April 10, 2023, Employee #1 was utilizing a chainsaw to cut a
tree limb while standing on an eight-foot A-frame ladder. Employee #1 was
trimming a tree limb while standing on the third rung from the bottom of the
ladder. A coworker noticed Employee #1's hands fall to his side (indicating
Employee #1 may have had a heart attack/stroke) and the tree limb fall, striking
the ladder. Employee #1 was transported to the hospital and was later pronounced
dead on April 11, 2023 at approximately 6:35 p.m. An autopsy was not conducted
on Employee #1. According to the death certificate, Employee #1 suffered from
complications of blunt traumatic injuries.
At 1:00 p.m. on April 10, 2023, an employee was clearing snow from a roof more
than 30 feet above ground level. The employee stepped too close to the edge of
the roof and fell to the ground.  The employee was killed due to fatal head and
body injuries.
At 11:00 a.m. on April 11, 2023, Employee #1 was inside a locomotive.  A
locomotive struck a line of stationary rail cars.   Employee #1 was crushed when
the locomotive made contact with parked rail cars.  Coworker #1, a trainee, was
operating the locomotive. On the day of the accident, the rail cars were loaded
at the elevator yard. The rail cars were parked on track 11; there were 25 rail
cars. The locomotive operator stayed on track 11 and proceeded through the
switch. The locomotive was operating at walking speed. Coworker #2, a ground
man, threw the switch and then the locomotive operator was on track 10 before
heading back on track 11. The rail cars that were staged on track 11 were placed
too far forward.  Employee #1 sustained major trauma to the chest, broken ribs,
and a lacerated heart.   Employee #1 was killed.
At 9:00 a.m. on April 12, 2023, an employee was operating a Toyota, propane
fueled, sit-down forklift to unload stacks of empty pallets off of a flatbed
truck. As the employee was attempting to back off of the truck with his third
load of pallets, the left rear wheel of the forklift slipped off of the truck.
As the forklift began to tip off of the truck, the employee jumped off of the
forklift.  The forklift landed on the employee, pinning him to the ground.  The
employee was killed.
At 9:30 a.m. on March 20, 2023, an employee was working on an elevated platform.
The owner of the company was using a vibration device to shake dirt out of a
railroad car, and pushed over the railroad car. The railroad car tipped over and
struck the elevated platform where the employee was standing, causing the
platform to fall into a pit. The employee fell on to the concrete ground below.
The employee suffered blunt force trauma to his head, when striking the concrete
floor below. The employee was killed.
At 3:49 p.m. on April 12, 2023, an employee was killed when struck by an object.
At 8:15 a.m. on April 12, 2023, Employee #1 was assisting in the installation of
insulation on the roof of a pre-engineered building. The roof was approximately
27 feet 4 inches high. Employee #1 was utilizing a personal fall arrest system
attached to a 50-foot lifeline. As Employee #1 worked to secure the insulation,
he fell from the section of roof through the insulation. The employee fell
approximately 10 to 12 feet before his fall was arrested and struck the column
of the building. Employee #1 was killed due to head trauma.
At 7:40 p.m. on December 5, 2022, an employee was working with a crew of
coworkers preparing to remove a Christmas tree and install a blowout preventer
on a gas well. The crew was working on a mobile pumping station that was hooked
up to the Christmas tree which this was used to relieve the pressure in the
well. The crew connected approximately 50 feet of 2-inch pipe from the pumping
station to the Christmas tree. When they opened the valve on the Christmas tree,
the pipe ruptured at the pumping station causing it to swing wildly back and
forth. The pipe was rated for 5,000 pounds and the estimated well pressure was
2,500 pounds. A coworker (an independent contractor) and the employee were
killed. Three coworkers were struck by the pipe and hospitalized. They have
since been released. The crews were working two 12-hour shifts with five man
crews and both companies were out of the same State.
At 7:40 p.m. on December 5, 2022, Employee #1 (Laborer) and Employee #2
(Supervisor) were contracted to perform work on a client site. The employees

connected approximately 50 feet of 2-inch pipe from the pumping station to the
Christmas tree. When they opened the valve on the Christmas tree, the pipe
ruptured at the pumping station causing it to swing wildly back and forth. The
pipe was rated for 5,000 pounds and the estimated well pressure was 2,500

coworkers who worked for the host employer were struck by the pipe and
hospitalized. They have since been released. The crews were working two 12-hour
shifts with five man crews and both companies were out of the same State.
At 11:00 a.m. on April 11, 2023, an employee was attempting to break apart grain
clumps inside a grain bin elevator. The employee was engulfed by corn and
suffocated to death.
At 11:30 a.m. on April 13, 2023, an employee was using a Black & Decker 4076 (7
inch/9 inch heavy duty/industrial) angle sander (Type 5), with an abrasive wheel
(12 inches by 1/8 inch by 20 millimeters metal portable saw cut-off wheel).  The
employee accessed the work area from a front end-loader.  The employee was in
the process of cutting the blenders auger with the angle grinder.  At the time
of the accident, as the employee was cutting, the abrasive wheel broke and
struck the employee in the face. The employee was killed due to exsanguination.
The injuries included a large deep wound, left side of the mouth; laceration
right side of the mouth; and fractures of the left mandible and maxilla.
At 2:16 p.m. on April 12, 2023, an employee was installing a thermostat line.
The employee was walking backwards to uncoil the spool of wire he was going to
head injuries and was killed.
At 12:04 p.m. on Jun 1, 2023, an employee was parked at a truck stop in Sumner,
onto the concrete ground below. The employee fell approximately 34 feet and 6

utilize a restraint device while working from the elevated aerial lift.
During the morning of October 25, 2023, Employee #1, a ranch hand, reported that

bed in the afternoon. At around 7:30 p.m., a coworker went to check on Employee
#1. The coworker found Employee #1 collapsed in the hallway outside his bedroom.
Employee #1 was found unconscious. The fire department, an ambulance, and Nevada
County Sheriff's Department responded to the scene. They were unable to
resuscitate Employee #1, and he was pronounced dead at the site.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 31, 2023, an employee was performing landscaping
activities, including the removal of leaves by using a lawn mower to mulch up
the leaves. The employee was operating a zero-turn Gravely Pro-Turn 600 lawn
mower on a commercial property, when it tipped into a lake, pinning the employee
under water.  The employee was hospitalized and subsequently died on November 6,
2023. The employee died due to complications of drowning after being pinned
under the mower under water.
At 10:45 a.m. on October 26, 2023, three employees were travelling southbound on
the I-190 near milepost 6.3 in an employer-owned pickup truck. They had
completed a job at the wastewater treatment plant and were heading to lunch.
Employee #1 was sitting in the front passenger seat. Employee #2 was driving the
vehicle, and Employee #3 was sitting in the rear passenger seat. The pickup
truck was shot at multiple times by person(s) in another vehicle. Employee #1
was killed, and Employees #2 and #3 were hospitalized to treat unspecified
injuries.
At 5:00 p.m. on October 30, 2023, an employee was retrieving a waste container
from the north side of the road.  The employee went to cross the road and was
hit by a speeding vehicle.  The employee was killed.
The employee worked as a paramedic on an ambulance. The employee was directly
exposed to a COVID-19 positive patient on September 27, 2023, during patient
transport.  The employee exhibited COVID-19 symptoms on October 10, 2023 and
tested COVID-19 positive on October 11, 2023.  The employee was in-patient
hospitalized on October 26, 2023 and discharged from the hospital on October 27,
2023.  The employee died on October 29, 2023, due to complications associated
with COVID-19.
At 10:00 a.m. on June 3, 2022, an employee was caulking a windowsill while
standing on a six-foot A frame ladder that was seven inches from an open fire
pole hole.  When the employee stepped down from the ladder, he stepped into the
hole and fell 14 feet to a concrete surface below.  The employee sustained
unspecified head injuries and was admitted to the hospital, where he died two
days later.
At 7:30 am on July 19, 2023, an employee was working on a steel tubing induction
line and he was receiving tubing on the conveyor. The employee was waiting for
tubing to be fed by the kicker which kicked the tubing in place but it was
misaligned. The employee was trying to align the tubing when the backup caused
tubing to be lifted up against the induction coils. The contact with the coils
caused current to be transmitted through the tubing and the employee was
electrocuted.
The employee worked at a fitness center as a manager. The employee was
hospitalized and tested positive for COVID-19. The employee died at the hospital
due to COVID-19 complications on October 28, 2023.

began to unhook the fountain/aerator, separating it from the ropes that were

freely when not anchored; the only other restraint is the electrical cord
running into the pond to the shore.) Employee #1 then pulled the
fountain/aerator into the boat to gain access to the power cord cap connectors
still attached. Employee #1 was having a hard time separating the cord cap
connectors when the event occurred. Employee #1 fell out of the 10-foot John
Boat due to leaning over the edge of the boat, combined with the weight of the
water fountain/aerator. Employee #1 was not wearing a floatation device. When
Employee #1 entered the water, Employee #1 attempted to swim back towards the
10-foot John Boat. The 10-foot John Boat was still under power and moving in
circles around Employee #1, making it difficult to get to. The depth of the pond
is estimated at 10 feet.  The coworker was assessing the situation from the
shore and made the decision to strip down and attempt a rescue. Employee #1 was
at least 30 yards away from the coworker. The coworker was able to swim out to
Employee #1 to attempt a rescue. The coworker began to swim with Employee #1
towards the shore. Employee #1 began to go limp, and the coworker was not able
to get to shore with Employee #1 due to fatigue. The coworker released Employee
#1 and swam to the 10-foot John Boat. The coworker got the 10-foot John Boat to
calling the employee, the facility manager walked the yard to find the employee.
When the facility manager got close to the truck, he heard the phone ringing.
The facility manager decided to open the passenger side door but could not see
anyone; then, he went to open the driver side door. The facility manager saw the
employee on the floor of the truck face down, where the feet were by the gas
paddle upside down, and the face was towards the bed of the truck with hands on
the side of the body. The facility manager then called 911, who then transported
the employee to the morgue. Per the Coroner's report, the cause of death was
hypertensive cardiovascular disease with other significant conditions listed as

At 3:33 p.m. on April 24, 2023, an employee was working in the substation. The
employee started feeling ill and had chest pains. The employee died of a
possible heart attack.
At 8:45 a.m. on April 24, 2023, an employee was driving a Case SV250 Skid Steer
Loader in attempt to pull out a Ford F650 bucket truck and a Bandit Model 250 XP
woodchipper that were stuck on the lawn of a private residence. The owner
directed the employee to drive the skid steer loader to the front of the bucket
truck that was attached to the woodchipper. The owner attached the rigging line
via a double bowline knot on the front axle of the bucket truck to the tie down
loop on the bucket of the skid steer loader. There was approximately 15-20 feet
of rigging line in between the skid steer loader and the bucket truck. There was
a tree and a small barn that were directly behind the skid steer loader after
the owner attached the rigging line. The owner told the employee to watch out,
making sure not to hit the tree or small barn; so, the employee moved the skid
steer loader approximately 5-6 feet after the knot was tied, causing
approximately 5-6 feet of slack in the rigging line. The owner said that when
the employee reversed the skid steer loader, the slack rigging line was shock
loaded. The rigging line snapped approximately three feet from the tie off point
on the front axle of the bucket truck and flew into the cab of the skid steer
loader, directly hitting the employee in the chest. The owner got out of the
bucket truck to make sure the employee was ok; when the owner got to the skid
steer loader the employee was gasping for air. The owner then removed the
employee from the skid steer loader, called 911, and proceeded with CPR until
the responding authorities arrived. The employee was taken to the McKenzie
Health System Emergency Room in Sandusky, MI via Sanilac EMS, where he died from
his injuries. The employee sustained blunt force trauma to his chest.
At 11:15 a.m. on April 24, 2019, an employee working for an automobile parts
