coworker. While working on the roof of the structure, he fell approximately 10
feet 9 inches to the ground. He sustained a head injury from the impact and was
hospitalized. The employee died from his injuries on December 2, 2024.
At 11:30 a.m. on December 23, 2024, Employee #1 was working near the rear of a
skid steer. While kneeling to straighten landscape fabric, his foot was in the
path of the skid steer track. The skid steer moved in reverse and ran over his
foot. The employee either fell or twisted and fell further into the path of the
skid steer, which ran over him, causing multiple crushing injuries. The employee
was killed at the scene.
At 6:44 p.m. on December 20, 2024, an employee was either working on or had
arrived to work on a pump for a septic system. The employee was found
unresponsive by a tenant, who summoned medical services. The cause of death was
determined to be severe coronary stenosis.
At 11:15 a.m. on December 20, 2024, an employee helper was assisting a driver
backing up a Freightliner garbage truck at a cul-de-sac. The employee attempted
to jump onto a step on the back passenger side of the truck, where another
employee was standing operating the hopper. The employee slipped and fell from
the step and was crushed by the truck's rear passenger-side tires. The employee
sustained multiple head and torso injuries and was fatally injured.
At 10:00 p.m. on December 22, 2024, Employee #1 was on the ground level,
hoisting down a canvas bag from approximately 180 feet above, containing the
last of the equipment for the day. He was later found lying face up on the
ground with a damaged helmet and the canvas bag nearby. The bag was not attached
to the hoist line when discovered. Coworkers believe the bag became unhooked due
to inclement weather and struck the employee. No one witnessed the incident.
Employee #1 sustained a head injury, was hospitalized and placed on a ventilator
on December 20, 2024, and was later pronounced dead on December 22, 2024.
At 4:30 p.m. on December 17, 2024, an employee had just finished his workday and
clocked out. While near the time clock changing his boots to leave the building,
the employee suffered a seizure, fell backward, and died. The cause of death was
determined to be natural causes.
At 11:33 a.m. on December 19, 2024, an employee was installing racks when he
began experiencing chest pains. The employee suffered a fatal heart attack.
At 5:30 p.m. on December 20, 2024, Employee #1 was cleaning up debris from a
roof when he fell through the roof surface. He sustained fatal injuries as a
result of the fall.
At 10:45 a.m. on December 20, 2024, Employee #2 was attempting to warm a frozen
hose inside the cab of a Bobcat E35i compact excavator. Employee #1 was
positioned on the opposite side of the equipment. For unknown reasons, Employee
#2 disengaged the console lever lock, causing the excavator to suddenly move.
Neither employee had observed that the frozen hose had come into contact with
one of the machine's steering levers. When the lock was disengaged, the
equipment lurched and began to move, running over both employees. Employee #1
sustained serious injuries, including a broken and crushed foot, and was
hospitalized. Employee #2 sustained fatal injuries to the abdomen, pelvis, and
upper extremities.
At 6:15 a.m. on December 24, 2024, an employee was mowing the slopes of hole #10
green when the lawn mower rolled into a pond. The employee drowned due to water
intrusion into the lungs.
At 3:00 p.m. on July 8, 2024, an employee was assisting in removing cedar roof
tiles from a residential roof and gathering the debris and transporting it to
the onsite dumpster using a wheelbarrow. The employee began to feel ill and
stopped working to rest in the shade. Soon after that the employee, suffering
symptoms of heat stroke such as altered mental state, walked away from the
worksite and into the adjacent wooded area. After entering the woods, he
collapsed and eventually lost consciousness due to heat stroke.  He was found
dead later that evening by police.
At 6:45 p.m. on December 24, 2024, an employee was recovering a disabled vehicle
on the right side of eastbound I-94 at milepost 283.8. While beginning towing
operations, the employee was struck by a traveling vehicle and died as a result
of the incident.
At 12:30 p.m. on December 26, 2024, an employee was walking between a steel beam
and a conveyor when he became caught and was crushed between the two. The
employee died at the scene.
At 1:05 p.m. on December 17, 2024, an employee fell from an elevated work area.
The fall resulted in fatal injuries.
At 11:38 a.m. on December 6, 2024, Employee #1 was operating forklift #9 to move
materials in and out of a warehouse. While traveling backward outdoors, he
complained of vapors or fumes and stopped the forklift to vomit into a trash
can. A fellow forklift operator noticed and reported Employee #1's condition to
their supervisor.  Employee #1 was escorted to the break room to rest while
medical advice was obtained over the phone. The attending doctor recommended
rest and fresh air. At the end of his shift, Employee #1 declined offered
boilermakers for a facilities support service were working on a 12-inch pipe to
flip the blind. The pipe released hydrogen sulfide gas exposing the crew. The
employee died from poisoning from the hydrogen sulfide gas.
At 4:15 p.m. on October 10, 2024, an employee installing electrical equipment
and tubing in a process unit was exposed to a release of hydrogen sulfide. The
employee suffered fatal poisoning due to hydrogen sulfide exposure.
An employee was working as a registered nurse between two healthcare facilities
when she was exposed to COVID-19. The employee contracted COVID-19 and
subsequently died from her infection at 9:30 a.m. on August 26, 2021.
An employee had worked as a receptionist for a skilled nursing care facility.
The employee contracted COVID-19 outside of work. The employee was tested for
COVID-19 on June 1, 2022, and received a positive result on June 3, 2022. The
employee's symptoms worsened on June 5, 2022, prompting her to go the doctor and
then to the hospital on June 6, 2022, where she died the same day. The employee
worked in a facility where coworkers and residents have tested positive for
COVID-19 recently. The spouse of the employee did not report the definitive
cause of death. Information regarding engineering, administrative and personal
protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 11:30 a.m. on February 23, 2022, Employee 1 and Employee 2 worked in a
ten-foot-deep trench to install a new sewer pipe. At some point, the trench wall
collapsed and both employees were caught in the collapsed soil. Both employees
were hospitalized to treat fractures to two ribs, spine, pelvis and tailbone,
and a collapsed lung.
At 11:00 a.m. on June 13, 2022, an employee was delivering compost loaded in the
bed of a grapple truck.  The employee was working in a two-man crew and was
being trained to operate the grapple truck. A coworker was operating the
hydraulic grapple and inadvertently swung the grapple into 14.4 kV overhead
power lines. The employee was climbing out of truck cab at the same moment the
grapple contacted the power lines. The employee was killed by electrocution.
At 1:30 p.m. on June 15, 2022, an employee was driving a dump truck loaded with
hot asphalt to a paving jobsite.  The employee lost control of the truck and was
unable to stop, driving through an intersection with a stop sign and striking a
vacant home with the vehicle.  The employee was not able to stop the vehicle due
to the steep grade of the road and possible brake failure.  The hot asphalt in
the truck caused the house and truck to catch on fire. The driver was killed as
a result of burns and fractures sustained from the truck collision with the
house and ensuing structure fire.
At 11:30 a.m. on June 13, 2022, an employee was operating a Caterpillar #AB5B74
front loader to clean up manure in cow pens at a dairy farm. The employee began
his work shift at 5:00 a.m. and had been scraping dried manure from the milk
barn floor and placing it into a large bin.  Coworker #1 had observed the
employee operating the loader at 9:30 a.m. Although Coworker #1 did not see the
employee after this time, the Coworker #1 could hear the loader's engine running
from 200 yards away. Coworker #2 observed the loader not moving and investigated
at 11:30 a.m., and found the employee slumped over in the air-conditioned cab of
the loader.  The loader was still running but was in neutral gear. Coworker #2
called emergency medical services (EMS),  The employee's heart was not beating
at the time that EMS arrived.  The employee was killed by a heart attack.
An employee was working as a correctional deputy probation officer for a county
probation department when he was exposed to COVID-19. The employee underwent
weekly COVID -19 testing at the facility and there was no parolee or staff who
tested positive for COVID-19 prior to his exposure to COVID-19. The employee was
not identified or notified to be in close contact with a known case of COVID-19
at the facility. The employee began having symptoms on December 9, 2021, which
was his last day of work. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 on December
10, 2021 and was quarantining at home until he was admitted to the hospital for
COVID-19 pneumonia on December 18-25, 2021.  Another correctional deputy
probation officer who was assigned to the same office tested positive for
COVID-19 on December 14, 2021, but was not hospitalized.
At 11:45 a.m. on December 1, 2021, an employee was performing repairs on a
commercial laundry machine. The machine is equipped with a drop table with a
vinyl belt that catches garments from overhead slings and distributes the
garments for folding. The employee  and Coworker #1 and Coworker #2, attempted
to fix a broken belt instead of waiting for maintenance to fix it. As Coworker
#1 was trying to roll the belt onto the roller, Coworker #2 was using the
controls to wind the belt up while the employee held the belt onto the roller.
The employee caught his arm between the roller and the equipment causing a
fracture to his forearm and requiring hospitalization.
At 6:50 a.m. on October 18, 2021, an employee was adjusting a forming machine
used to shape cheese at a manufacturing facility. When the employee tried to
remove cheese stuck to the machine before the forming machine came to a complete
stop, the employee's wrist caught by the machine. The employee sustained a wrist
sprain and was treated without hospitalization.
At 9:15 a.m. on June 17, 2022, an employee who worked for an HVAC contractor was
utilizing a Trimble Unit to mark the locations of plumbing components such as
PEX chairs and sleeves. The employee had his back turned when he was struck by a
load of 4-foot by 8-ffot decking sheets. The load of decking sheets was being
offloaded on the 31st floor by a crane operator. The employee was pushed from
the 28th floor approximately 30-feet down a stairwell shaft that was under
construction. The employee struck his head on the steps and his legs on the
wooden stair railing on the outside perimeter of the stairs. The employee broke
his legs on the top and middle rail of the 28th floor guardrail system due to
the fall. In addition, multiple decking sheets fell down the unfinished
stairwell shaft hitting multiple shoring posts and destroying the existing
guardrail systems from the 31st to the 28th floor. Overall, the employee
encurred head and lead injuries and whole body impact from being struck-by the
load and the fall and was killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on June 17, 2022, an employee was working on repairing a vehicle
at a junkyard. The employee was one of multiple independent self-employed
contractors who subleased space at the junkyard as tenants to store and repair
automobiles purchased at auction prior to transporting them for resale in
Mexico. The employee was in a verbal contract with another independent
contractor, a coworker, to sublease a portion of the employee's workspace to
also independently repair vehicles at the junkyard.  The employee was working
alone under a Chevrolet Impala with the front end elevated by two jack stands
and both front tires removed, when the vehicle fell from the jack stands. The
coworker returned from an offsite meeting and discovered the employee pinned
under the vehicle.  The coworker called out to the junkyard's other tenants for
help, who called 9-1-1 and used a portable jack to pull the employee out from
under the car.  First responders from the San Diego Fire Department attempted
life saving measures but declared the employee dead at the scene.  The employee
was killed by traumatic asphyxia and crushing injuries to the upper chest.
At 8:47 p.m. on June 13, 2022, an employee was supervising a work crew level
grading roads in agriculture fields.  While the employee was seated inside his
vehicle, Coworker #1 attempted to call his cell phone to ask for additional
instructions, but the employee did not answer.  When coworker #2 drove to check
on the employee, he discovered the employee unresponsive and not breathing.
Coworker #2 called 9-1-1 to request assistance and initiated CPR on the
emergency response and was found on unconscious and did not have a pulse.
Responders provided CPR and was revived by paramedics. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a head injury and heart arrhythmia.
At 5:30 p.m. on September 19, 2021, an employee was working as a cashier for a
discount retail store when two people entered the store. The employee was
working on cash register #3 when the two individuals approached her and
attempted to get a refund of 25 dollars. The employee told the individuals that
the store would not honor the refund and that a local bank would refund their
money instead. Upon being told that information the two individuals became upset
and left the store. Approximately 1 hour later, the two individuals returned to
the store. One person was wearing a black hoodie and a face mask the other was
wearing a white shirt and face mask. They approached the employee at the same
register clearly agitated demanding their refund. As they reached the register,
they cornered the employee and struck her several times, knocking her to the
floor. As she fell to the floor she screamed for help and Coworker #1 approached
the register. Seeing Coworker #1 approach, the two individuals ran from the
store north bound through the parking lot and disappeared. As they left the
scene, the remaining coworkers came to the employee's assistance and noticed she
was bleeding. Coworker #2, a manager, called 911 and local emergency medical
services and law enforcement responded to the scene. EMS stabilized the employee
and transported her to a nearby medical center. The employee was hospitalized to
treat three stab wounds to her left chest, right abdominal area, and lower left
back/kidney area.
An employee was working as a heavy mobile equipment mechanic whose job was to
perform maintenance on heavy mobile equipment that was used in the mine. The
employee's last day on site was September 22, 2021, and COVID-19 symptoms
commenced on September 25, 2021. The employee tested positive for COVID-19 at a
drive-through test on site on September 28, 2021, and was instructed to
self-quarantine. The employee's symptoms worsened and he was admitted to the
hospital on October 4, 2021, and was discharged on October 10, 2021.
At 11:05 a.m. on December 9, 2021, an employee, a machine operator, was using a
260-ton hot metal press to form the ends of pre-heated metal rods when a 14.5
pound, 8-inch by 4-inch by 2-inch metal die spacer, which had been left in the
press, shot out and struck him in the chest. The employee suffered a chest
contusion, multiple rib fractures and a spleen laceration.
An employee, a care partner at a medical center, tested positive for COVID-19 on
March 30, 2020.  The employee was hospitalized for three days and recovered from
her infection.
At 6:00 a.m. on January 15, 2022, an employee who was working as a Produce Clerk
Supervisor for a grocery store was walking in an aisle when he lost
consciousness and fell. Coworkers reported seening the employee walking back and
forth in an aisle with his cart when they heard a loud sound and observed that
the employee fell to the concrete floor. The employee lacerated his head but
declined treatment from the fire departments emergency medical tecnician (EMT).
The employee was eventually taken to the hospital and admitted for two days.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 5, 2020, an employee was sealing a well with concrete.
The employee was struck by a hose from a concrete pump.  The employee suffered
head and neck injuries and was treated without hospitalization.
An employee worked for a public utilities department. In early December 2021,
the employee had traveled to Mexico. The employee last worked on December 15,
2021, and left work due experiencing symptoms. By December 19, 2021, the
employee noticed his symptoms were COVID-19 related. On that day, the employee
went for a COVID-19 test and received a positive test result. The employee was
later hospitalized and died at 8:00 a.m. on January 18, 2022. None of the
employee's coworkers tested positive for COVID-19 within the 2-week timeframe
before and after December 15, 2021. Information regarding engineering,
administrative and personal protective equipment controls for COVID-19 are not
included in the narrative.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 22, 2021, an employee working as a groundskeeper for
a community college district was operating a woodchipper. The employee and a
coworker were using the chipper to mulch branches and other debris at the site.
The operation came to a stop when the chute got clogged. The employee stopped
the machine. He then obtained some tools and removed the bolts holding the chute
in place. As the employee was working on the machine, the chute started to
detach from the chipper. The employee noticed that it was falling off and so he
tried to hold it with his hand. That was when he realized that the chute was too
heavy and he let it go. At that moment, the employee lost his balance and fell
nearly 3 feet from the machine. The employee was hospitalized to treat multiple
fractures from impact with the ground.
At 5:30 p.m. on April 16, 2022, an employee was moving a pot from a burner.
While walking backwards, the employee tripped and fell backwards in a sitting
position into another pot of boiling water that had been placed on the floor.
The employee suffered burns to the lower back, buttocks, pelvis and upper thighs
and was killed.
At 11:45 p.m. on May 17, 2022, an employee was using an air compressor to
inflate the tire on the truck trailer he was preparing to haul. As the employee
filled the tire, it ruptured at the rim, and struck the employee.  The employee
At 5:30 p.m. on May 19, 2022, an employee was straddling a tree branch to remove
an existing light.  The employee's feet disturbed a beehive inside the tree, and
he was stung by bees.  The employee was killed.
At 10:00  a.m. on January 25, 2022, an employee was preparing the heating
stripping pot, when a foreign object made contact with the heated element,
causing a chemical reaction to splash onto the employee.  The employee suffered
burns to the right arm and was treated without hospitalization.
At 6:10 p.m. on June 23, 2022, an employee was operating a forklift in a
warehouse.  The warehouse had recently received an order of resin pellets,
contained in Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container (FBIC) bag.  There were two
FBICs with one stacked on the other, each weighing approximately 2,000 pounds.
The employee's forklift tore open the FBIC on the bottom of the stack, causing
the resin pellets to pour out of the bag.  As the pellets emptied, the FBIC on
top was no longer supported and slid off and crushed the employee.  The employee
was killed.
At 8:30 a.m. on April 1, 2022, Employee #1 walked up to Employee #2 to have a
discussion about their relationship that had recently ended. After Employee #2
failed to agree to reconcile, Employee #1 drew a firearm in an attempt to take
Employee #2's life. Employee #1 attempted to harm Employee #2 by use of a
firearm. A coworker began a physical struggle for the weapon with Employee #1,
after witnessing the incident. During the struggle, Employee #1 was able to turn
the weapon toward himself and fire, taking his own life.  Employee #2 also
suffered a  gunshot wound and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 12:18 p.m. on May 12, 2022, an employee was cutting the grass on the side of
a hill with a Dixie Chopper XCaliber 3674D Zero Turn Riding Mower.  The mower's
rollover protection system was not in use. The mower made an abrupt turn and
traveled straight down the hill with a 10-to-15-degree slope. At the bottom of
the hill, the mower hit a rock and overturned on top of the employee, trapping
him.  The employee suffered traumatic asphyxia and was killed.
At approximately 8:50 a.m. on February 11, 2022, an employee walked on  a ramp
outside of her classroom.  Then, the employee slipped  fractured an ankle due to
slippery condition (vomit residue) and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 11:15 a.m. an employee who worked as an excavator had been driving a digger.
As the employee sat in the equipment, he experienced a heart attack and died.
At 12:08 p.m. on June 6, 2022, an employee was walking through the yard, looking
for a container. A semi-truck was backing up and hit the employee. The employee
was killed.
At 5:24 p.m. on June 23, 2022, an employee had been performing soft scaping
(hand digging with a shovel) in direct heat with no shade. The employee was in
the process of moving fiber optic cable from the street to behind a curb in a
grassy area. The goal was for the employee to bury the cable about 12 inches
into the ground. The employee complained of feeling tired and was also
experiencing cramping.  Due to these complaints, the employer took the employee
off the digging crew and sent him with a coworker (vac truck operator) to dump a
load. When the employee returned from dumping the vac truck, he began performing
soft scaping again.  Shortly after, the employee became combative and the police
were called. The employee continued to be aggressive, was refusing aid, then
passed out and was unresponsive.  EMS was called and the employee was
transported to the hopsital and died the following day. The employee had been
diagnosed with severe heat stroke and had a core temperature of 110 degrees
Fahrenheit.
On June 22, 2022, an employee, who worked for a roofing contractor, was coming
down from a roof. The empoyee was on the walk-board of a ladder jack scaffold
about 5 feet off of the deck. The employer believes he may have been
transitioning from the walk-board to the ladder when he fell. The employee
struck the deck railing and then fell an additional 22 feet from the railing to
the ground.  The employee was transported to the hospital, where he was
pronounced dead later that afternoon.
On June 19, 2022, an employee was working on a construction crew for a new
single family home. The employee was sanding something not specified in the
narrative when she fell from either a ladder or a scaffold. The employee struck
some equipment on the way down before landing in the basement. The employee
broke her neck and was pronounced dead by Emergency Medical Services at the
scene.
On June 23, 2022, an employee was ejected from a vehicle that had a roll-over
accident. The employee was killed.
At 10:30 a.m. on June 24, 2022,  an employee was cutting a tree.  The tree fell
and landed on the employee's chest, pinning and killing him.
At 7:00 p.m. on June 15, 2022, an employee was trimming the top of a pine hedge
from an Altec LR7 Front Mount Aerial truck, approximately 40 feet above ground.
An outrigger slid off the wood block and onto the soft grass, causing the truck
tip towards the driver's side. The boom, extended approximately 40 feet high,
tipped over and ejected the employee from the bucket.  The employee was not
wearing a fall protection harness or body belt with lanyard secured to an anchor
point on the boom.  The employee suffered contusions from his neck to his chin
and was killed.
At 9:00 a.m. on June 24, 2022, an employee was working in a trench repairing a
new sewer line when the trench collapsed. The employee was asphyixated and died
on the scene.
On July 13, 2021, an employee who worked for a property manager was killed after
being struck by a falling beam. No other details are indicated in the narrative.
At 11:45 a.m. on December 27, 2021, an employee was assembling a truss using a
Max Super Stapler TA551B/16-11, pneumatic stapler with 1 ? inch staples for a
roof and floor truss manufacturer for residential and commercial construction.
The employee was working on top of a truss table when he stapled one side of the
truss and moved forward to staple another section with his finger on the trigger
of the stapler.  As the employee moved, the air hose became caught in a grove on
the edge of the table pulling the gun and causing it to hit his knee lodging a
staple in it. The employee was transported to a local hospital, where he was
the concrete floor below and died due to blunt force trauma to his head and
body.
At 3:00 a.m. on December 24, 2022, an employee was performing duties as a
bouncer at a drinking establishment (bar). The employee was struck in the head
during an altercation with a patron outside of the establishment.  The employee
incurred a fractured skull and was hospitalized. On December 28, 2022, the
employee died.
At 1:00 a.m. on January 6, 2023, an employee was troubleshooting a hydraulic
leak under skid steer when the skid steer fell on top of him. The employee
suffered crushing injuries to his upper torso and died.
At 11:18 p.m. on August 27, 2022, an employee was providing security at an
establishment as a guard. During the evening, the employee removed two patrons
who were fighting from the establishment. One of the patrons went to his vehicle
where he retrieved a sharp object before returning to the establishment and
attempting to enter. When the employee refused to allow the patron back inside,
the patron stabbed the employee in the neck with the sharp object. The employee
was killed by lacerations and puncture wounds to the neck.
At 10:45 a.m. on November 30, 2022, an employee was using an all-terrain
forklift to elevate himself to perform welding at a covered parking structure.
The employee welding steel pipes to the top and bottom of the structure. The
employee welded the first steel pipe to the top right side of the structure, and
then proceeded to weld the second steel pipe at the top center before climbing
down the forklift carriage. While scaling down, the employee misplaced his foot
and stepped on the back/forward and top/down control levers at the same time.
Contacting the levers at the same time caused the employee to be crushed between
the forklift carriage and cab safety bar. The employee was killed by crushing
injuries.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee was working from a scaffold at
approximately 8 feet above a concrete surface installing wooden trusses when a
scaffold brace failed and the scaffold collapsed. The employee fell from the
scaffold and landed on his head and suffered fatal head injuries.
At 1:45 a.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee was assisting with stabilizing
freight that had become unstable when the freight fell on him and crushed him to
death.
At 10:45 a.m. on January 9, 2023, an employee and coworkers, steel erectors,
were performing structural steel erection operations of a 1,000,000 square foot
warehouse building. The scope of the work included the installation of metal
decking on the roof which consisted of welding 22 Gauge, Type B, 3-foot wide by
18-foot long metal decking panels. For fall protection, the workers were
utilizing full body harnesses with self-retractable lifelines attached to roof
anchors. The installation process consisted of dividing 12 workers in groups of
two to handle the panels. Ten workers were positioning the panels while two
employees were tack-welding the panels in place. The employee was assigned to
tack weld the panels in place during. After approximately 20 panels were secured
to the roof, most of the workers came down to the ground however four workers
remained on the roof, including the employee. The employee, for unknown reasons,
was not wearing his harness when he fell approximately 45 feet from the roof to
the concrete floor below and died instantly as result of the impact.
At 12:00 noon on January 2, 2023, five employees were working on a mast climbing
work platform on the tenth floor of a new multi-unit residential building under
construction when the platform collapsed and 3 employees fell approximately 70
feet from the tenth floor to the fourth floor. The employees died on the impact.
The other two employees on the platform were rescued by the local fire
department and transported to a medical center with non-life-threatening
injuries.
At 10:00 a.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee was breaking down a traffic
control zone when he fell in the middle of the road and struck his head on the
ground. The employee suffered blunt force head trauma and died.
At 9:40 a.m. on December 9, 2022, an employee who performed maintenance duties
was inspecting the sag in a crane cable when he was struck by the crane's rear
catenary trolley. The employee incurred multiple blunt force trauma injuries to
the back and neck and was killed.
At 1:00 p.m. on January 9, 2023, an employee was assigned to work on the twelfth
floor roof to perform clean up and other minor punch list items when he  fell 8
stories from a parapet walkway down to the fourth floor roof. The employee
suffered fatal injuries from the fall.
At 9:15 p.m. on January 5, 2023, an employee was attempting to control
over-foaming on a tank when he removed a grate and accidentally stepped into the
opening. The employee fell into the drilling mud and drowned.
At 10:45 a.m. on December 21, 2022, an employee was installing a steel stud
internal wall framing from a 5-foot baker's scaffold when he fell and struck his
head on the concrete floor. The employee refused medical attention at the time
and was transported home. The employer called an ambulance to the employee's
home the next day due to the employee not willing to go to the hospital on his
own will. The employee was in care at the hospital from December 22, 2022 until
his death on January 6, 2023.
At 2:00 p.m. on January 9, 2023, an employee was attempting to remove a piece of
wood that was stuck in the lift chain of the lumber stacker lift. When the jam
was cleared, the lift dropped, crushing the employee's chest and head between
the lift and another piece of equipment. The employee died due to his injuries.
At 3:00 a.m. on January 9, 2023, an employee threw a knife up to a coworker on a
derrick platform and instructed him to cut the rope holding up a removable metal
grate that was part of the workover rig derrick platform. The coworker cut the
rope while the rope while the employee was standing directly beneath the
platform. The section of platform fell approximately 10 feet and struck the
employee in the head. The employee died due to blunt force trauma to the head.
At 3:30 p.m. on January 16, 2023, an employee was filling up a vehicle with
gasoline stored on site when the gas fumes ignited and engulfed him in flames.
The employee suffered burns over the majority of body and died.
At 8:33 p.m. on January 3, 2023, an employee was working as a process operator
at a petrochemical facility and was with making the rounds, checking furnace
temperatures with a laser gun. The employee was found unresponsive by the
furnaces and subsequently died.
On December 19, 2022, an employee working for a polyester manufacturer was

At 8:30 p.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee moved a clamp truck and placed two
household appliances at either side of the clamps. The employee bypassed two
safety systems on the clamp truck and clamped himself between two household
appliances. The employee was killed due to asphyxiation.
At 7:30 a.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee was working on the Level #74 of a
plastic plant. The employee fell 25 feet through a hole in the floor grating.
The employee was killed.
At 12:00 p.m. on June 21, 2023, an employee had been cleaning, prior to getting
off work and going home. The employee died of a heart attack due to the heat
inside the plant.
At 6:00 p.m. on July 13, 2023, an employee was playing basketball and then went
into the pool to cool off because his heart was racing. The lifeguard notified
the employee's mother that he was floating on his stomach with blood discharging
from his nose. The cause of death was unknown, although there were speculations
of heart issues.
At 8:30 a.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee was preparing to trip pipe out of
well to be scanned/inspected, when the well "came in" covering the employee with
oil and gas.  This caused the employee to step back from the controls, releasing
the brake and allowing the traveling blocks to fall approximately 15 to 20 feet,
knocking the employee through the guard rail off the platform to the ground.
The employee was killed.
At 12:20 p.m. on July 16, 2023, an employee working as a painter for a
construction company had climbed a ladder, stopped and was standing on the
ladder when he fell. The employee fell to the concrete surface below and died
from blunt force trauma including skull fractures.
At 7:00 a.m. on January 24, 2023, an employee working for an HVAC maintenance
company was preparing to check an HVAC unit on a roof. As the employee stepped
onto the roof, he fell through a skylight. The employee fell approximately 21
feet onto a cart and died.
At 11:00 a.m. on July 13, 2023, an employee working on a plastering project for
a construction company was filling buckets with concrete. The employee needed to
take the buckets to the second floor of a building using a scaffold pulley
system. The pulley system fell off and the top part hit the employee in the
head. The employee died from blunt force trauma including a concussion and neck
injury.
At 7:45 a.m. on July 17, 2023, an employee was digging a 1-foot ditch to remove
the irrigation system. The employee was crossing over a 1-foot ditch, when he
suddenly fell to the ground. The employee died due to natural causes.
At 1:00 p.m. on July 10, 2023, an employee was picking cherries.  A coworker
heard a thump and found the employee on the ground.  It appears as if it was a
medical issue, as the ladder was intact, and the employee fell a minimal
distance.
At 2:30 p.m. on July 13, 2023, an employee was limbing trees from the bucket of
a lift truck at approximately 30 feet. The boom was rubbing on the trunk of the
tree, and there was enough pressure to make the bucket bounce when the boom was
released from the trunk.  This caused the employee to fall, striking the bed of
the boom truck. The employee was killed due to severe blunt force trauma to the
head and chest.
At 1:00 p.m. on June 15, 2023, an employee was performing traffic control
adjacent to an excavator being operated by a private contractor. The employee's
heel became caught under the track of the excavator, and he fell to the ground
on his back, fracturing his pelvis and femur.  The employee was hospitalized and
died approximately 9 days later from complication of his injuries.
At 7:45 a.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee was removing a drive shaft.  The
vehicle's rear passenger tire rolled onto the employee's chest.  The employee
was killed due to blunt force trauma.
At 9:30 a.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee was fixing a leveling valve.  The
employee went under the vehicle and was run over.  The employee was killed due
to crushing injuries.
At 10:35 p.m. on July 17, 2023, an employee working as an installer for a
mechanical contractor was assisting with the installation of a curb for an HVAC
system. The employee was gathering tools on the roof to pack up for the day when
he collapsed. The employee had died from the toxic effects of methamphetamines.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 14, 2023, Employee #1 was standing next to a semi-trailer.
Employee #1 was struck by the arm of the spraying equipment and caught between
the arm of the sprayer and the trailer of the truck.  This occurred as a
coworker was driving the sprayer next to the semi-trailer. Employee #1 was
crushed and killed when caught between heavy machinery.
At 11:56 p.m. on July 14, 2023, an employee, a groundman, was attempting to prep
a train chassis for the arrival of a container to be placed on top of the train
chassis. After the prep of the train chassis, the employee walked between two
truck chassis that were positioned on the rail. As the employee walked between
both truck chassis, the crane operator attempted to move a container from
another truck chassis. Not all the container pins were disengaged; as a result,
the truck chassis with the container moved forward, crushing the employee
between two truck chassis. The employee was transported to Advocate Christ
Hospital and Medical Center in Oak Lawn, IL and pronounced dead.
At 2:40 p.m. on July 17, 2023, an employee working as a roofer with a roofing
contractor crew was working on a roof of a commercial building. The crew saw bad
weather moving in and started to come off the roof. They were bringing down
5-gallon buckets of silicone by descending an aluminum extension ladder while
carrying the buckets. The employee and the ladder fell to the left and the
employee struck his head on the concrete floor. The employee died from head
injuries from impact with the floor.
At 10:30 a.m. on May 4, 2023, an employee working for a crop farming business
was loading a skid steer and auger onto a flatbed trailer. The auger fell off
the skid steer forks while employee was beneath the load. The employee died from
severe head trauma.
At 3:00 p.m. on Jully 17, 2023, an employee and a coworker were loading granite
slabs onto a delivery flatbed truck with the use of an overhead gantry crane.
Each slab weighs 980 pounds, and the employees were loading two at a time.  The
crane is equipped with a "grabber clamp" that can close and hold the two slabs
and carry them in a standing up position across the facility.  The employee was
operating the wireless hand-held controller for the crane and the coworker was
walking in front of the load as they moved it towards the flatbed truck.  The
flatbed truck had an "A-Frame" in the bed where the slabs could be placed and
leaned back against, so that they would stay in place.  The A-Frame is an
industry standard piece of equipment that keeps the slab upright and leaned back
approximately 9 degrees.  The slabs are secured in place with cargo straps prior
to moving the truck. The employee used the crane to raise the slabs up and into
position on the flatbed truck and onto the A-Frame.  The slab appeared to be in
its correct position, and the grabber clamp automatically released itself from
residential roofing activities on a steep-slope roof. The employee fell 20 feet
from the rake edge to the lower level below. No fall protection system was being
utilized. On January 6, 2024, the employee was admitted to the hospital to treat
blunt force head injuries. On February 1, 2024, the employee died from his
injuries. Weather did not play a role in the incident.
At 9:45 p.m. on March 8, 2024, an employee was working on a battery bucket
assembly line, performing her task in zone #4. The employee lost an ear pod and
went under the conveyor table to try to retrieve the lost ear pod, and her long
hair was caught in and grabbed by the conveyor system, causing a traumatic brain
injury.  The employee was killed.
At 10:40 p.m. on February 22, 2024, an employee working as a special education
teacher for a charter school had been working after hours. The teacher was
completing student individual education plans (IEPs) before leaving the school.
The employee left the third floor and was descending the 2nd set of steps when
he fell. The employee died from a massive head injury from impact with the
floor.
At 8:38 a.m. on March 4, 2024, a maintenance worker was cleaning gutters of a
school building. The employee used a 25-foot extension latter to access the roof
the building in order to clean gutters that were approximately 10 feet high. The
employee knelt on the metal roof top to clean gutters by hand with a scooper.
After cleaning a section of gutter, the employee stood up about three feet from
the edge of the roof, became dizzy and fainted, fell forward, striking the edge
of the roof gutter, flipping and landing on the grass ground below. The employee
landed on his  back, head and neck and sustained blunt force neck injuries. The
employee was hospitalized and later died as a result of his injuries.
At 7:15 a.m. on October 10, 2023, an employee working as an automobile mechanic
for a transportation services company was standing at his workstation eating
breakfast and looking at his cell phone. The employee fell backwards striking
his head on the concrete floor. The employee died from cranio-cerebral trauma,
including complications from his injury.
At 7:30 a.m. on March 9, 2024, an employee was collecting signs that had blown
around the property, he traveled over 1,000 feet to a retention pond. The
employee slipped or fell into the pond and drowned. He was killed.
At 8:15 a.m. on March 11, 2024, an employee was using a powered industrial
vehicle to remove pallets from a box truck.  The box truck shifted forward, and
he jumped from the powered industrial vehicle. The powered industrial vehicle
fell on him, crushing his head and torso.  The employee was killed.
At 3:00 p.m. on March 8, 2024, Employee # 1 and Employee #2, both laborers, were
working with a coworker, using a 40-foot metal ladder to install light fixtures
on a palm tree.  The ladder was within ten feet of a power line. After
installing the fixture, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were taking down the ladder
when ladder made contact with a 7.97 KV overhead power line. Employee #1 was
killed due to electrocution, and Employee #2 received severe electrical burns
and was hospitalized.
On March 7, 2024, following an automatic cleaning process of a tank trailer, the
employee entered the tank, presumably to conduct routine inspection of the tank
following the wash process. The employee was wearing rubber gloves, boots, and
coveralls and was not wearing a respirator or a retrieval line.  The employee
was discovered by a coworker at the bottom of a ladder.  The employee was killed
due to probable asphyxia after the chemical exposure.
At 5:30 a.m. on March 11, 2024, an employee was using a powered industrial truck
to remove skids of product from a large freezer for shipping. Employee was found
unconscious on the powered industrial truck. The employee died from
arteriosclerotic and hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
At 2:46 p.m. on December 14, 2023, an employee had disposed of cardboard boxes
in a trash bin. When returning back to his workstation, the employee slipped on
a dropped piece of cardboard and went headfirst into a wooden support pole. The
employee appeared to be intoxicated. The employee was killed due to blunt force
trauma to the forehead.
At 10:00 a.m. on March 9, 2024, an employee was driving a three-axle Volvo D16
truck with a roll-off bed in the elevated position, not wearing a seatbelt. He
struck the bottom of an overpass, stopping the truck, and the employee was
partially ejected through the windshield. The employee was killed and the
coroner determined that the death was a result of atherosclerotic and
cardiovascular disease.
At 8:45 a.m. on March 7, 2024, an employee working for a construction contractor
was standing on the back of a truck. The employee was located near a spool
attempting to lower a SEMCO hydraulic pump hoist into the hazard zone. The pump
hydraulics line was damaged causing a leak which resulted in the hoist to fall
and strike the employee. The employee died from blunt trauma injuries to his
chest and abdomen.
At 2:15 p.m. on February 14, 2024, an employee working as a ship to store
manager for a department store was operating a wave lift powered industrial
vehicle (PIV) cutting plastic straps off new boxes. The boxes were located on a
shelf that was approximately 9 feet high. The plastic straps that held the new
boxes were horizontal to the shelf and the employee had to reach to cut the
plastic straps. As evidenced by the surveillance video, the employee positioned
the PIV parallel to the racking system before repositioning the PIV
perpendicular to the racking system. The employee was now working with the PIV
guardrail facing the racking system. The doors on the PIV were facing the front
of the shelf. The employee stepped out of the basket to cut the plastic strap
closest to the wall approximately 43 inches from the PIV. The guardrail of this
type of PIV has two metal swinging doors that swing in towards where the
employee. This PIV also has an alarm that emits an audible beeping noise when
the lift guardrail system is bypassed, which is activated when the lift is above
22 inches. The employee died from head trauma when he fell approximately seven
feet to the concrete floor below. The fire department confirmed that someone had
disengaged the alarm, and that the PIV had been moved after the employee had
fallen, but was still in its raised position with one of the doors open.
At 2:36 a.m. on March 11, 2024, an employee was backing a garbage truck into a
narrow driveway between two apartment buildings in order to empty a dumpster.
The employee was killed from a gunshot and was found hours later.
At 11:30 a.m. on March 11, 2024, an employee was driving a 2020 Fort Micro Bird
25-passenger school bus eastbound on a highway. She was about half-way through
navigating a right-hand curve when the truck crossed over the broken yellow
center lane line into the westbound lane and collided head-on with a loaded
39-foot semi-truck and trailer. Both vehicles left the roadway in a northerly
direction and caught fire. The collision occurred while the school bus was about
halfway through navigating a right-hand curve. Both vehicles veered off the
roadway in a northerly direction and caught fire. The employee sustained
multiple unspecified blunt force injuries and thermal injuries, resulting from
the fire.  She was killed.
At 2:30 p.m. on March 9, 2024, an employee  was at the back of a tank with a
hose and had two wrenches to take the tank valve cap off. The employee was found
dead at the site of the tank valve. It was later determined by the coroner the
employee was killed due to a flash fire at the location of the valve.
At 8:27 a.m. on August 16, 2023, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were preparing a
meal for lunch in the establishment kitchen. They were using gas ranges and an
oven. The establishment exit doors were locked. A fire started, and they
couldn't escape from the kitchen. There were flammable materials stored along
the exit route. They searched for refuge in the kitchen cooler but died.
At 12:50 p.m. on March 11, 2024, an employee was harvesting strawberries in an
outdoor field.  The employee collapsed as the employee was walking to the lunch
face-first off the roof and landed on the pavement. The employee sustained a
fatal head injury from the impact with the pavement.
At 8:00 a.m. on May 24, 2024, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was preparing to stage materials for a basement foundation on a new residential
building. The employee died from natural causes while performing the job duties.
At 12:45 a.m. on May 23, 2024, a lineman employee of Entergy Louisiana, Inc. was
engaged in power restoration operations when he was found unresponsive in an
elevated aerial unit attached to the work truck. Emergency Medical Services
(EMS) were immediately summoned to the scene, but the employee was pronounced
dead upon their arrival. The coroner and EMS personnel informed the employer
representative that a potential cardiac event may have caused the employee's
death.
At 6:45 a.m. on May 13, 2024, Employee #1, operating a JLG E300 AJP/AJ Boom
Lift, was driving it off a flatbed trailer onto a dock approximately 5 feet
above ground level in a loading/unloading area identified as D4. During the
operation, the lift became high-centered on the flatbed when Employee #1 was
moving in reverse, causing the steering tires to become suspended. As the tires
were suspended, a coworker stepped onto the flatbed in front of the steering
tires, causing the lift to veer left. The coworker then returned to the docking
area, and Employee #1 moved the lift forward, at which point the lift ran off
the left side of the flatbed trailer. Employee #1 was ejected from the extended
platform control box, which was approximately 15-20 feet above the ground. The
troubleshoot lights not working. The employee was working on a removable
corrugated steel grating over a 19.5-foot deep vault.  The vault is used for air
intake and discharge for the hospital building HVAC system. For unknown reasons,
the steel grate fell off its supports, causing the employee to fall with it to
the concrete below.  The employee was killed.
On January 11, 2024, after completing a safety brief, a four-person crew
proceeded the operations of removing and installing the overhead power lines
onto a newly installed 95-foot long concrete utility pole. The crew consisted of
a foreman, Employee #1 (lineman), Coworker #1 (heavy equipment operator),
Coworker #2 (lineman), and Coworker #3 (operator).   Coworker #1 was operating a
derrick digger to remove the second 65-foot long concrete pole. The other
65-foot long concrete pole had been removed from the ground the day prior.
Employee #1 was acting as the Groundman, directing Coworker #1. Coworkers #2 and
#3 were installing the overhead power lines, utilizing an electrical utility
bucket truck. The three 115 kv transmission power lines were not energized while
performing these operations. At approximately 9:30 a.m., after Coworker #1 had
the concrete utility pole cleared off the ground, he started to lower the pole
into the ground. The boom assembly rotated towards the right, allowing the top
end of the utility pole to make contact with an adjacent 46 kv overhead power
line, creating an arc flash. Employee #1 was in contact with the utility pole,
which had the grounding cable still attached, suffering an electrocution.
Employee #1 was killed.
At 2:40 p.m. on January 9, 2024, an employee was cleaning out the rotating auger
on the sand spreader on the rear of his dump truck after his shift.  The
employee was utilizing a piece of wood lathe to clean out the sand from the
spreader, when his arm was caught by the rotating auger, pulling him into the
equipment, causing fatal injuries.  The employee was working alone at the time
of the accident, and weather did not play a part in the accident.
At 7:45 a.m. on January 9, 2024, an employee was walking on an aluminum beam.
The employee suffered an acute heart attack and fell off the beam, resulting in
a fatality.
At 12:42 p.m. on January 10, 2024, an employee was found unresponsive in the
bathroom due to a fentanyl overdose.  The employee was killed.
At 3:39 a.m. on December 21, 2023, Employee #1 was working for a street/highway
construction contractor.  Employee #1 was struck by a car causing fatal
injuries.
At 8:55 a.m. on January 12, 2024, an employee was standing between a street rail
and a trench box. When the excavator was attempting to pick the trench box up to
put into the trench, the road he was on gave way (caved in), and the excavator
fell on its side, which pulled the trench box over on its side and pinned the
employee between the trench box and the street rail. The employee suffered fatal
injuries.
At 10:00 p.m. on January 10, 2024, Employee #1, a 33-year-old male, was
delivering a pizza to a residence. Upon arrival, Employee #1 was robbed at
gunpoint by three assailants and was subsequently shot in the torso several
times. Employee #1 died at the scene as a result of the injuries sustained in
the attack.
At 4:01 p.m. on December 6, 2023, an employee working for a sawmill was removing
wood debris that had fallen between the conveyor belt and a roller on a firewood
processing machine. While reaching for the wood, the employee was caught by and
pulled into the machinery which was running at the time. The employee was
working alone at the time of the incident, and no environmental factors played a
role in the accident. Medical intervention was unsuccessful, and the employee
was pronounced dead at the scene of crushing injuries.
At 8:30 a.m. on November 21, 2023, a log truck was loaded and parked on the
landing. An employee went to the trailer to release the airbrake. While the
EMS performed CPR and was able to get him back briefly, but about 10 minutes
after leaving the store, he was pronounced dead via cardiac arrest.
At 9:00 a.m. on March 22, 2024, Employee #1 had been tuckpointing a residential
building for approximately 4 weeks. Employee #1 was preparing the site and
beginning work. Employee #1 climbed the scaffold/roof. Employee #1 fell from the
scaffold/roof. Employee #1 was unconscious and sustained a broken arm and blunt
force trauma to the head. First responders believe Employee #1 had a seizure as
a result of the head injury. Employee #1 was hospitalized and subsequently died
in the hospital from increased intracranial pressure from the blunt force head
trauma.
At 7:00 a.m. on March 25, 2024, Wildcat Concrete Services arrived on location to
pour the last concrete foundation support for the overpass bridge. As the crew
was prepping the pad, two coworkers were working near the base, while the
employee was working near the top guardrail by the overpass road. Shortly after
the work started, a passenger vehicle, whose driver had fallen asleep, entered
the work zone driving approximately 70-75mph, injuring two and hitting/pinning
the employee against the concrete barrier as the car traversed up the slope. The
employee sustained blunt force trauma to the torso and legs and died from his
injuries.  Two employees also sustained blunt force trauma to the body area and
were hospitalized.
At 8:30 a.m. on March 26, 2024, an employee was offloading skylight boxes from a
company vehicle while inside the bed of a pickup truck and parked on an incline
at a construction site. The employee, a project engineer, was injured when he
was lifting a skylight box weighing approximately 50 pounds by the perforated
box handhold, and the box handle tore from where the employee was pulling the
box.  The employee fell backwards off the tailgate of the pickup truck and
landed on his head.  The tailgate of the pickup truck was open when the employee
fell less than 4 feet onto the concrete/asphalt floor.  He later died on March
31, 2024, from acute subdural hematoma and brain contusions due to blunt force
head trauma.  The factors that contributed to the accident were lack of training
while offloading boxes.
At 3:30 p.m. on March 8, 2024, an employee was working in her classroom, when
she died. According to the death certificate, the employee's death was caused by
heart disease as a consequence of mitral valve prolapse and complication of
third trimester pregnancy.
At 9:30 a.m. on March 23, 2024, the Sole Proprietor and Employee #1 were working
inside of the timber frame barn building, when it collapsed.  The Sole
Proprietor sustained head injuries that resulted in his death.  Employee #1's
left leg was broken during the barn collapse, and he was hospitalized.  The wood
structure was approximately 45 feet long by 25 feet wide, a single story with a
loft.  The crew was using hand tools to deconstruct the barn.  Some temporary
bracing had been installed prior to the demolition work, but there was no
evidence (written or otherwise) that an engineering survey had been conducted.
At 9:45 a.m. on March 28, 2024, Employee #1 was moving grain and needed to open
the gate on the C-1 bin conveyor, but the gate would not open, so Employee #1
began to troubleshoot the gate. When Employee #1 could not effectively
troubleshoot the gate to open, Employee #1 needed to go into the conveyor and
trouble shoot further. Employee #1 went to the control room and locked out the
C-1 conveyor. A coworker was in the control room at the time Employee #1 locked
out the C-1 conveyor. When Employee #1 effectively locked out the C-1 conveyor,
Employee #1 left the control room and inadvertently entered the C-3 conveyor and
began troubleshooting.   The coworker in the control room started the C-3
conveyor to conduct equipment checks for a scheduled train load occurring on
March 29. Once the coworker started the C-3 conveyor, the coworker received an
alarm that the conveyor had shut down. Employee #1 was completely ingested and
dismembered by the conveyor and was killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on March 28, 2024, an employee was installing a number sign over
the dock doors. The employee fell off the ladder. The employee sustained a head
injury causing death.
At 11:10 a.m. on March 27, 2024, two employees appear to have set oil or fumes
in a gun barrel tank on fire using a heat gun. The employees were attempting to
get out of the tank, when it exploded. One employee suffered a concussive
injury, resulting in a fatality.  The other employee suffered 20% burns and was
hospitalized.
At 11:15 a.m. on March 26, 2024, an employee was installing a paint booth
ventilation system in an auto body shop. The employee was caulking a seam
approximately 10 feet above ground on the unit while standing on forklift forks.
The employee fell approximately 10 feet and struck his head, resulting in a head
injury with loss of consciousness. The employee died from his injuries while
hospitalized.
At 12:00 a.m. on March 26, 2024, firefighters were inside a house conducting
firefighting operations on an actively burning structure fire. Firefighter A
informed Firefighter B that he was going to pull more hose. Firefighter B lost
visual, radio, and verbal contact with Firefighter A while inside the structure
operating the nozzle. The employee representative called for an evacuation of
the structure. Firefighters became aware that Firefighter A had not exited the
structure, and a RIT located and extracted Firefighter A from the structure.
Firefighter A was briefly treated by EMS personnel before being airlifted to
Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center, where he died on March 29.
At 12:33 p.m. on April 1, 2024, an employee working as a tow truck driver for a
24-hour towing service was dispatched to tow an abandoned vehicle. The employee
the roof, the employee lost his balance, fell, hit a part of the home, and then
fell to the ground 15.8 feet.  The employee was killed.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 31, 2024, Employee #1 and a coworker were loading a
BOMAG compactor onto a trailer partially on the shoulder of Anawana Lake Road in
Monticello NY. Employee #1 was struck and killed by a motorist traveling east on
Anawana Lake Road.
At 2:02 p.m.  on October 13, 2023, an employee passed out while hiking and was
killed.
At 9:00 a.m. on January 30, 2024, Employee #1 was removing shipping packaging
for components for a roof solar power generation system, when s/he fell through
a skylight of a storage shed building.   Employee #1 was working on a 2-3 inch
12-pitch roof with four skylights made up of semi-translucent fiberglass.  The
roof was a sheet metal roof that was approximately 60 feet long by 40 feet high.
The four skylights were approximately 6 feet long by 3 feet wide and were
located along the peak in the middle of the roof.   Employee #1 was working with
two supervisors to install a solar panel system to generate electrical power.
The weather conditions were sunny and dry.   Employee #1 was removing shipping
packaging (cardboard boxes and packing material from various components) and
bringing the components to the two supervisors for installation on the roof.
Employee #1 was asked by management if he would want to use personal fall
protection that was available on the site.   Employee #1 fell approximately 21
feet to the ground level receiving severe head injuries.  Employee #1 was
transported to the hospital, where he died on February 1, 2024.
At 7:38 a.m. on August 4, 2023, an employee arrived to work and, when talking to
a co-worker, he collapsed. He was pronounced dead at the scene at 8:12 a.m. The
employee died of a heart attack.
At 12:00 a.m. on January 29, 2024, two employees were attempting to set up lane
closure signs for a work zone. One employee was flagging traffic to merge over,
while the second employee was at the back of the vehicle getting the large arrow
sign that was attached to the truck ready. The flagger was struck by a vehicle,
and then the vehicle struck the arrow sign causing the second employee to be
crushed between the arrow sign and the vehicle.  The flagger was hospitalized to
treat unspecified injuries, and the second employee was killed.
On February 1, 2024, an employee working as a heavy truck driver for a freight
company was delivering a load of corn mix feed. The employee opened the rear
door and started the belly conveyor. He attempted to cross over behind the truck
just as the load started to empty out and force the rear door to swing. The
employee was killed when he was struck by the door and crushed between the door
and a bin wall.
At 11:45 a.m. on February 1, 2024, an employee working as a truck driver for a
waste disposal service was in the process of removing the tarp off their
roll-off truck. The employee was conducting unloading operations on the trash
deck of a county landfill. While removing the tarp, the employee was engulfed in
a sawdust cloud causing him to abruptly travel across the front of his truck
into the opposite direction to escape the dust cloud. Simultaneously, in the
same direction of travel, approximately 25 feet away, a coworker was driving
another roll-off truck backing into their directed spot. The coworker driving
the other truck unknowingly struck the employee. The employee was wearing dark
clothing over his high visibility PPE. The employee was died due to crushing
injuries and blunt trauma to the torso and neck with visceral, vascular and
skeletal injuries.
At 12:30 p.m. on February 2, 2024, Employee #1 was working for a general
contractor.  Employee #1 was removing dirt in the basement level of a commercial
building which resulted in a partial collapse. Employee #1 was struck by the
falling materials, resulting in a fatality.
At 1:00 p.m. on February 1, 2024, an employee working for a telecommunications
company was splicing fiber optic cable. The employee was discovered unresponsive
on the floor of a work trailer. The employee had died from cardiac arrest.
At 9:45 a.m. on January 31, 2024, Employee #1 was supervising the operation of
separating two delivered and stacked 40 cubic yard roll-off storage containers.
The operation was in the second phase of righting the second container, which
was originally upside down and had already been flipped onto its right side
using a chain attached to a bucket loader boom. The first half of the
uprighting/flipping procedure was completed. The unit was on its right side, the
front being the forward wall containing the cabling bar. Employee #1 had walked
around to the opposite side of the container from the position of the bucket
loader. The doors for both containers were in the second container. Employee #1

the face and head by the 150 pound forklift's fork.  The employee was
