employee was removed from life support and died.  The employee suffered blunt
force injures to the head: a.) cutaneous abrasions; b.) subscapular and galea
hemorrhage; c.) multiple skull fractures; d.) subdural hemorrhage; e.) cerebral
contusions.
At 9:30 a.m. on January 26, 2023, an employee and coworkers were cutting down a
white ash tree when it snapped near the cut line. The bottom section of the tree
swung up and struck the employee in the head and face. The top section of the
tree, above where it snapped, fell over on top of the employee. The employee was
crushed and killed.
At 2:29 p.m. on January 29, 2023, an employee was picking product to be stocked
on the sales floor. The employee collapsed and died. It is preliminarily
believed to be cardiovascular in nature.
At 4:45 p.m. on January 30, 2023, an employee was installing a tile roof when he
fell to the ground and subsequently died from his injuries.
At 2:30 p.m. on January 23, 2023, Employee #1, Employee #2, and Employee #3 were
working at a farm. Just prior to this incident, a former coworker shot and
killed multiple people at another nearby farm where he had worked previously.
The former coworker then went with a firearm to the farm where Employee #1,
Employee #2, and Employee #3  were working and shot and killed all three
employees.
On January 25, 2023, an employee was performing maintenance on a Volvo L70H
wheel loader that was experiencing a hydraulic oil leak.  The employee was
working from underneath the loader boom and the boom fell and crushed him.  The
employee was killed as a result of unspecified injuries to his abdomen.
At 12:00 a.m. on November 29, 2022, an employee was performing post maintenance
testing on a scrubber tank at a natural gas power plant. The employee used a
fixed ladder to access the elevated working platform approximately 7 feet above
the ground to vent the natural gas scrubber filter for the unit. The employee
was in a squatting or kneeling position for approximately 20 to 30 seconds while
operating a quarter turn vent valve before he stood up and turned to exit the
platform. The employee opened the safety gate and rotated to exit the platform
to descend the ladder. However, the employee lost consciousness before
descending the ladder and  instead cartwheeled sideways off the platform and
fell 7 feet, landing on his head. Because the employee lost consciousness, he
did not give any verbal indication when he fell or make any attempt to arrest
the fall. The employee was transported to the local hospital before being
transferred to a larger medical center. The employee sustained head trauma and
fractured neck vertebrae, and died from his injuries on December 1, 2022.
At 3:00 a.m. on January 30, 2023, an employee was taking trash to a receptacle
located outside of a facility.  As the employee was going outside, a contractor
was using a highway use dump vehicle to spread salt in the driveway and parking
areas of the facility.  As the employee opened a double door, the vehicle began
to back up in the direction of the employee. The employee was struck and pushed
by the truck for approximately 10-15 feet before the employee fell.  When the
employee was on the ground, the truck drove over the employee.  The driver of
the truck noticed that they had struck something, stopped, and began to drive
forward, driving over the employee again.  The employee was killed.
At 5:30 a.m. on January 19, 2023, an employee was standing next to a trailer bed
when crane crawler mats fell on and crushed him to death.
At 2:00 a.m. on January 22, 2023, an employee self-admitted to the hospital
after experiencing respiratory problems and chest pain.  Employee died from non
work-related health issues.
At 12:30 p.m. on January 31, 2023, Employee #1 was performing cathodic
protection maintenance on a 4-inch natural gas pipeline.  Employee #1 removed
the resin coating off the external portion of the pipeline to test the hull
thickness of the pipeline.  While removing the coating, the pipeline exploded.
Employee #1 was killed by immolation. Employee #2 and Employee #3 were injured
from the heat, blast and vapors from the explosion and were hospitalized for
treatment.
At 2:00 p.m. on January 31, 2023, an employee was stocking shelves with product.
A former coworker, entered the store and shot the employee.  The employee was
killed.
On January 24, 2023, an employee was tightening belly straps on stacks of PVC
pipe. The belly straps were not level across, and the top two bundles began to
tip from the middle, and the bundled pipe fell on top of him.  The suffered
multiple fractures in the lumber region, ribs, and pelvis.  The employee was
hospitalized and died three days later as a result of the injuries.
At 12:00 noon on January 30, 2023, an employee was making repairs on a warehouse
roof when he accidently stepped on and fell through the roof's skylight. The
asphalt sealant inside) was pulling away and uphill, when power and control to
the truck was lost and it rolled backwards.  The employee was behind and was
warned that the vehicle and trailer were rolling toward him.  The employee began
to move, when he slipped on the wet asphalt and fell onto the ground and into
the path of the trailer which crushed him.  The employee was killed.
At 7:45 a.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee was unloading fumigation chambers
at an almond processing facility using a forklift. The employee noticed that the
pallet conveyor was malfunctioning. The injured worker got off his forklift and
attempted to wipe off the sensor, but the pallets still did not advance. As he
turned away, the pallet conveyor moved and a pallet crushed his right hand. The
employee was hospitalized  to treat a right ring fingertip amputation.
At 5:30 p.m. on January 29, 2022, an employee was exiting a reception area when
she fell in the adjacent hallway. The employee struck her head on the wall
before hitting the floor causing multiple injuries. The employee fractured her
right femur and fractured her left wrist and was hospitalized.
An employee was working in an outdoorsman retail store when he was exposed to
customers and coworkers infected with COVID-19. The employee contracted
COVID-19, was hospitalized and subsequently died at 8:00 a.m. on July 9, 2022.
At 8:45 a.m. on July 9, 2022, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were standing on a
fully extended 42-foot JLG forklift telehandler while performing painting
operations. Employee #1 was killed and Employee #2 was injured, when the
motorized boom truck overturned.  The two employees were transported to
Schneider Hospital for treatment. Employee #1 was pronounced dead at 9:24 a.m.
from head trauma.
At 5:44 p.m. on June 27, 2022, an employee was standing/riding on the folded,
raised side frames of the grain drill while attempting to lift a phone line so
that the grain drill could pass underneath. The employee lost his balance and
fell approximately 10 feet from the side frame to the ground below, hitting his
head. Two other coworkers were riding on the drill at the time and were exposed
to the same fall hazard.
At 6:45 p.m. on April 20, 2022, an employee was preparing to collect his
personal belongings at the end of his shift. The employee collapsed due to a
medically related illness and died.
At 12:27 p.m. on July 15, 2022, an employee was performing site clearing on a
residential plot of land. A coworker was operating an excavator nearby to bring
down trees onto a tree pile. The employee was tasked with cutting the felled
trees into smaller pieces that could be transported off site after the excavator
had knocked down a few trees. The employee was to stand in a safe zone while the
excavator would then bring down a few more trees. The employee was to stand in a
safe zone until the coworker operating the excavator gave him approval to
approach the pile and start cutting.  The coworker began to work on felling two
trees next to each other, and after felling the first tree he verified that the
employee was in the safe zone before he started working to bring the second tree
down onto the pile.  However, the employee moved out of the safe zone and was on
the tree pile when the second tree was felled onto the pile by the excavator.
The employee was struck and killed by the falling tree, sustaining blunt force
trauma to the head.
At 1:45 p.m. on July 18, 2022, an employee was preparing to replace an ice
machine at a retail store. The employee searched for the electrical panel to
de-energize the ice machine but was unable to locate it. The employee was
employed by a refrigeration equipment company and did not work at the retail
store. The employee asked a supervisor at the store to help find the electrical
panel but the supervisor was unable to help him. The employee decided to replace
section of pipe closer to the excavator. The employee then approached the
excavator to communicate with the foreman. The foreman saw the employee
approaching and set down the excavator bucket. The excavator was not turned off
nor was the pilot shutoff lever pulled. Due to the weather and wind conditions,
the excavator window and door were closed at the time. The employee was standing
in front of the left track and attempted to verbally communicate with the
foreman. The foreman opened the cab door and the wind slammed the door against
the side of the machine. The excavator lurched forward twice, initially knocking
the employee to the ground, then running him over up to the waist. The foreman
pulled the safety lever to disengage the machine. The pipe layer yelled for the
foreman to back up in order to free the employee. The foreman disengaged the
lever and used the bucket to raise the tracks up. The pipe layer pulled the
employee out from under the track. The coworkers covered the employee with
jackets until emergency personnel arrived at the site. The employee was taken to
the hospital but died due to his injuries.
At 12:00 noon on September 14, 2022, an employee was working as a day laborer
hired by a family friend to assist in framing a residential home. The employee
was completing the framing of an exterior wall and went to retrieve bracing
material nearby when he walked too close to the edge of a portal of the level.
The employee lost his balance and fell, headfirst, through the portal nine feet
onto a concrete pad. The employee was conscious but was gasping for air and was
bleeding from the nose and mouth. The employee was laid down at the site for
approximately an hour with no medical aid rendered. Later, the employee was
attempting to exit the confined space at the end of the shift, when the employee
reported to the hole watch that he could not breath. The hole watch told the
employee to turn on the emergency bottle. The employee then reported that he was
on the bottle. The hole watch told the employee to connect to the emergency
escape line. The employee refused and attempted to climb out of the confined
space. The employee climbed approximately 30 feet up a fixed vertical ladder.
The employee stopped responding to the attendant and other exterior employees. A
man down alarm was called, and emergency rescue operations were attempted. The
employee was extracted from the confined space. CPR was performed. An AED was
applied, and the AED advised not to administer a shock. The employee was
transported by ambulance to a nearby hospital emergency department, where he was
pronounced dead. The employee was killed by probable asphyxia due to nitrogen
gas exposure and/or oxygen deprivation.
At 5:30 a.m. on September 16, 2019, an employee was throwing pistachios into a
fan while working as a farm worker. The fan suction pulled the employee's hand
into it, causing his right thumb to contact the fan blade. The employee's thumb
was amputated and he was hospitalized.
At 12:30 a.m. on October 17, 2022, an employee was cleaning out excess hot
asphalt from a truck dump bed.  A highway paver machine struck the tail gate of
the truck and crushed the employee between the tail gate and the truck dump bed.
The employee was killed.
At 5:00 a.m. on February 7, 2023, Employee #1 was descending a ladder from the
second deck to get to the main deck. Employee #1 was performing maintenance on
the second deck with two coworkers. Employee #1 did not step on the last two
rungs of the ladder and fell into the Mississippi River on the side of the dock
barge where he was working. Employee #1 did not emerge from the river. Employee
#1 drowned.  As of February 21, 2023, his body had not been found.
At 11:30 a.m. on February 20, 2023, an employee entered the hazard zone without
protective gloves on and may have been removing the hook from the new pole. No
coworkers were looking at the employee at moment of contact with energized
equipment. Employees had just finished setting and tamping the pole. The
employee reached for and grabbed the hook and was electrocuted. The employee was
killed.
At 7:00 p.m. on January 28, 2023, an employee, a nail technician, was giving
pedicures to a customer and his girlfriend when another man came into the salon
and started arguing with the customer. The customer brandished a gun and tried
to shoot the man who had come in but missed and shot the employee instead. The
employee died from his wounds.
At 10:58 a.m. on February 19, 2023, a volunteer fire fighter recruit was
participating in a fire fighter survival training course at a training center.
The course was located at the third level of a three-story metal storage
container. During the confidence course, the employee went unconscious and was
removed from the area and medical attention was rendered.  The employee died at
the scene.
At 1:40 p.m. on February 14, 2023, an employee was pinned under the wheels of a
skid steer that was being loaded onto a transport truck by the skidder operator.
The employee was killed.
At 8:30 a.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee was installing waterproof paper on
a roof when he slipped and fell to the frozen ground below. The employee
incurred severe head trauma trauma to his upper torso and died.
At 8:00 a.m. on September 8, 2021, an employee was performing roofing work on a
two story multiple family home when he fell from the roof. The employee suffered
multiple fractures and was killed.
At 2:45 p.m. on August 18, 2022, an employee was taping off a bathroom to begin
bathtub refinishing work. The employee had not yet begun the refinishing work
when he died.  The death certificate indicated the employee died from natural
causes.
At 3:30 p.m. on February 20, 2023, an employee was loading bundles of metal
mesh. The employee was on top of a boom spreader,  which was mounted on a
forklift and not secured, when it slid off and fell from the top of a trailer
low bed.   The employee fell and  was killed due to head trauma.
At 2:30 p.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee was behind a company van,
preparing to load a piece of equipment.  A coworker backed up the van into the
employee, crushing his body into a railing and a concrete wall.
At 5:50 p.m. on January 4, 2023, an employee was delivering concrete to a
construction site in a 33,000-pound Advance Mixer cement truck filled with
26,443 pounds of concrete when he got stuck heavy mud at an outdoor worksite. A
coworker was operating a John Deere 650K Crawler Dozer and was attempting to
pull the cement truck out of the mud. One end of a 15-foot braided wire rope was
attached to the front-end tow plate of the cement truck and the other end of the
wire rope was attached to an aftermarket Buyers 8-ton combination hitch
attachment on the blade of the dozer. The four grade eight bolts securing the
hitch failed causing the hitch to snap towards the windshield of the cement
truck and struck the employee. The employee died due to blunt force trauma to
the face and head.
At 5:45 p.m. on February 22, 2023, an employee was standing and talking with a
coworker. They were standing about 5-6 feet apart from each other, approximately
40-feet away from where a branch was on fire on a powerline. While standing
there, a branch from another tree broke, striking the primary powerline. That
powerline broke and struck the employee to the ground. The employee was
electrocuted (14,400 volt powerline).
At 6:30 a.m. on February 11, 2023, an employee was loading material onto a roof.
The employee feel through the plastic section of the roof. The employee was
killed by a 25-foot fall.
At 9:30 a.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee was performing irrigation work
activities on row crops. The employee collapsed and was unresponsive.  Emergency
services transported the employee to the Modesto hospital, where he died. The
employee was killed due to a brain aneurysm.
At 3:00 p.m. on February 22, 2023, an employee was installing taller electrical
poles to make room for telecommunication lines. A line let loose from a sleeve
to adjoin two lines and fell to the ground.  The east side of the line was

re-closure.  The foreman stated that the re-closure was open and the line was

from the east pole with the use of PPE. The employee was electrocuted and
killed.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 19, 2023, an employee was working alone in the Mach 1
Corp facility.  He was working on a laser cutting machine, possibly making
internal adjustments.  The employee had opened an exterior sliding panel to gain

interlocks that were meant to prevent the machine from operating if they were
opened. At some point in time, while working inside the laser cutting machine,

body was not discovered until 5:45 a.m. on February 20, 2023.
At 3:00 p.m. on February 20, 2023, an employee was killed by carbon monoxide

At 11:00 a.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee working as a drill operator for

At 8:30 a.m. on February 21, 2023, an employee working as a manager at a gas
of a Liugong CLG936E excavator to raise and lower a submersible pump from
cylindrical pilings. The employees were standing under the excavator bucket that
was elevated approximately 6 feet from the ground attaching the pump's hose to
the bucket when the operator exited the running excavator. The unoccupied
excavator's bucket dropped down and struck the employees. One employee was
struck in the head by the bucket and was killed. The other employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputation.
At 12:30 p.m. on July 11, 2022, Employee #1 (the owner), Employee #2, and
Employee #3 were bringing down a LadderVator to disassemble it, as the roofing
job was nearing completion. As Employee #1 was pulling the LadderVator away from
the building, he lost control of it, and it fell into a 14.4KV powerline.
Employees #2 and #3 tried to assist with the ladder and assist Employee #1.
Employee #1 was electrocuted, and the two other employees received critical
electricity-related injuries and were hospitalized.
At 8:50 a.m. on December 12, 2022, an employee was clearing shingles and debris
from a steep sloped roof. The employee was not attached to a lifeline and fell
approximately 22 feet to a concrete curb. Employee suffered fatal head injuries.
At 1:00 p.m. on December 13, 2022, an employee was transporting and delivering

on the ground. The employee was working alone and was seen at the customers site
connecting his lines to fill the propane tank. The employee had shoveled some
snow to gain access to the tank. At 4:40 p.m. the customer's employee was
leaving work and spotted the delivery driver on the ground between the propane
tank and the propane truck. The truck was still running and the valves were
still connected to truck and tank so the customer turned off the truck and
closed the valves. CPR was administered and emergency services were called. The
employee was pronounced dead at the scene due to a heart attack.
At 12:00 noon on December 15, 2022, an employee, a public works worker, was
using a SCL 800 Leaf Collection vacuum being pulled behind an International dump

truck but failed to put the truck in neutral, or he put it in neutral partially

employee moved quickly from behind the vacuum trailer and tried to re-enter the
truck. The employee lost his balance, fell and was struck by the 22,000-pound
trailer. The employee died at the scene from a crushing injury to the head. The
truck traveled up the road diagonally, went over a curb, crossed a sidewalk went
down an embankment and struck a tree. The towing company driver stated that when
he and a state trooper went to the cab of the truck, they found the truck in
drive and the parking brake was set.
At 8:15 a.m. on December 16, 2022, an employee climbed a ladder to gain access
to the HVAC unit on a church's roof. The employee was standing on the roof when
he fell 10 feet 6 inches to ground. The employee died due to blunt force trauma.
At 12:00 noon on December 15, 2023, an employee and four coworkers were
installing upgraded radios and antennas on a telecommunications transmitting and

of the up tower crew that was preparing to raise a hybrid line further up the
tower. The hybrid line was attached to the tower by a hoisting grip which failed
causing the rigging and hybrid line to fall. The employee was struck and
entangled by the line and the rigging. The employee suffered broken bones,
contusions, crushing injuries, internal injuries, and lacerations that resulted
in his death.
At 4:00 p.m. on December 14, 2022, an employee was operating an excavator
clearing a site in preparation for construction of a multi-family residential

trapped him in the excavator. The employee was engulfed and died due to
asphyxia.
At 1:00 p.m. on December 16, 2022, an employee was monitoring the start-up and
operations of a high-pressure International Boiler Works Water Tube Generator
Boiler in preparation for an anticipated winter storm. A threaded plug on the

and allowed the release of high temperature and high pressure steam. The steam
sprayed the employee and resulted in severe burns to approximately 80% his body.
The employee was transported to the hospital but died due complications from the
burns.
At 2:50 p.m. on December 16, 2022, a crew of four employees were excavating a
trench to install concrete inlet/outlet boxes for underground utility services.
Two employees were working in the trench, one employee was operating the John
Deere 160G Excavator, and one employee was outside of the trench. The crew was
aligning the concrete box that was approximately 41 and 1/2 inches in length and
37 inches wide with the other piping. The concrete box was rigged to the arm of
the excavator for lowering it in place. The excavator operator lowered the
concrete box and exited the excavator to discuss with the crew what adjustments
needed to be made. The operator went to get back in the excavator to lift the

arm. This caused the box to lift upwards and swing forward, away from excavator
cab, and struck Employee #1. The operator attempted to correct the error and
swung the arm back the other direction, towards the excavator cab, causing the

to crushing injuries.
At 9:00 a.m. on July 21, 2022, an employee was walking under a roof truss

At 9:15 p.m. on December 13, 2022, an employee was stocking shelves in a

he suffered a heart attack and died.
At 1:30 p.m. on November 23, 2022, an employee was experienced a personal health

employee was working alone and was found dead. The employee was killed by a
brain hemorrhage.
At 12:00 noon on December 10, 2022, an employee was walking in a medical supply
manufacturer's warehouse when he was struck by a forklift carrying a load. The
employee suffered a head injury when his head struck the concrete floor, was
hospitalized, and was pronounced dead the following day.
At 3:00 p.m. on December 5, 2022, an employee was driving a dump truck on
logging road when he suffered a medical emergency causing the truck to go off
the road and roll over. The employee died due to the combination of the medical
emergency and trauma from the roll-over.
At 5:10 p.m. on December 17, 2022, an employee was picking oranges in an orchard
using an18-foot aluminum ladder to reach the oranges. The employee was moving
the ladder when it made contact with overhead powerlines, and he was
electrocuted.
At 2:00 p.m. on December 1, 2022, an employee was cutting a hazardous maple tree
that had fallen on power lines. When the employee made his cut, the pressure on
the power line was released and caused the tree trunk to stand upright for a
moment before falling. When seeing this development, the employee decided to
change his escape route at the last moment and turned directly into the path of
the falling tree. The tree fell on the employee, and he was killed due to the
blunt force trauma.
At 1:00 p.m. on December 19, 2022, an employee was assisting with truck
refueling and was positioned behind the 2007 Freightliner Business Class M2
truck in a manner that did not allow the driver to see him. The driver began
backing the vehicle and the employee was struck and run over and suffered fatal
injuries.
At 7:15 a.m. on January 30, 2023, an employee was guiding an industrial truck
operator carrying a large, 4,000-pound, metal pile driving attachment to place
it in the garage area when the attachment swung forward and crushed the employee
between the attachment and a parked trailer. The employee died due to a crushed

At 10:30 a.m. on February 17, 2023, an employee fell while he was installing

The employee was installing some blocks on the edge of the wall. This is

unlicensed contractor. The employee, day laborer, was an employee of the

accident occurred.
An employee was working in a county social services department performing
administrative duties when she developed COVID-19 symptoms. The employee's
symptoms worsened, and she was hospitalized with a COVID-19 on January 25, 2023.
At 4:30 p.m. on March 9, 2023, an employee was fighting a forest wild fire,
while riding an ATV.  The ATV ran over two dead tree limbs on the ground and
overturned.  The employee was killed when pinned underneath the ATV.
At 1:15 p.m. on February 2, 2023, an employee working as a truck driver for
freight business was standing on the driver side of trailer tightening a cargo
on a deenergized CM-22 Network Protector that was connected to an energized
2,000 kilovolt-ampere (kVA) transformer. Faulty insulators caused an electrical
explosion and the employee was struck by an arc-flash. The employee died from
severe burns and a blood clot.
At 1:40 p.m. on July 12, 2023, an employee was performing roofing work during
elevated temperatures. The employee became dizzy and collapsed while working on
top of the roof. The employee was killed.
At 2:15 p.m. on July 27, 2023, an employee was operating forklift to get an
empty pallet to bring back to the fabrication area. While operating the forklift
on a gravel surface with a significant slope, the employee appeared to have
taken the turn while moving too fast, causing the forklift to roll over onto its
side. The employee was not wearing a seat belt and was caught between the
forklift and the ground. The employee was killed. The Harris County Medical
Examiner's office did not have any information for the employee.
On July 26, 2023, an employee was hired and completed orientation.  At 6:30 a.m.
on July 28, 2023, the employee arrived onsite to begin work as a concrete
finisher. The employee was tasked with setting concrete forms, while awaiting
the arrival of concrete trucks.  During this time, the employee was observed
stumbling and was directed by the foreman to sit in his personal vehicle to cool
off.  The concrete trucks arrived at noon, and the employee was tasked with
finishing the concrete by smoothing out curbing with a finishing trowel.  At
2:00 p.m., the lead man observed the employee staggering while walking to his
vehicle. The lead man assisted the employee to his vehicle and applied ice to
him.  The lead man contacted emergency services.  The employee was unconscious
but breathing upon the ambulance's departure from the site.  The employee died
while enroute to the hospital.
At 1:30 p.m. on July 24, 2023, an employee was a welder working on reskinning a
cone-shaped, above-ground storage tank.  The employee was connected to a cable
grab fall protection system.  It was alleged that the fall protection system
failed, and the employee suffered a 40-foot fall to inside of the tank.  The
employee was killed.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 13, 2023, Employee #1 (a 55-year-old male) was working
alongside two coworkers, tasked with servicing ATM machines. The employer
dispatched employees to this location twice per week to service the ATM machine.
When Employee #1 exited the armored truck, he was approached by an armed robber,
who shot and killed Employee #1. The investigation discovered that new employees
wee offered a bullet proof vest after 90 days of service; however, the use of
these vests was not required by the employer. The investigation also discovered
that previous robberies had taken place at this location.
At 8:00 a.m. on July 28, 2023, Employee #1 was loading furniture by hand for an
assigned route. Employee #1 felt ill after loading 4 or 5 pieces of furniture
onto the delivery truck for 30 minutes. Employee #1 told coworkers he was having
difficulty breathing. Employee #1 died during emergency transport to the local
hospital. Employee #1 died due to the heat conditions.
At 1:45 p.m. on July 28, 2023, an employee had just taken a break to drink water
and use the bathroom. Prior to this, the employee had been removing boxes from
the rear of a truck at the loading area of the warehouse. The employee suffered
heat-related and carbon monoxide-related exposure, which led to multiple organ

zone, struck, and killed Employee #1 and injured Employee #2.  Employee #2
incurred unspecified injuries and was hospitalized for treatment.
At 12:40 p.m. on November 17, 2021, an employee was climbing a non-extended
extension ladder to access a piece of equipment.  While stepping off the ladder
to access the room's landing area, the employee slipped and fell to the ground
below.  The employee was hospitalized for 7 days to treat fractures to his foot
and lower back vertebrae.
At 6:03 a.m. on October 12, 2021, an employee was walking down a loading dock
where a coworker was moving pallets out of a trailer at a freight warehouse.
The coworker operating the forklift was maneuvering to avoid a pallet on the
ground and he was not looking back while backing out of a trailer. The forklift
struck the employee who walking down the loading dock. The employee suffered
left ankle fracture and was hospitalized.
At 12:50 p.m. on January 28, 2022, an employee worked as a Carpenter Framer for
a Construction company. The employee had climbed a ladder to the second level in
order to frame the pitched roof section of a single-family residence. When the
employee was walking on the second level approximately 9 feet from the ground,
he stated he had stepped on sawdust and slipped. The employee fell and hit his
upper torso on a rafter. Although he knew he was hurt, he climbed down the
ladder. Coworkers alerted the company owner and immediately called an ambulance.
The employee was hospitalized with five fractured ribs on his left side.  The
employee remained in the hospital for approximately three days.
At 9:00 a.m. on January 21, 2022, an employee was operating a lathe machine when
he bypassed the interlock device and removed the guard to continue working. The
employee caught his hand in the lathe incurring a severe hand injury and
requiring hospitalization.
At 12:00 a.m. on March 22, 2022, a sales employee was found slumped over the
counter at a business which does retail for the power sports industry.  The
employee died of natural causes at the counter.
At 10:30 p.m. on November 11, 2021, an employee was operating a loom. While
reaching into the loom, he accidentally hit its pedal, which activated the
machine and injured his torso. An ambulance transported the employee to a
hospital, where he was hospitalized to treat a collapsed lung and multiple
broken ribs. The full list of injuries included: pneumothorax, small right-sided
contusion, right lung, right sixth rib fracture, right displaced seventh rib
fracture, right eighth rib fracture, right ninth rib fracture, right lateral
chest abrasions, and right flank abrasion.
The gravity fed chute/spout was connected to the grain elevator leg to Grain
Silo #2. The chutes lower end was attached by bolts to the grain bin lid. The
lid rested on top of the grain bin.  An employee was standing on the lid on top
of Grain Silo #2. The employee was not wearing any PFAS. There was a guardrail
system encompassing the top of the grain bin.  At approximately 3:00 p.m. on
April 6, 2022, the employee removed an observation plate and chute choke
indicator to look inside the gravity fed chute, which is located on the lower
end of the chute, to find blockage using his phone and flashlight. He sent
photos to the maintenance supervisor. At approximately 3:15 p.m., the supervisor
requested the assistance of a crane service. The crane was on site at
approximately 4:00 p.m. and conducted a lift test. At approximately 4:30 p.m.,
two other maintenance employees were lifted up in a man basket by the crane to
the north side of chute for inspection and possible repair.  At 5:00 p.m., the
maintenance employees removed a section of the top plate and began to lower the
plate to the employee, when the chute collapsed, subsequently falling.  The
employee and the chute/spout landed on the concrete ground between Grain Silo #1
and Grain Silo #2. The employee fell 95 feet to his death. The fatality was
confirmed by North Scott County EMS.
Kyle Lane, EHS Manager, stated that the employee was walking with a coworker,
and that the employee was returning a ladder to its storage area. At 6:45 a.m.
on April 6, 2022, while the employee and coworker were walking, the employee
collapsed. Emergency personal arrived at the scene and were unable to revive
him. Coroner report listed heart failure.
At 9:00 a.m. on January 12, 2022, an employee was cleaning a food filler
dispensing head on  40 ounce line in the entr�e production area. The employee
was using her hand to clean the bottom side of the dispensing head when her left
index finger contacted the metal on the bottom. The employee partially amputated

At 9:00 a.m. on February 2, 2022, an employee was attending a 4-hour class
required by the employer prior to hire. The employee was on top of scaffolding,
attending training on scaffolding and fire watch.  The employee complained of
feeling light-headed and collapsed on the scaffolding due to a heart attack.
At 10:05 p.m. on November 10, 2021, an employee was working for a firm that
fabricated structural metal components. He was operating a model number SE07536
Hill Acme Metal Worker hydraulic single-end punch. It had serial number
86SE-040-01. He was using the machine to punch holes in a piece of flat steel to
make a larger hole. The steel plate, 0.1875 in by 4 in by 20 in (4.8 mm by 101.6
by 508 mm), was to become part of a lifting device. The employee was operating
the punch's jog toggle switch with one hand while he held the plate with his
other hand. The only guarding on the hydraulic single-end punch was the
stripper, which was not adjusted to have an opening less than 0.25 inch (6.35
mm). There was open access to the punch in the front. As the employee engaged
the punch, a piece of metal projected out toward the employee and struck him on
the left side of his neck. He turned around and yelled at a nearby coworker. The
coworker grabbed a first aid kit and provided items requested by the employee.
The employee was driven to the local emergency room by the supervisor and the
coworker. The employer was later transported to another facility. He had
suffered a traumatic penetrating injury. He was hospitalized.
At 2:00 p.m. on April 6, 2022, two employees were performing well servicing on a
salt water disposal well. The mobile service rig turned over, fatality injuring
one employee, a floorhand who was working on the ground, and seriously injuring
employee was pinned against the concrete wall at his knees. The employee
incurred injuries to his legs that required hospitalization which led to a
double leg amputation at the knee.
At 5:30 p.m. on January 28, 2022, an employee was drying cars off in car wash
line of a car wash when he walked onto the conveyor system which was missing a
plate. The employee tripped and fell in front of a car coming down the line and
was run over by the vehicle. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured
leg.
At 2:00 p.m. on May 3, 2022, an employee who worked as an Archivist for the
National Personal Records Center tested positive for COVID-19. The employee
experienced COVID-19 symptoms on April 30, 2022 and tested positive on May 2,
2022. A coworker tested positive on May 4, 2022. Information regarding
engineering, administrative and personal protective equipment controls for
COVID-19 are not included in the narrative.
At 5:00 a.m. on January 18, 2022, an employee was stepping out of an elevator
when the elevator malfunctioned and did not stop flush with the floor. The
employee fell 18 inches from the elevator to the floor. The employee was
hospitalized to treat fractures to his left knee and left shoulder.
At 4:10 a.m. on May 5, 2022, an employee was performing work as a drill
operator.  The drill collar struck the employee in his upper body and killed
him.

On September 16, 2021, an employee who worked as a Registered Nurse for a

At 9:10 a.m. on February 23, 2022, an employee was working at an onion farm. He
was packing onions in a packing machine. An onion got stuck in the conveyor, and
the employee reached in to pull it out. The thumb on his left hand was
amputated. He was treated without hospitalization.
At 1:30 p.m. on December 27, 2021, two employees worked in spray painting
operations on a ship. At some point, the hose line became clogged with debris
and paint material. The employees poured paint thinner into the hose to attempt
to clear the clog. Employee #1 held the hose line while Employee #2 regulated
the air pressure in the line. The pressure became great enough in the line that
it jerked out of Employee #1's hands and released the paint and paint thinner
mixture in the line out onto an operating kerosene powered heater (DeWalt
Kerosene portable torpedo heater). The paint and thinner mixture caught fire and
both employees received burns to their hands, legs, and abdomens.  Both
employees were hospitalized for treatment.
At 2:25 p.m. on February 24, 2022, an employee was working as a cabinet maker
and bench carpenter for a firm that manufactured wood kitchen cabinets and
countertops. He was operating a Powermatic model number 60HH jointer, with
serial number 180160HH2648. The jointer was unguarded. The employee was cutting
eight or nine pieces of wood. The last piece was a 1.5-inch by 3.5-inch (38-mm
by 89-mm) piece of wood. As he was pushing the material over the blades, the
middle finger on his left hand slipped off the material. It came into contact
with a blade or the blades, and it was cut by the machine. The employee suffered
the partial amputation of that finger. He was taken to a local hospital for
treatment. He was not hospitalized. The employee notified the Division of the
injury on March 14, 2022, and the employer notified the division of the injury
on March 15, 2022. The Division arrived at the site to start the investigation
on March 15, 2022.
At 5:30 a.m. on January 28, 2022, an employee was moving a forklift into
position to change out a dust collection bag when it came into contact with the
auger on the bottom of the hopper. The contact resulted in the auger assembly
breaking off from its mount. The employee got off the forklift and was
attempting to move the electrically operated auger assembly when his hand made
contact with the auger that was still moving inside. The employee suffered an
amputation of his right middle fingertip and was treated without
hospitalization.
At approximately 2:00 p.m. on November 29, 2021, an employee was in the process
of clearing/ unclogging the concrete pump, which required him to turn the pump
off, then raise the hood on the concrete pump/ motor, and then use his hands/
manually turn the belt pully. After the employee used his hands/ manually turned
the belt pully, he alleged that he restarted the pump, using the key/ ignition
switch on the control panel.  He then unintentionally placed his hand onto the
drive chain, subsequently resulting in the amputation of three of his
fingertips. The amputation of three of his fingertips on his right hand and was
hospitalized to treat these injuries.
At approximately 3:00 p.m. on February 8, 2022, an employee was involved in
performing minor job duties at the construction project.  The employee was asked
by his supervisor to place caulking above all canopy areas at the work site.
The employee completed two canopies with no issues. When starting his work on
the third canopy, he placed an A frame ladder on the canopy and leaned it on the
wall.  The employee climbed the ladder and started to descend the steps to get
on the canopy. During this process, the employee and ladder fell through the
canopy onto the balcony. The employee sustained injuries to his leg and back.
The employee was hospitalized to treat these injuries.
On March 12, 2022, an employee who worked in an unspecified capacity for a
agencies responded. The building was evacuated by the county fire department.
The building was cleared by a hazardous material agency after an interior entry
and inspection by the hazardous material team. It was determined that the grape
packing room was cooled by a mixture of propylene glycol and water. No abnormal
air readings were found at the time of the incident by the facility plant
manager or first responders. No evidence of a refrigeration leak was found in
the grape packing area or from other adjacent refrigerated areas of the facility
The building was found to be safe and returned back to control of the vineyard
at approximately 4:00 p.m. Packing operations resumed the next day without
incident. No chemical release was found. The workers had experienced chest pain,
headache, and nausea. They were all treated without hospitalization. This was a
joint employer site, but it was not a multiemployer site. This incident is also
recorded as investigation number 145410, which covers the vineyard. That
investigation lists six employees. The UPA is the same for both, 1829092.
At 11:50 a.m. on December 20, 2021, an employee was setting up the mold machine
to troubleshoot it.  The employee had turned on the heaters to the mold
injection gates.  The employee had checked the injection gates on the operator
side and found them to be operating properly. The employee went to check the
gate operation on the non-operator side.  The employee could not reach the
solenoid to activate the gates with his right arm/hand, so he reached across the
front of the mold with his left arm/hand. One of the injection gates on the
operator side shot some hot molten material on to the employee's left arm,
burning his upper arm.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 9:00 a.m. on November 1, 2021, an employee was troubleshooting a Lemo Model
Intermat 1100cc BM 15 machine, which required him to pull back on the gripper
belt to adjust the gripper carriage. A coworker started up the machine without
realizing the employee was pulling the gripper belt back, causing the employee
to get stuck in the machine. The employee amputated his ring and middle fingers
to the first knuckle and required hospitalization.
At 10:00 a.m. on December 14, 2021, an employee entered a catwalk to perform
maintenance on an air handler unit. As the employee cleaned up, the employee
fell approximately thirty-five feet over the catwalk guardrail and onto some
auditorium bleachers. The employee was hospitalized to treat lacerations,
fractures, and a concussion.
At 10:30 a.m. on October 18, 2021, an employee was cleaning out the lids under a
magnetic wheel on a bulk station at a metal manufacturing facility. When the
employee reached beneath the moving conveyor, his hand contacted the chain and
sprocket. The employee injured his left ring finger, resulting in amputation and
required medical treatment.
At 10:30 a.m. on November 13, 2021, an employee was resetting the belt on a
feeder.  The employee's finger was caught in an ingoing nip point of an
unguarded drive chain and sprocket, resulting in the amputation of his pinky
finger.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 12:00 p.m. on April 9, 2022, an employee was assisting a coworker as he
worked on a miter saw. The employee went to go grab another piece of molding,
when he tripped over a leg of the saw table and struck his head on the concrete
ground. The employee was killed.
The worksite is a warehouse food distribution center where employees perform
order selector activities by utilizing powered industrial trucks (PITs),
specifically an electric pallet jack rider. At 6:50 p.m. on February 27, 2022,
Employee #1, an order selector, was preparing to finish his work shift by
parking the PIT in the charging area where PIT's are stored. Employee #1 was
operating a Crown PE4500-80 electric pallet jack rider and was approaching the
charging area to park the PIT for end of shift. A contributing factor to the
accident involved Employee #1 trying to step off the PIT before it coasted to a
complete stop, resulting in a broken ankle. The employee was hospitalized.  No
accident-related citations to be issued, but other citations to follow.
At 8:30 a.m. on October 22, 2021, an employee was working as a lead maintenance
technician at an apartment complex. The employee was remodeling an apartment and
was using a Makita XSS02, battery-powered, circular saw to trim the side of a
wooden door without the use of a rip fence or straight edge to prevent the blade
from binding. As the employee was trimming the door, the blade bound and made
contact with his hand. The employee was hospitalized to treat suffered
lacerations to his left ring and pinky fingers with the pinky finger near a
complete amputation.
At 2:30 p.m. on October 27, 2021, an employee was loading roofing material rolls
onto a flat bed of a delivery truck. The employee was standing on the bed of the
deliver truck while his coworker was operating a Yale GLPP060 forklift. The
roofing material loaded onto the forks of the forklift, and the forklift driven
with the forks held in a upward position to secure the material.  Once the
forklift was parked next to the truck where the employee was standing, the
coworker operating the forklift lowered the forks downward onto the truck.  When
the employee observed that one of the roofing rolls was about to fall off the
bed of the truck, he reached to stop the roll at the same time his coworker
lowered the forks of the forklift.  The employee's thumb was injured when it was
working with a coworker who was also a logger while servicing the machine. The
employee was servicing the accumulator or piston without locking out the
seat the tire on a single piece truck wheel, the tire would not seat properly.
While the employee was using a small sledgehammer to bang on the wheel to seat
the tire properly around the wheel, the wheel suddenly was ejected from the tire
and struck the employee in the head. The employee was killed by blunt force
trauma injuries to the head.
At 12:00 noon on August 17, 2022, three employees were erecting and installing
blocks on 45-foot long roof trusses for a new amenity building when one of the
trusses was released too early by the crane operator before the employees were
able to block it out. While trying to hold and upright the roof truss, the truss
broke and the employees fell with the truss and another roof truss fell on top
of the employees when one of them attempted to hold himself up with the
installed truss. One employee landed face down on the concrete slab and the roof
truss that had fallen and was killed.
At 1:30 p.m. on August 11, 2022, an employee was installing new electrical
transformers at Memphis Light Gas and Water electric power distribution
facility. A coworker closed the circuit before the employee completed his work.
The employee was killed by electrocution.
At 02:45 p.m. on February 23, 2022, an employee was attempting to use a rag to
clean a clear plastic shield on a generator. The employee took it upon himself
to access the inside area of the plastic shield using an extension ladder
without supervision or supervisor direction. The inside of the shield was
positioned near the generator fan.  The employee climbed the ladder and reached
in near the top of the generator, approximately 9 to 10 feet high, and had the
rag in his hand.  The moving fan blades struck the employee's hand. The employee
was treated at the hospital for lacerations and fractures to the hand.
At 8:30 a.m. on July 13, 2022, an employee was assisting the owner with
repairs/maintenance of a skid loader. The lift arm fell onto the employee's
head. The employee was pronounced dead at the scene by emergency personnel. The
employee was struck by the lift arms and fork attachments of the skid loader.
At 1:30 p.m. on February 22, 2022, an employee assisted a coworker operating a
forklift to put the forks of the forklift under a load. As the coworker began to
lift the load of joists, the coworker believed that the load was slipping and
attempted to maneuver the load towards the mast.  The load struck the employee
as he attempted to jump off the truck bed. The employee was hospitalized to
treat fractures to the left hip and arm.
At 6:00 p.m. on August 17, 2022, an employee was a technician checking the pump
jack at an oil well to assess the cause of low oil production. The employee was
either caught in or between and then struck by the pump jack counterweights. The
employee was killed by upper torso crushing injuries.
At 10:11 a.m. on July 1, 2022, an employee was observed using the forklift to
lift a large wooden pallet into a roll-off dumpster. The forks were raised, the
forklift driven forward, and the fork angle lowered to get the pallet to slide
off the forks into the dumpster. After this did not work, the driver got out,
reached up, and attempted to push the pallet off the forks, which caused the
pallet to move a few inches but remain on the forks. Next the worker stepped up
onto the flat surface between the mast and the control panel and reached forward
from behind the mast in an attempt to knock the pallet forward off the forks. He
then returned to the forklift seat and elevated the forks and tilted the mast
forward and moved the forks up and down. The worker again stepped up behind the
mast and was using both hands to push the pallet forward, when one of his feet
inadvertently activated the middle lever which moved the boom backwards, pinning
his chest between the back of the boom and the front of the forklift roof. The
worker immediately used his foot to try and hit the lever in an attempt to move
the mast forward, however was only successful in dropping the forks. The worker
then began to lose consciousness and remained pinned for approximately 16
minutes before another worker noticed he was pinned and rushed to rescue him.
The employee was killed.
At 9:30 a.m. on August 18, 2022, an employee was standing behind his truck,
waiting to pick up outriggers when he was struck by a passing tractor trailer.
The employee died from his injuries.
At 5:15 p.m. on August 15, 2022, an employee was leaving the restroom at a
pastries and baked goods manufacturing facility. The employee smelled a strong
odor from a cleaning compound and fainted, causing him to fall and strike the
left side of his head against the floor threshold. The employee sustained a
concussion and was killed.
At 10:00 p.m. on July 30, 2022, an employee was working alone.  There were no
witnesses to exactly what the employee was doing right before he collapsed. The
employee clocked in for shift, but was later found unresponsive in the worksite
bathroom. He died due to pulmonary edema from fentanyl.
At 8:30 a.m. on February 22, 2022, an employee was offloading a trailer using an
electrical pallet jack. The employee collided with the inner wall of the
trailer. The employee suffered a torn foot/heel ligament. He had a surgery and
was hospitalized for about two days.
At 6:38 a.m. on August 22, 2022, an employee was vertically positioning
galvanized steel coil at a sheet metal work manufacturing facility. Three
unsecured 2,200 metal coils fell and struck the employee in the legs. The
employee sustained shearing injuries to the legs and was killed.
At 6:15 p.m. on August 19, 2022, two employees were digging a trench with a JCB
245XR Excavator for a storm sewer line that was located in the center of a new
multi-residential housing complex that was under construction. The trench was
approximately 29 feet long by 16 feet wide and 7 feet 6 inches deep. Both
employees entered into a manhole section of an existing sanitation sewer line
that was located approximately 6 feet from the trench. Both employees lost
consciousness in the manhole section. The EHS service that attempted to conduct
the rescue of the employees noted that the oxygen levels were at 12.1%. The
employer had completed this sanitation sewer line prior to working on the storm
sewer line. The employer did not have a means of testing the atmosphere in the
manhole section, and the employees were not trained on OSHA requirements for
working around and entry into confined spaces. Both employees died of
asphyxiation.
At 2:30 p.m. on August 18, 2022, an employee was using a boat hoist to setup
scientific equipment for erosion control. When the equipment did not settle
correctly on the river bottom, the employee entered the water to troubleshoot
the situation. The employee never resurfaced from the river and was killed by
drowning.
At 6:45 p.m. on August 22, 2022, an employee was attempting to seal a leaking
bag of plastic media at a plastics product manufacturing facility. The leaking
bag was underneath of a second 2,000 pound bag of plastic media, and the
shifting material caused the bag stacked on top to fall onto the employee. The
employee was crushed between the bag of plastic media and the cement floor and
was killed by asphyxiation.
At 3:30 p.m. on August 19, 2022, an employee was welding a steel template while
working on construction of a new power transmission line at a solar electric
generation facility.  While the employee was welding, the steel template fell
off the skid steer loader holding it and onto the employee. The employee was
killed when he was struck and crushed by the steel template.
At 10:30 a.m. on July 21, 2022, an employee was performing
agriculturally-related hand-labor operations in a blueberry field and was
waiting for his tote of picked berries to be weighed. An approximately 40 foot
tall dead tree, located within a nearby wooded area, fell, striking the
individual in the head while he was standing in the field. The individual's
death was ruled an accident due to multiple blunt force injuries.
At 1:30 a.m. on February 25, 2022, an employee was operating an ice bagging
machine. The employee stuck his hand under a belt guard to pull an item out of
the machine. The employee amputated the tip of a finger in the conveyor belt,
but there was no bone loss. The employee was hospitalized.
At 2:00 p.m. on August 11, 2022, an employee was inflating a tire at an oil well
drilling site when the tire experienced a sudden sidewall blowout.  The employee
was struck in the face and front of his body by the force of the blowout and
thrown into a metal Conex shipping container box. The employee was killed by
head and blunt force injuries sustained during the blowout.
At 1:55 p.m. on August 18, 2022, an employee was kneeling down and opening a
sprinkler valve box when he collapsed onto his left side. The employee was
killed by a heart attack.
At 3:00 p.m. on August 18, 2022, an employee entered an empty liquid propane gas
(LPG) tank for servicing at an industrial equipment wholesaler facility. Earlier
in the day, the employee approached a supervisor and stated that he wanted to
enter the tank to spray Torq CB III penetrating oil product on an internal valve
to loosen it overnight so it could be worked on the next day. The supervisor
told the employee to wait until the next morning when the tank could be vented.
The employee entered the tank by using a manlift connected to a forklift and a
ladder and was overcome by the vapor residue inside the tank. The employee was
not wearing a respirator but had a blower nearby which was unused. At
approximately 3:30 p.m., the supervisor began looking around the shop for the
the ice machine without de-energizing it since he could not locate the
electrical panel, so he attempted to disconnect the fixed wired 220 volt power
cord. The employee was killed when he received an electrical shock from the
power cord.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 14, 2022, an employee was removing and repairing a tire on
a woodchipper while working for a landscaping service. The woodchipper was
supported by a jack stand, and while the employee was laying underneath the
woodchipper, the woodchipper fell off the stand and pinned the employee to the
ground. The employee sustained injuries to the chest and body and was killed.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 24, 2022, an employee worked nailing roofing paper on a
roof. At some point, the employee fell approximately twenty-eight feet through a
skylight. The employee was hospitalized to treat head trauma, neurological
injuries, arm fracture and a facial laceration.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 18, 2022, an employee was using a trailer-type aerial lift
to trim a tree while working for a landscaping service. The employee was using
the aerial lift to trim a tree limb that was located over the porch roof of a
house. The employee used a ratchet strap to strap the tree limb to the aerial
lift platform before attempting to cut the tree limb. While the employee was
cutting the tree limb, the limb broke. The weight of the limb bent the aerial
lift platform 90 degrees, and the employee was not tied off to the lift. The
employee fell approximately 15 to 20 ft and was killed.
An employee an employee worked as an Eligibility Worker II for a County
Employment and Human Services Division since November of 2018. The employee
performed administrative duties such as reviewing applications and making
determinations as to which applicants meet the requirements for government
assistance programs. On January 7, 2022, the employee began to experience
COVID-19 related symptoms. That same day was his last day in the office.  At
5:00 p.m. on January 10, 2022, the employee went to the hospital for a doctor
appointment and was tested for COVID-19. That same day the employee received a
positive test result and phoned his immediate supervisor after 5:00 p.m. to
report the result.  Plus, the employee was admitted to the hosptial due to
shortness of breathe and respiratory concerns. The employee was fully vaccinated
when he tested positive for COVID-19. Several factors may have contributed to
the hospitalization including, but not limited to, that the employee had
recently been hospitalized for blood clots in his lungs as well as other on
going medical issues.    The date, time and other details leading up to exposure
are not indicated in the narrative. The employer did not have an effective
COVID-19 Prevention Program in place.
An employee was working as a deputy probation officer for a county probation
department and was regularly tested for COVID-19 when he tested positive on
December 29, 2021, but had no symptoms at that time. The employee developed
symptoms and subsequently died from his infection on January 4, 2022.
At 1:50 a.m. on July 16, 2022, an employee was closing an overhead door adjacent
to a welding station at a fabricated metal manufacturing facility. A portable
electric fan mounted on a pedestal was plugged into a wall receptacle at the
overhead door. Coworkers noticed several minutes later than the employee was
sitting on a crate at the overhead door and his left arm was in contact with the
portable fan. When a coworker attempted to close the overhead door and moved the
portable electric fan, he noticed an electric arc when contact between the fan
and the employee's arm was broken. A coworker initiated CPR and requested
medical assistance. The employee was transported to the local hospital where he
died from the electric shock injuries. It was determined that the portable cord
run through a wire way hole was exposed to a sharp edge which cut the wire
sheath and insultation and exposed the bare conductor. The attachment plug was
also missing the ground pin.
At 9:54 a.m. on June 13, 2022, an employee was holding onto a pressurized pipe
as a coworker was loosening the joint with a wrench. The pipe came loose and
swung around striking the employee on the left side of his head. The employee
incurred head injuries, including a concussion, and was killed.
At 12:00 p.m. on July 15, 2022, an employee was cleaning the bottom surface of a
pool while working for the City of Deming, MN. The employee was using weights to
help hold herself to the bottom of the pool. The employer trained the employees
to tie or strap weights to themselves as anchors while cleaning the bottom
surface of the pool. While using the equipment, the employee was killed by
